Tents or pole structures of any kind
Pets (service animals only)
Frisbees, sports balls, beach balls, etc
Weapons or anything that could resemble a weapon
Gang insignia, offensive signs/clothing, etc
Noise makers, fireworks, laser pointers, pocket knives, tools or any other potentially harmful items
All guests and their belongings will be subject to search prior to entering the festival site. Security and Festival Management reserves the right to refuse entry to persons and/or belongings at their discretion
Please see ONE Spokane Stadium policies & procedure
HERE.
Can I bring mosquito repellent, including bug spray or a thermacell?
Permitted
Personal insect repellent sprays (aerosol or pump spray) intended for individual use.
Insect repellent lotions, creams, wipes, sticks, and roll-ons.
Personal mosquito repellent bracelets, clips, patches, and wearable devices.
Mosquito head nets and bug jackets/shirts intended for personal use.
Small personal Thermacell® style devices (electric or butane-powered).
Butane-powered devices must use single personal-size cartridges only (approximately 12 g / 0.42 oz), such as the standard Thermacell refill cartridges.
Guests may bring a reasonable quantity of sealed replacement cartridges for personal use.
Battery-powered or rechargeable personal insect repellent devices.
Prohibited
Large or patio-style Thermacell® style devices (including lanterns, table-top units, and area repellents designed to protect multiple people).
Butane cylinders or fuel canisters larger than 12 g / 0.42 oz, including camping-style fuel canisters (e.g., 110 g, 220 g, 450 g, or similar).
Mosquito coils, Electric Mosquito Tennis Rackets, Citronella candles, tiki torches, or any open-flame mosquito repellent.
Propane-powered mosquito repellents or traps.
Mosquito foggers, misters, thermal foggers, or insecticide sprayers.
Any fuel-powered device not intended for individual personal use.
Any mosquito repellent device that produces a sustained open flame, excessive heat, smoke, or presents a fire hazard.
What kind of chair can I bring?
** Canada shows only **
Enjoy the live comedy from the comfort of your own camping chair!
Festival approved chairs must be single person, collapsible, not recline or have protruding leg rests or coverings. Chairs not adhering to festival guidelines will not be permitted through the gates. Blankets or tarps have a maximum size of 6′ x 6′.
VIP ticket holders will have standard plastic chairs at your table, however, feel free to bring your own for added comfort.
Chairs will only be available for rent to General Admission ticket holders if inventory is available.
I have a VIP Ticket - Do I need to bring a chair?
No, all VIP Table and VIP Club tickets have seating supplied for you!
Can I smoke anywhere?
No, smoking is only permitted in the designated areas. Please note, outside cannabis is not permitted, but is available for purchase on site in Edmonton and Calgary.
Can I leave and come back?
There is no re-entry – please ensure you have everything you need for the event before arriving!
I have a multi-show pass - Do I need to leave between the Afternoon and Evening Shows?
Yes – for security purposes, we do require all guests to leave the festival grounds between afternoon and evening events. We try to make this process as smooth as possible, and appreciate your cooperation to get you back to the laughs quickly!
TICKETING
I'm having problems with my ticketing order, help?
If you are having any technical difficulties on Tixr, please visit Tixr’s Help Centre for assistance. If you need further support, you can connect with Tixr’s Fan Support using the chat box on the bottom left, and a Tixr Customer Service Agent will be happy to help. For any Spokane related ticketing questions, please reach out to customercare@ticketswest.com.
Can I upgrade my tickets?
Absolutely! You can upgrade your tickets anytime, provided that inventory is available and you’re moving to the same Ticket Tier or a higher one. Simply log into your Tixr account to make the upgrade yourself! For detailed instructions, click
HERE
. For upgrading your purchase in Spokane, please reach out to customercare@ticketswest.com.
I purchased tickets but haven't received them yet!
To help combat scalping there is a ticket limit of 12 per order/email address & tickets will be emailed to purchasers 2 weeks prior to the event.
Are there any designated accessible seats/areas?

About Me
From The Comic's Comic
Hi! I’m Sean L. McCarthy.
My resume, in brief…Grew up in the newspaper age; got to cover the 1992 presidential election while interning at my hometown paper, The Hartford Courant ; moved West after college and learned how to work a beat at The Times-News in Twin Falls, Idaho; became a comedian in Seattle, then an entertainment reporter in the suburbs, and published my first newsroom blog in 1998 before “blog” was even in the dictionary, while competing in the Seattle International Comedy Competition (winning an innovation bonus from Scripps Howard). Became a columnist and reporter at The Arizona Republic in Phoenix, then The Boston Herald , then The Daily News in NYC.
Gawker and MediaBistro judged me New York’s Funniest Reporter in 2007, and I subsequently started my own site, The Comic’s Comic , first on TypePad, eventually moving it to WordPress. Since 2015, I’ve reviewed comedy specials and provided expert analysis for Decider , while also since 2018 freelancing for the Weekend Arts section of The New York Times , curating live event listings . My byline also appears in The Daily Beast now.

ABOUT DUBAI COMEDY FESTIVAL
Dubai Comedy Festival 2026 returns for its 7th edition from 9-18 October, 2026, bringing together world-class comedy in multiple languages for 10 days of non-stop laughs. From global stand-up icons to rising regional and local voices, the festival transforms the city into the region’s ultimate destination for laughter.
Taking over Dubai Opera, New Covent Garden Theatre, Pepperoni Comedy Club, and more, the 2026 edition of Dubai Comedy Festival will deliver an exciting mix of headliners, cult favourites, and breakthrough performers. Audiences can expect bold humour, diverse perspectives, and endless punchlines across the festival.
More than just a festival, Dubai Comedy Festival is a platform where cultures connect through comedy, the laughs don’t stop coming, and everyone is guaranteed a good time!
DIRECTIONS
Dubai Opera
How to get there
By car:
If you're coming from Sheikh Zayed Road (E11), take the exit towards Financial Center Road/D71 and follow the signs for Burj Khalifa/Downtown Dubai. Keep right and merge onto Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard. Continue straight until you reach Dubai Opera, which will be on your right.
By public transportation:
You can take the Dubai Metro Red Line and get off at the Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall Station. From there, you can either walk for about 10 minutes to Dubai Opera or take a short taxi ride to reach the venue.   ‍  ‍
By taxi:
You can also take a taxi to Dubai Opera from anywhere in Dubai. If you're coming from downtown, the journey typically takes around 15-20 minutes, depending on traffic conditions.
GET DIRECTIONS
New Covent Garden Theatre, Mall of the Emirates
How to get there
By car:
New Covent Garden Theatre is in Mall of the Emirates, Level 2 The closest parking is on Level 2, Orange Zone A5 & A6
By Dubai Metro:
Take the Red Line and get off at the R32 - Mall of the Emirates station
By taxi:
Ask for Mall of the Emirates, most drivers will know it well  Ask to be dropped off at the Taxi Drop-Off point (Entrance A) Use the lift or take the escalator up to Level 2
GET DIRECTIONS
Coca-Cola Arena
How to get there
By car:
Coca-Cola Arena is located in the City Walk area and it's easily accessible from Sheikh Zayed Road. From Sheikh Zayed Road, take Exit 47 towards Al Safa Street and follow the signs for City Walk.
By public transportation:
Coca-Cola Arena Dubai is easily accessible by metro, you can take the Red Line and get off at the Dubai Mall/Burj Khalifa Metro Station. From there, you can walk a few minutes to reach Coca-Cola Arena.

We’ve also got the return of Goblin Happy Hour, Cheers Queers Happy Hour, and our big and beautiful Closing Night Party. VENUES You’re deep in the heart of ATX now and you’ll be hopping around some of Austin’s most iconic downtown venues! Outside of the Paramount & State Theatres, you can take in comedy up-close and personal at Antone’s Nightclub, The Creek & The Cave, The Velveeta Room, Higbies, The Sunset Strip, Rozco’s Comedy Club, Vulcan Gas Company, Fallout Theater, and Cap City Comedy Club. WRISTBANDS Having trouble committing? Heard that one before. If a badge is more than you need, you can purchase a daily wristband and get access to our club shows and parties! Single tickets are also available to club shows, but do not guarantee entry. It’s possible that badges and wristbands will fill a venue, resulting in any single ticket holders receiving a refund. Moontower FAQs You got me. I have a badge. Now what? With two weeks of shows in the Paramount and State Theatres, and a 4-day comedy club binge from April 15-18, you have the ability to build your own fest experience. Headliners: Want to see a headliner at the Paramount or State Theatres? You’ll receive an email the day your badge holder presale starts with instructions and links to purchase tickets to all of the shows you want to see. Unsubscribed from our mailing list? Give us a call at (512) 474-1221 to get back on the list so you don’t miss a show! If presales are over closer to the fest, simply purchase single tickets to headliners of your choice through this site. Club Shows: To see shows during the 4-day comedy club binge, all you have to do is show up with your badge! No tickets or reservations necessary to catch the hottest acts in intimate club settings UNLESS you want to catch a show at Cap City Comedy Club.If you’re heading up to The Domain to see one of the shows hosted by our friends at Cap City Comedy Club Main Room or Cap City Comedy Club Red Room , Moontower badge holders can request complimentary, reserved tickets by calling the Cap City box office at 512-467-2333. Tickets should be requested at least 48 hours prior to the show. PLEASE NOTE: One Badge = One Ticket. When will I receive my badge(s)? If you’re heading to any headliner shows in Week 1 of the fest, all you’ll need is your ticket to the show. For Week 2’s comedy club binge, you’ll be able to pick up your badge starting on Wednesday, April 15th. Head up the 8th floor of the Hyatt Centric Hotel at 721 Congress Avenue—right next to the State Theatre—to get your badges (and snag some fest merch). You will need to bring your ID and/or receipt to pick up your badges. Badge pickup will be open at the following dates and times: Wed (4/15): 3-9pm Thu (4/16) – Sat (4/18): 3-10pm Can I buy single tickets to club shows? Yes, but they will not be guaranteed entry. All badge holders will receive priority access to all club shows. Single ticket holders will be seated 10 minutes prior to the start of the show in remaining available seats. If no seats are available, ticket purchasers will be refunded. Club tickets will go on sale in April before the fest. What about age restrictions? Can underage patrons get into shows? There is no age restriction on the festival as a whole and minors can purchase badges or single tickets to the Paramount shows. However, some of our Moontower venues are 18+ and, due to their liquor licensing/permit, are not able to let in underage patrons regardless of the event. All Ages The Paramount Theatre The State Theatre Fallout Theatre 18+ Antone’s Nightclub Cap City Comedy Club Higbie’s Sunset Strip Rozco’s Comedy Club The Velveeta Room Vulcan Gas Company 21+ The Creek and the Cave What time do doors open for performances? If you’re attending the first show of the night at the Paramount or State, doors will open one hour before showtime . We recommend getting there early and enjoying a drink. After that, typically doors will open 30 minutes prior to showtime . Other venues will open doors 30 minutes before showtime for all shows. These are rules of thumb only and actual times may vary by venue depending on size. Where should I park? We encourage rideshare when possible! If you’ve got a crew with you, our friends at Fetii group rideshare are offering festival goers a deal with code MOONTOWER that gets new Fetii users a free ride and existing Fetii users 25% off a ride. Tomorrow’s stars. The SXSW Comedy Festival has a long-standing history of bringing together the biggest names in comedy and the next generation of breakout talent. Open to all badge holders, it’s where fans, artists, and industry gather for unforgettable shows, discover new favorite comics, and experience a creative energy that’s pure SXSW. Audience at Cracked Comedy Club Official Showcase at SXSW 2026. Past Comedians Highlighting the industry’s brightest stars and showcasing up-and-coming acts since 2008. You might just catch your new fav before they go stratospheric. Standup showcases, taped specials, live podcasts, surprise cameos, improv, storytelling, and gameshows. Terms and Conditions box doesn’t enable Make sure you scroll all the way to the end of the Terms and Conditions. The checkbox will only enable once you’ve viewed the full text. If you’ve already done this and the box still isn’t enabling, try again using a different browser, an incognito/private window, or a different device. What’s the best way to get around Austin, and should I rent a car? + Rental cars can be convenient if you plan to travel outside the downtown area, but traffic congestion will be significant and parking can be difficult to find. Most of our hotels are just a quick trip to official SXSW venues and SXSW works with a variety of services to provide a comprehensive selection of transportation options. These options are available to help you design your commute to SXSW events within your individual budget and needs. Once you are downtown, most everything is within walking, pedicab or shuttle distance. Parking is at a premium in downtown Austin during SXSW. # Clashfinder Overview

## What It Is
Clashfinder provides "free, printable timetables for an event like a music festival or conference." The platform enables attendees to plan which acts to see and avoid scheduling conflicts.

## Creation and Maintenance
Clashfinders are "created by the community for the community." Users can search an existing database or create new timetables if one doesn't exist. While some are "made by event organisers," most appear to be community-driven. Collaborative editing is supported—clashfinders can have multiple administrators and allow edits by other users.

## Festival Coverage
The page doesn't specify total festival count but demonstrates broad coverage through prominent search links to major events including Glastonbury, Reading, Leeds, Coachella, and Bonnaroo. No comedy or fringe festivals are mentioned.

## Key Features
- **Personal highlighting**: Users can color-code preferred acts and save selections via account login
- **Data export**: Download in JSON, XML, or iCalendar formats; Excel downloads available with a free account
- **Spotify integration**: Build playlists from lineup acts
- **Mobile access**: Dedicated mobile interface with search functionality
- **Google Calendar import**: Sync schedules to calendar applications

  itinerary), the plan is delivered by **email-gated PDF** (name + address
  before the itinerary), the site still checks against **"3,649 shows"** — the
  stale 4 June launch snapshot, ~15% short of the delivered festival, the exact
  trap [market-and-audience/](../market-and-audience/README.md) documents — and
  it now pushes a companion app, **FringePal** ("bigger and better than this
  site"), not previously in this wiki. Its early-access pitch names **live
  "near me now"** as a coming feature — the first competitor seen announcing
  intent on the live-reachability axis.
- **[Fringe Finder](https://fringe-finder.netlify.app/)** — browse every 2026
  show, **track ticket availability**, and plan days with an **AI assistant** that
  builds a day-by-day plan from what is *still on sale*. Its own page (fetched
  2026-09-01) asserts "an official pilot with the Edinburgh Festival Fringe" —
  the claim is on the page, though still unconfirmed from the Fringe Society's
  side — counts "4,128 shows", says listings are "refreshed several times a
  day and may lag the box office", sends all ticket sales to edfringe.com, and
  pitches concierge-built days "that actually work — **walking times
  included**". Availability-aware planning is the piece most tools skip — and
  the one axis where we are behind rather than ahead; walking-time-aware
  itineraries bring it a step closer to the travel-model territory this wiki
  previously recorded as ours alone.

Dubai Comedy Festival
In 2020, Brag partnered with DTCM and Live Nation to bring back the Dubai Comedy Festival after a long hiatus. Since then, year after year, we have taken the festival to great heights, inviting some of the world’s funniest men and women to perform in prime venues across the city. With thousands of festival-goers attending every year, the Dubai Comedy Festival has become a milestone event in the city’s entertainment calendar.
Going from a 4-day event in 2020, the festival has grown to become a 10-day comedy extravaganza. In the past 4 years, comedy superstars such as Mo Amer, Michelle Wolf, Gad Elmaleh, Mo Gilligan, Katherine Ryan, Jim Jeffries, Jimmy Carr, Bassem Youssef and so many more have all graced the Dubai Comedy Festival stages. Additionally, we molded the festival to become a hub for a more global representation of comedy. With shows being performed in English, Arabic, Hindi, Tagalog, French, and Russian, we made sure the festival really reflects the multi-cultural nature of Dubai.
Running alongside the festival, we established Comedy Bizarre, a fringe comedy calendar that showcases up and coming comedians from the Emirates and around the world. This year also saw the addition of the Happy’nings calendar, where DCF helped shed light on all of the happiest events happening around Dubai, creating a concentrated dose of laughter and joy throughout the events 10-day run.
In our constant pursuit for laughs, we know that every edition of the Dubai Comedy Festival will always be even more hilarious than the last.

Twitter Facebook Pinterest LinkedIn Just for Laughs season is upon us once again, folks. The Montreal comedy institution celebrates yet another year of laughs, jokes, and a diverse array of comedic talent — some less concerned with political correctness than others — on display at the festival that has launched many a lucrative career in the comedy industry. Though this year’s edition is headlined by the likes of “Weird” Al Yankovic (read our interview with him here ), Nurse John, Atsuko Okatsuka and Gabriel Iglesias, among others, there’s plenty of shows worth catching that might not necessarily be on your radar. content.content: OFF JFL 2026 highlights Montreal Series As part of OFF JFL, aka Just for Laughs’ “unique edgy sibling”, comedy fans will get to see a bevy of local talent as part of the Montreal Series. One of the most iconic cities in North America for comedy is unsurprisingly a hotbed of talent in its own right, with shows hosted by Rachelle Elie, Mike Paterson and John Cotrocois respectively. An entirely queer-themed night will also be part of the programming, which takes place July 16 and is hosted by Tranna Wintour, featuring comics like Eve Parker Finley, Ray Resvick, Raquel Maestre and Tony McIntyre. The Comedy Nest (2313 Ste-Catherine W.), July 16–17, 7 p.m. or 9 p.m. (depending on individual show), $31.87 Maddy Kelly Having since relocated to New York City, the half-Indian, half-Irish Vancouver native Maddy Kelly has been making big moves since being named a New Face of Comedy at the 2023 edition of JFL. Kelly has gone from writing for This Hour Has 22 Minutes to making her comedy debut on Jimmy Fallon, receiving plaudits from outlets like The New York Times and The New Yorker for her cuttingly self-aware comedic style, whether discussing herself, her ethnic background, or the differences between Millennials and older generations. Café Cléopâtre (1230 St-Laurent) , July 23, 7 p.m., $26.74 Janine Harouni A London-based New Yorker who’s made a name for herself in Britain before reaching massive heights in the American comedy scene, Janine Harouni performs at Café Cléopâtre this year riding high on some major career Ws. With her own Amazon Prime special under her belt, as well as more than 250 million views online, Harouni hilariously riffs on subjects like marriage and mothering her young son while her punchlines go from charming to sharp in the blink of an eye. Café Cléopâtre (1230 St-Laurent) , July 23, 8:30 p.m., $26.74 Late Bad Hosted by Ben Sosa-Wright and Laura Cilevitz (with assistance from a sidekick named Monsieur Sex), Toronto’s Late Bad late-night comedy party “where anything can happen and almost always does” makes its debut in Montreal for OFF JFL over two nights this year. A comedy-meets-variety show full of improv, music, dancing, games, challenges and various surprise guests, both nights look to be especially raucous in a setting as intimate as Café Cléopâtre. Café Cléopâtre (1230 St-Laurent) , July 23–24, 11:30 p.m., $23.91 The Improvaneers This Cleveland seven-piece are first improv troupe ever to consist entirely of people with Down syndrome. The Improvaneers have become seasoned performers on the comedy circuit, giving audiences witty, energetic sets while also aiming to leave those audiences feeling happier, more inspired, and more inclined to challenge stereotypes and preconceptions than they were upon arrival. Théâtre Sainte-Catherine (264 Ste-Catherine E.) , July 25, 5 p.m., $24.57 Abby Wambaugh This Copenhagen-based American comic will be performing her debut show in Canada at this year’s OFF JFL. But instead of a typical standup routine, Abby Wambaugh will perform a wide range of styles across 17 of her best ideas for a debut show. Fittingly, this event is called The First 3 Minutes of 17 Shows, and sees Wambaugh exploring devastating subject matter in hilarious fashion during a one-person variety show. # The comedy-festival circuit

The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
genre. Compiled once, refined in place.

Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
[festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/](../festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/README.md)
owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
reachability. Planner-type competitors found along the way live on
[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

## Key insights

- PLACEHOLDER

## The census: a year of comedy festivals

The seed source is the festival tracker kept by From The Comic's Comic
([fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/),
fetched 2026-09-01), which lists the circuit by month for 2026 with a stated
confirmation policy — "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet." The full
2026 list, with run lengths computed from its dates:

<CENSUS_TABLE>

Not in the table: three undated entries — the **San Francisco Comedy
Competition** ("across the Bay Area") and **Seattle International Comedy
Competition** ("all month across Western Washington", November), both
month-long *touring competitions* rather than city takeovers, and **Just For
Laughs Singapore** (tbd) — plus the first 2027 confirmations (JFL Bermuda,
17–20 Feb 2027; SXSW, 17–20 Mar 2027). The tracker's own dates are treated
here as launch-time claims, not delivered totals.

What the census says before any per-festival research:

- **The circuit is mostly weekend showcases.** 45 of 85 dated festivals run ≤4
  days, and 56 of 85 are in the US — overwhelmingly club-scale, curated or
  submission-based weekends where a visitor picks a headliner, not a schedule.
- **The fringe-length tier is small and un-American.** Only 13 festivals run
  ≥14 days, and the US contributes just two (SF Sketchfest and the new Fallout
  Fringe in Las Vegas); the rest are UK, Irish, Australian and NZ events —
  Edinburgh, Adelaide, Brighton, Melbourne, Sydney, NZICF, Leicester,
  Aberdeen, plus the Dublin entry examined below.
- **Run length is a strong first classifier.** A festival long enough to need
  repeat performances of the same show is where a scheduling product has work
  to do; a weekend of one-night showcases is not. The dossiers below test that
  presumption festival by festival.

## The two shapes, and what decides planner-worthiness

PLACEHOLDER-SHAPES

## The planner-relevant tier: dossiers

PLACEHOLDER-DOSSIERS

## Annual fixtures vs one-offs and rovers

PLACEHOLDER-ANNUAL

## Concurrent-festival clusters

PLACEHOLDER-CONCURRENT

## Ticketing and data across the circuit

PLACEHOLDER-TICKETING

## Festival trackers

Sources that track the circuit itself — what a future multi-festival product
would use to keep a festival calendar current:

- **[From The Comic's Comic — Comedy Festivals](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/)**
  — the seed list above: one page, by month, one line and one link per
  festival, with a stated only-if-confirmed policy. Hand-maintained on
  WordPress.com; not machine-readable beyond the HTML. Two link defects found
  on the 2026-09-01 fetch are worth knowing when reusing it: its Melbourne
  International Comedy Festival link points at the festival's stale `/2024`
  page, and its "Dublin Comedy Festival" entry links to
  `dublinwestcomedyfest.ie` — a different, smaller festival than the label
  suggests (untangled in the dossiers below).

PLACEHOLDER-TRACKERS

## Sources

- [Comedy Festivals (From The Comic's Comic)](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/) — the 2026 census table above: every festival, date and official-site link, fetched 2026-09-01.

## Open questions

- PLACEHOLDER-OPEN

## Growth log

- **2026-09-01** — page created deliberately on the owner's direction, from the
  From The Comic's Comic festival tracker: the 85-festival 2026 census with
  computed run lengths, the fringe-shaped ↔ showcase-shaped taxonomy, dossiers
  for the planner-relevant tier (organizer, recurrence, scale, show model,
  venues, ticketing, data reachability, concurrent festivals), the annual/
  one-off map, and the festival-tracker list. All claims cited; per-festival
  deep dives deliberately deferred to adoption time.

The New Zealand International Comedy Festival ( NZICF ; sometimes the NZ Intl Comedy Fest ) is a comedy festival in both Auckland and Wellington , New Zealand. The festival is run by the New Zealand Comedy Trust, and is held across three weeks during April and May. [ 1 ] From its beginnings in 1993 as a 2-day event, the festival has developed into a major nationwide event, with a total attendance of over 100,000 people each year. Main events [ edit ] Each year the Festival features over 200 shows and involves around 250 performers. The Festival contains a wide range of comedy performances – from emerging artists through to NZ comedy industry veterans and stars of the international comedy circuit. Similarly, the Festival caters for a wide range of audiences with specific shows aimed at children and teenagers, and a diverse offering of comedy fare. The opening of the Festival is the televised Comedy Gala, a showcase of performances by the top local and international comedians appearing in the festival. # The comedy-festival circuit

The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
genre. Compiled once, refined in place.

Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
[festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/](../festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/README.md)
owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
reachability. Planner-type competitors found along the way live on
[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

## Key insights

- PLACEHOLDER

Competition** ("all month across Western Washington", November), both
month-long *touring competitions* rather than city takeovers, and **Just For
Laughs Singapore** (tbd) — plus the first 2027 confirmations (JFL Bermuda,
17–20 Feb 2027; SXSW, 17–20 Mar 2027). The tracker's own dates are treated
here as launch-time claims, not delivered totals.

What the census says before any per-festival research:

- **The circuit is mostly weekend showcases.** 45 of 85 dated festivals run ≤4
  days, and 56 of 85 are in the US — overwhelmingly club-scale, curated or
  submission-based weekends where a visitor picks a headliner, not a schedule.
- **The fringe-length tier is small and un-American.** Only 13 festivals run
  ≥14 days, and the US contributes just two (SF Sketchfest and the new Fallout
  Fringe in Las Vegas); the rest are UK, Irish, Australian and NZ events —
  Edinburgh, Adelaide, Brighton, Melbourne, Sydney, NZICF, Leicester,
  Aberdeen, plus the Dublin entry examined below.
- **Run length is a strong first classifier.** A festival long enough to need
  repeat performances of the same show is where a scheduling product has work
  to do; a weekend of one-night showcases is not. The dossiers below test that
  presumption festival by festival.

# product-wiki

Agent-maintained market, user, and competitor research for EdFringeNow, kept as
self-growing wikis under this directory (compile findings once, refine in place,
cite everything). This tree is **walled off from the app code** — nothing in the
repo may reference `product-wiki/` except the reviewed distillation under
`product-requirements/`, so no code silently depends on unreviewed research.

## What lives here

- **`product-requirements/`** — the human-reviewed distillation of the wikis into
  product requirements. The only `product-wiki/` content the rest of the repo may
  reference. Never auto-grown.
- **`sample-data/`** — small illustrative assets a wiki claim points to (created
  when first needed; never test fixtures).
- **Everything else** — wiki space. A wiki is a folder with a `README.md`
  carrying `## Sources`, `## Open questions`, and `## Growth log`. The weekly
  growth pass researches each wiki's own open questions and writes back cited.

## Wikis

- **[competitor-landscape/](competitor-landscape/README.md)** — the existing
  Fringe discovery/planning tools, split by which of the product's two questions
  they answer, and where each gap is.
- **[market-and-audience/](market-and-audience/README.md)** — festival scale, the
  overwhelm problem, and the two audiences the product targets: the live
  in-festival crowd and the trip planners.
- **[audience-divergence/](audience-divergence/README.md)** — where those two
  crowds' requirements pull apart, where they actively conflict, and the narrow
  spine they share.
- **[festival-season/](festival-season/README.md)** — the other Edinburgh
  festivals in August and across the summer: their scale, diversity, locations,
  the six different shapes an "event" takes across them, and whether the data is
  reachable.
- **[fringe-ticketing/](fringe-ticketing/README.md)** — who actually sells a
  Fringe ticket (the Society, the venues, edfest.com), the definitive operator
  census, why no third party can sell or earn commission on tickets, and why
  the edfringe scrape has no full replacement.
- **[festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/](festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/README.md)** —
  the same question pointed outward: which *other cities* carry the
  Edinburgh-in-August pattern, ranked by how close they are structurally rather
  than by fame, plus the candidate tail.

Based on the search results, here's the information about Del Close Marathon 2026 (DCM '26):

## Event Dates and Duration

The Upright Citizens Brigade's Del Close Marathon (DCM) returns to New York June 12–14 with 56 nonstop hours of comedy across six stages scattered throughout the city. The 56-hour Marathon runs from Friday June 12 at 4:00pm through Sunday June 14 at midnight at UCBNY's MainStage on 14th Street.

## Venues

The 2026 festival spans six stages across two walkable venues: UCBNY (Stages 1-2, the Marathon HQ) and Theater for the New City on 1st Avenue (Stages 3-6, used primarily for headliner showcases).

## Festival Highlights

The annual improv blowout gathers hundreds of teams from around the country, alongside headliners like this year's Edi Patterson, Chris Flemming, Please Don't Destroy, Patti Harrison, Rory Scovel, Paul Scheer and more, for marathon improv sets, sketch shows, workshops, podcasts and the kind of sleep-deprived comedy chaos that becomes improv lore.

This edition also expands beyond pure improv for the first time, welcoming stand-up, podcasts, sketch comedy, and alternative programming alongside the traditional improv lineup.

## Pre-Festival Events

A week of pre-festival headliner shows runs June 8-11 ahead of the 56-hour main marathon.

## Badge and Pass Information

All badge holders have access to Marathon programming for the full festival. If you purchase a 3-Day Badge or Festival Single Day Pass, individual headliner tickets are available now!

**History and Origins:**

The first Lucille Ball Festival of New Comedy took place in late May 1991 with comedians performing at several venues throughout the city, including the Cherry Lounge, the Marvin House, the former Holiday Inn on Fourth Street, among others. The festival was established to fulfill Ball's vision of transforming her hometown of Jamestown, New York, into a premier destination for comedy enthusiasts.

**Annual Tradition:**

Since the festival started in 1991, Lucy Comedy Fest has featured performances by Lewis Black, Ray Romano, Ellen DeGeneres, Paula Poundstone, Joan Rivers, Bob Newhart, George Wallace, Billy Gardell, and many more. In 1991, the National Comedy Center established the annual Lucille Ball Comedy Festival, which is now held every August to honor Ball's August 6 birthday.

**Current Status:**

Today, the festival attracts over 10,000 visitors annually. Held annually in August over four to five days, it draws crowds to the city's venues for a concentrated program of laughter and learning.

Skankfest is an annual stand-up comedy festival founded in 2016 by comedian Luis J. Gomez, producer Rebecca Trent, and the comics behind the Legion of Skanks podcast. Skankfest started in 2016 as a two-night DIY collaboration between Luis J. Gomez and Rebecca Trent, held at Trent's Long Island City venue, The Creek and the Cave.

content.text:
All research complete. Here is the report.

---

# Research report: comedy-festival trackers & festival planners beyond Edinburgh

Evidence labels: **[fetched]** = page retrieved via curl/WebFetch in this session and read directly; **[snippet]** = WebSearch result snippet, attributed to its publisher, not independently opened.

## Headline findings

1. **No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists anywhere.** The best global list is one journalist's hand-maintained newsletter page (~90 festivals for 2026, free-text dates, no feed). Wikipedia has no "List of comedy festivals" article at all (the URL 404s). Chortle has no festivals index (its /festivals URL 404s). A festival calendar for a "plan any festival" product would have to be assembled and maintained by us.
2. **The third-party festival-planner category is empty outside Edinburgh — verified festival by festival.** Nothing third-party found for MICF, Adelaide Fringe, Brighton Fringe, JFL Montreal, Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, no planner at all), SF Sketchfest, or SXSW's official programme. Searches for Adelaide/Brighton planners return *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe as the top hits — the category exists only there.
3. **Where planning tooling exists elsewhere, it is official or outsourced SaaS**: Sched (SF Sketchfest), Eventbase (SXSW GO), DabApps-built official app (Brighton), Katalyst-built official app + on-site MyFringe planner (Adelaide).
4. **In music festivals the planner category is crowded**: Clashfinder (crowdsourced grids, JSON/XML/iCal export — the closest structural cousin to us, and it already hosts a few small UK comedy/fringe events) plus a dozen consumer set-time apps and organizer-side platforms (Woov). The demand shape we serve is proven at scale in music, unserved in comedy.

---

## Part A — comedy-festival trackers & directories

### 1. From The Comic's Comic — fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (seed)
- **Who runs it**: Sean L. McCarthy, career comedy journalist (Boston Herald, NY Daily News; reviews for Decider since 2015; freelance NYT Weekend Arts live-listings curation; Daily Beast) — confirmed from his About page **[fetched]** https://fromthecomicscomic.com/about-me/
- **What it is**: a single WordPress.com-hosted page on his newsletter site (509 subscribers per the subscribe widget), listing festivals by month. **[fetched]**
- **Coverage**: ~90 festivals for 2026, mostly US plus the majors abroad (SF Sketchfest, Leicester, Adelaide Fringe, JFL Vancouver/Belgium/Montreal/Quebec/Toronto/Paris/Sydney/Singapore/Bermuda, MICF, Sydney, Brighton Fringe, NZICF, Netflix Is A Joke, Edinburgh, Dubai, Tokyo, Galway, NY Comedy Festival…), plus two 2027 entries. **[fetched]**
- **Currency**: current — full 2026 calendar with a stated inclusion rule: "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet". His archive shows he actively reviews Edinburgh each August (54 posts in Aug 2026). **[fetched]**
- **How maintained**: by hand, with email submissions — the older list at thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (now frozen at 2023, with a banner redirecting to the newsletter page) invites festivals to email thecomicscomic@gmail.com to be listed. **[fetched]** https://thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/
- **Machine-readability**: none — plain HTML, one outbound link per festival, dates as free text under month headings. Scrapeable but unstructured; a name/date parse would be needed and the format is one person's prose.

### 2. Chortle — chortle.co.uk
- **Who runs it**: Chortle, "The UK Comedy Guide" — the UK comedy trade site. **[fetched]** https://www.chortle.co.uk/
- **Festival calendar**: none. https://www.chortle.co.uk/festivals returns 404 (generic site frame). **[fetched]**
- **What it does have**: (a) the **Comedy Diary** (https://www.chortle.co.uk/comedy-diary) — a gig-level live-comedy listings engine for UK/Ireland, filterable by region and date, where "Edinburgh Fringe" is one region among England/Scotland/Wales/…; listings are venue/promoter-submitted via an "Add a listing" form **[fetched]**; (b) per-festival show databases at /shows/, e.g. /shows/edinburgh_fringe_2026/ with per-show pages **[fetched, homepage links]**; (c) heavy editorial Fringe coverage (awards, reviews).
- **Machine-readability**: none exposed; HTML listings only.
- **Read for us**: Chortle is a listings+editorial destination, not a festival tracker — useful as a per-show data source for UK festivals, not for keeping a festival calendar current.

### 3. British Comedy Guide — comedy.co.uk
- **Access**: Cloudflare-blocked to both curl and WebFetch (403 "Just a moment…") **[fetched block page]** — everything below is **[snippet]**.
- **Directory**: BCG maintains a UK comedy festivals directory at https://www.comedy.co.uk/live/festivals/ ("UK comedy festivals — British Comedy Guide"), with per-festival pages (e.g. /live/festivals/write-on-comedy/), plus dedicated Edinburgh Fringe listings coverage at /fringe/ "since 2010". **[snippet]**
- **Who runs it**: BCG, launched 2003, ~500k uniques/month per Wikipedia's article on it. **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Comedy_Guide
- **Coverage/currency**: UK-only by design; per-festival detail level unverifiable from here (blocked).
- **Machine-readability**: none known; the block itself is a signal that scraping it would be contested.

### 4. Wikipedia
- **No list article exists**: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals is a 404. **[fetched]**
- **What exists**: Category:Comedy_festivals — 5 subcategories (by continent: 4, by country: 12, plus burlesque/improv) and only 2 direct pages **[fetched]**; and the "Comedy festival" article whose "Notable examples" section lists just ~19 festivals, unsourced-tagged since August 2010, alphabetical, no dates, with obvious gaps (no Netflix Is A Joke, no NY Comedy Festival, no Moontower). **[fetched]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_festival
- **Verdict**: usable as a seed of notable names via the category tree (individual articles carry dates of varying staleness); useless as a calendar.

### 5. World Fringe — worldfringe.com
- **Who runs it**: World Fringe, the fringe-festival network association (membership org — "Support World Fringe" membership page, World Fringe Congress, World Fringe Day). **[fetched]** https://worldfringe.com/
- **Directory offering**: "Fringe A-Z" member listings at https://worldfringe.com/members/ — searchable by ~32 countries (Austria…Taiwan) — plus a "Fringe Calendar" page (https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/, "Annual list of Fringe Festivals"), a Touring Directory, and Fringe Maps. **[fetched]**
- **Machine-readability: effectively none.** The member directory is rendered client-side by the Ultimate Member WordPress plugin over admin-ajax (the static HTML contains only the country filter and `{{filter.name}}` templates); the calendar page's static HTML contains no festival entries either — both are JS-loaded, so per-festival data (dates, links) is invisible to plain fetches and would need session/nonce-aware scraping. **[fetched, verified against raw HTML]**
- **Verdict**: authoritative for *which fringes exist* worldwide, weak as a data source; fringe-network only (no non-fringe comedy festivals).

### 6. Others checked
- **FilmFreeway** (filmfreeway.com): 12,000+ festivals/contests listed platform-wide **[snippet]**; comedy entries are overwhelmingly comedy *film* festivals and screenplay contests seeking submissions (LA Comedy Festival, All Comedy Short Film Festival…), though some live fests use it for performer submissions. Direct fetch is proxy-blocked here. A third-party Apify "FilmFreeway Festival Scraper" exists, confirming it is scrapeable in principle. **[snippet]** https://apify.com/hypebridge/filmfreeway-festival-scraper — submission-side directory, wrong lens for a visitor-facing calendar.
- **Everfest** (everfest.com): defunct — Wikipedia lists it defunct (2020); reporting says services shut down effective June 1, 2024. Domain rejected by our proxy (denial vs unreachable indistinguishable from here). **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest
- **FestivalNet** (festivalnet.com): 26,000+ US/Canada events but craft shows/art fairs/music, vendor-oriented; no comedy presence in its own homepage copy. **[fetched]**
- **MusicFestivalWizard** /comedy-festivals/ URL exists but is Cloudflare-blocked to bots; the site self-describes as a music-festival database — no documented comedy section found. **[fetched block page + snippet]**
- **Punchup.live**: "the platform that empowers comedians to connect directly with their fans" (its own meta description) — comedian profile/ticketing, not a festival tracker; zero festival mentions in its static page. **[fetched]**

---

## Part B — festival planners beyond Edinburgh

### B1. Per-festival third-party planners (the core question)

| Festival | Third-party planner found? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Melbourne Intl Comedy Festival (750+ shows) | **None found** | Search "MICF planner app third party schedule tool" returns only official program guide + city guides **[snippet]** |
| Adelaide Fringe | **None found** | Search returns the official app + on-site planner; the only third-party hits are *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Brighton Fringe | **None found** | Search returns official DabApps-built app; third-party hits again Edinburgh's Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Just For Laughs Montreal (~250 ticketed shows, ~25 venues) | **None found** | No attendee planner surfaced; official site schedule only **[snippet]** |
| SXSW | **None for the official programme**; a third-party ecosystem exists for *unofficial parties* | Official schedule.sxsw.com + SXSW GO; Do512's SX hub (2025.do512.com) and RSVPATX.com aggregate unofficial-party RSVPs; attendees resort to Google Docs for cross-source planning **[snippet]** |
| Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, 500+ performers, 35 LA venues, May 4–10 2026) | **None found — no official app either** | Schedule lives on NetflixIsAJokeFest.com; scale per Hollywood Reporter/Netflix Tudum **[snippet]** — the most Fringe-scale unserved festival found |
| SF Sketchfest | **None third-party; planning outsourced to Sched** | sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — generic event-SaaS with personal schedules + calendar sync **[snippet]** |

**Structural conclusion**: outside Edinburgh, no comedy festival has grown a third-party planner ecosystem. Multi-hundred-show festivals (MICF 750+, NIAJ 475+, Adelaide Fringe thousands) run on official sites/apps or rented SaaS. A well-executed generic planner would be first-in-category everywhere except Edinburgh.

### B2. Official apps as planners (one line each)
- **Adelaide Fringe**: official app (Apple id6499414523 / Google au.com.adelaidefringe, built with Katalyst Interactive) plus an on-site "My plan" planner (adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/plan) — wishlist, sort by time/day. **[snippet]**
- **Brighton Fringe**: official app built by agency DabApps — programme browsing, accounts, ticket purchase via festival APIs. **[snippet]** https://www.dabapps.com/work/clients/brighton-fringe-app/
- **SXSW**: SXSW GO official app, built on Eventbase (package com.xomodigital.sxswgo) — schedule building + networking; noted limitation: no custom events, no unofficial parties. **[snippet]** https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go
- **MICF**: no current official app found — the only trace is a 2010-era iPhone app (iTWire); no present-day store listing surfaced. **[snippet]**
- **SF Sketchfest**: no own app; Sched instance is the planner. **[snippet]**

### B3. Music-festival planner category (the structural analogue)
- **Clashfinder** (clashfinder.com) — the closest generic "schedule clash" tool. Free printable lineup grids "created by the community for the community" (some by organisers); collaborative editing with multiple admins; personal act highlighting with accounts; **data export in JSON, XML, iCalendar** (Excel with free account); Spotify playlist integration; Google Calendar sync; donation/premium model; active since ~2011 (Twitter join date). **[WebFetch of homepage + snippet]** Site is captcha-walled to plain curl. **Comedy/fringe coverage exists but is tiny and UK-local**: Exeter Comedy Festival 2025 & 2026 (real comedian grids — Wozniak, Duker, Watson…), Cambridge Fringe 2025, Tramlines Fringe 2022–26 **[snippet, clashfinder.com/s/… URLs]**; **no Edinburgh Fringe clashfinder surfaced** — plausibly because a 3,000-show open-access festival exceeds a hand-edited grid. Who runs it was not discoverable (no about/founder info in searches) — an anonymous/small UK operation.
- **Woov** (woov.com) — Amsterdam startup; official-partner festival companion platform (personal schedule, set-start notifications, map, find-your-friends); 600+ partner festivals in 41 countries / "1000+ events" claim; B2B revenue via organiser partnerships; €2M raised from Jägermeister's owners + MediaMonks founders. **[snippet]** — organizer-side, not a third-party planner.
- **Consumer set-time apps (crowded field, all music)**: Festival Dust (all US music-festival set times/lineups/maps in one app, group scheduling — "EDC, Ultra, Electric Forest", own site fetched) **[fetched]** https://www.festivaldust.com/; Headliners, Frontstage (100+ festivals), FestiPlannr, FestivPlanner, Festiveo, Festiverse, Lineup Finder — all discovered in two searches; Patchboard even runs a directory *of* festival apps. **[snippet]**
- **"Festival Scout"**: nothing found under that name (searches: `"Festival Scout" app music festival planner lineup`) — the results return the apps above instead. **Not a real product as far as we can tell.**
- **"Lineupning"**: nothing found (search: `Lineupning festival lineup tracking app`) — likewise resolves to the general category. **Not found.**
- **Songkick**: music-festival directory (songkick.com/festivals) + artist-tracking notifications, 15M users claim — and a public **Concerts and Festivals API** (songkick.com/developer), i.e. the machine-readable festival dataset that comedy lacks. **[snippet]** Rate Your Music: no festival-planner tooling surfaced.
- **Novelty tier**: Instafest (Spotify-history fantasy lineups), LineupSupply (poster photo → playlist). **[snippet]**

### B4. Generic trip/event planners
- Nothing genuinely relevant found. TripIt is generic email-forwarding travel itineraries with no festival features surfaced; Fever/DICE did not surface as festival planners (search: `"festival trip planner" app … "TripIt" OR "Fever" OR "DICE"`). **[snippet]** The only real "plan the festival trip" adjacents found are SXSW's party aggregators (Do512, RSVPATX), above.

# Research report: comedy-festival trackers & festival planners beyond Edinburgh

Evidence labels: **[fetched]** = page retrieved via curl/WebFetch in this session and read directly; **[snippet]** = WebSearch result snippet, attributed to its publisher, not independently opened.

## Headline findings

1. **No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists anywhere.** The best global list is one journalist's hand-maintained newsletter page (~90 festivals for 2026, free-text dates, no feed). Wikipedia has no "List of comedy festivals" article at all (the URL 404s). Chortle has no festivals index (its /festivals URL 404s). A festival calendar for a "plan any festival" product would have to be assembled and maintained by us.
2. **The third-party festival-planner category is empty outside Edinburgh — verified festival by festival.** Nothing third-party found for MICF, Adelaide Fringe, Brighton Fringe, JFL Montreal, Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, no planner at all), SF Sketchfest, or SXSW's official programme. Searches for Adelaide/Brighton planners return *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe as the top hits — the category exists only there.
3. **Where planning tooling exists elsewhere, it is official or outsourced SaaS**: Sched (SF Sketchfest), Eventbase (SXSW GO), DabApps-built official app (Brighton), Katalyst-built official app + on-site MyFringe planner (Adelaide).
4. **In music festivals the planner category is crowded**: Clashfinder (crowdsourced grids, JSON/XML/iCal export — the closest structural cousin to us, and it already hosts a few small UK comedy/fringe events) plus a dozen consumer set-time apps and organizer-side platforms (Woov). The demand shape we serve is proven at scale in music, unserved in comedy.

---

## Part A — comedy-festival trackers & directories

### 1. From The Comic's Comic — fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (seed)
- **Who runs it**: Sean L. McCarthy, career comedy journalist (Boston Herald, NY Daily News; reviews for Decider since 2015; freelance NYT Weekend Arts live-listings curation; Daily Beast) — confirmed from his About page **[fetched]** https://fromthecomicscomic.com/about-me/
- **What it is**: a single WordPress.com-hosted page on his newsletter site (509 subscribers per the subscribe widget), listing festivals by month. **[fetched]**
- **Coverage**: ~90 festivals for 2026, mostly US plus the majors abroad (SF Sketchfest, Leicester, Adelaide Fringe, JFL Vancouver/Belgium/Montreal/Quebec/Toronto/Paris/Sydney/Singapore/Bermuda, MICF, Sydney, Brighton Fringe, NZICF, Netflix Is A Joke, Edinburgh, Dubai, Tokyo, Galway, NY Comedy Festival…), plus two 2027 entries. **[fetched]**
- **Currency**: current — full 2026 calendar with a stated inclusion rule: "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet". His archive shows he actively reviews Edinburgh each August (54 posts in Aug 2026). **[fetched]**
- **How maintained**: by hand, with email submissions — the older list at thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (now frozen at 2023, with a banner redirecting to the newsletter page) invites festivals to email thecomicscomic@gmail.com to be listed. **[fetched]** https://thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/
- **Machine-readability**: none — plain HTML, one outbound link per festival, dates as free text under month headings. Scrapeable but unstructured; a name/date parse would be needed and the format is one person's prose.

### 2. Chortle — chortle.co.uk
- **Who runs it**: Chortle, "The UK Comedy Guide" — the UK comedy trade site. **[fetched]** https://www.chortle.co.uk/
- **Festival calendar**: none. https://www.chortle.co.uk/festivals returns 404 (generic site frame). **[fetched]**
- **What it does have**: (a) the **Comedy Diary** (https://www.chortle.co.uk/comedy-diary) — a gig-level live-comedy listings engine for UK/Ireland, filterable by region and date, where "Edinburgh Fringe" is one region among England/Scotland/Wales/…; listings are venue/promoter-submitted via an "Add a listing" form **[fetched]**; (b) per-festival show databases at /shows/, e.g. /shows/edinburgh_fringe_2026/ with per-show pages **[fetched, homepage links]**; (c) heavy editorial Fringe coverage (awards, reviews).
- **Machine-readability**: none exposed; HTML listings only.
- **Read for us**: Chortle is a listings+editorial destination, not a festival tracker — useful as a per-show data source for UK festivals, not for keeping a festival calendar current.

### 3. British Comedy Guide — comedy.co.uk
- **Access**: Cloudflare-blocked to both curl and WebFetch (403 "Just a moment…") **[fetched block page]** — everything below is **[snippet]**.
- **Directory**: BCG maintains a UK comedy festivals directory at https://www.comedy.co.uk/live/festivals/ ("UK comedy festivals — British Comedy Guide"), with per-festival pages (e.g. /live/festivals/write-on-comedy/), plus dedicated Edinburgh Fringe listings coverage at /fringe/ "since 2010". **[snippet]**
- **Who runs it**: BCG, launched 2003, ~500k uniques/month per Wikipedia's article on it. **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Comedy_Guide
- **Coverage/currency**: UK-only by design; per-festival detail level unverifiable from here (blocked).
- **Machine-readability**: none known; the block itself is a signal that scraping it would be contested.

### 4. Wikipedia
- **No list article exists**: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals is a 404. **[fetched]**
- **What exists**: Category:Comedy_festivals — 5 subcategories (by continent: 4, by country: 12, plus burlesque/improv) and only 2 direct pages **[fetched]**; and the "Comedy festival" article whose "Notable examples" section lists just ~19 festivals, unsourced-tagged since August 2010, alphabetical, no dates, with obvious gaps (no Netflix Is A Joke, no NY Comedy Festival, no Moontower). **[fetched]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_festival
- **Verdict**: usable as a seed of notable names via the category tree (individual articles carry dates of varying staleness); useless as a calendar.

### 5. World Fringe — worldfringe.com
- **Who runs it**: World Fringe, the fringe-festival network association (membership org — "Support World Fringe" membership page, World Fringe Congress, World Fringe Day). **[fetched]** https://worldfringe.com/
- **Directory offering**: "Fringe A-Z" member listings at https://worldfringe.com/members/ — searchable by ~32 countries (Austria…Taiwan) — plus a "Fringe Calendar" page (https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/, "Annual list of Fringe Festivals"), a Touring Directory, and Fringe Maps. **[fetched]**
- **Machine-readability: effectively none.** The member directory is rendered client-side by the Ultimate Member WordPress plugin over admin-ajax (the static HTML contains only the country filter and `{{filter.name}}` templates); the calendar page's static HTML contains no festival entries either — both are JS-loaded, so per-festival data (dates, links) is invisible to plain fetches and would need session/nonce-aware scraping. **[fetched, verified against raw HTML]**
- **Verdict**: authoritative for *which fringes exist* worldwide, weak as a data source; fringe-network only (no non-fringe comedy festivals).

### 6. Others checked
- **FilmFreeway** (filmfreeway.com): 12,000+ festivals/contests listed platform-wide **[snippet]**; comedy entries are overwhelmingly comedy *film* festivals and screenplay contests seeking submissions (LA Comedy Festival, All Comedy Short Film Festival…), though some live fests use it for performer submissions. Direct fetch is proxy-blocked here. A third-party Apify "FilmFreeway Festival Scraper" exists, confirming it is scrapeable in principle. **[snippet]** https://apify.com/hypebridge/filmfreeway-festival-scraper — submission-side directory, wrong lens for a visitor-facing calendar.
- **Everfest** (everfest.com): defunct — Wikipedia lists it defunct (2020); reporting says services shut down effective June 1, 2024. Domain rejected by our proxy (denial vs unreachable indistinguishable from here). **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest
- **FestivalNet** (festivalnet.com): 26,000+ US/Canada events but craft shows/art fairs/music, vendor-oriented; no comedy presence in its own homepage copy. **[fetched]**
- **MusicFestivalWizard** /comedy-festivals/ URL exists but is Cloudflare-blocked to bots; the site self-describes as a music-festival database — no documented comedy section found. **[fetched block page + snippet]**
- **Punchup.live**: "the platform that empowers comedians to connect directly with their fans" (its own meta description) — comedian profile/ticketing, not a festival tracker; zero festival mentions in its static page. **[fetched]**

---

## Part B — festival planners beyond Edinburgh

### B1. Per-festival third-party planners (the core question)

| Festival | Third-party planner found? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Melbourne Intl Comedy Festival (750+ shows) | **None found** | Search "MICF planner app third party schedule tool" returns only official program guide + city guides **[snippet]** |
| Adelaide Fringe | **None found** | Search returns the official app + on-site planner; the only third-party hits are *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Brighton Fringe | **None found** | Search returns official DabApps-built app; third-party hits again Edinburgh's Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Just For Laughs Montreal (~250 ticketed shows, ~25 venues) | **None found** | No attendee planner surfaced; official site schedule only **[snippet]** |
| SXSW | **None for the official programme**; a third-party ecosystem exists for *unofficial parties* | Official schedule.sxsw.com + SXSW GO; Do512's SX hub (2025.do512.com) and RSVPATX.com aggregate unofficial-party RSVPs; attendees resort to Google Docs for cross-source planning **[snippet]** |
| Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, 500+ performers, 35 LA venues, May 4–10 2026) | **None found — no official app either** | Schedule lives on NetflixIsAJokeFest.com; scale per Hollywood Reporter/Netflix Tudum **[snippet]** — the most Fringe-scale unserved festival found |
| SF Sketchfest | **None third-party; planning outsourced to Sched** | sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — generic event-SaaS with personal schedules + calendar sync **[snippet]** |

**Structural conclusion**: outside Edinburgh, no comedy festival has grown a third-party planner ecosystem. Multi-hundred-show festivals (MICF 750+, NIAJ 475+, Adelaide Fringe thousands) run on official sites/apps or rented SaaS. A well-executed generic planner would be first-in-category everywhere except Edinburgh.

### B2. Official apps as planners (one line each)
- **Adelaide Fringe**: official app (Apple id6499414523 / Google au.com.adelaidefringe, built with Katalyst Interactive) plus an on-site "My plan" planner (adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/plan) — wishlist, sort by time/day. **[snippet]**
- **Brighton Fringe**: official app built by agency DabApps — programme browsing, accounts, ticket purchase via festival APIs. **[snippet]** https://www.dabapps.com/work/clients/brighton-fringe-app/
- **SXSW**: SXSW GO official app, built on Eventbase (package com.xomodigital.sxswgo) — schedule building + networking; noted limitation: no custom events, no unofficial parties. **[snippet]** https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go
- **MICF**: no current official app found — the only trace is a 2010-era iPhone app (iTWire); no present-day store listing surfaced. **[snippet]**
- **SF Sketchfest**: no own app; Sched instance is the planner. **[snippet]**

### B3. Music-festival planner category (the structural analogue)
- **Clashfinder** (clashfinder.com) — the closest generic "schedule clash" tool. Free printable lineup grids "created by the community for the community" (some by organisers); collaborative editing with multiple admins; personal act highlighting with accounts; **data export in JSON, XML, iCalendar** (Excel with free account); Spotify playlist integration; Google Calendar sync; donation/premium model; active since ~2011 (Twitter join date). **[WebFetch of homepage + snippet]** Site is captcha-walled to plain curl. **Comedy/fringe coverage exists but is tiny and UK-local**: Exeter Comedy Festival 2025 & 2026 (real comedian grids — Wozniak, Duker, Watson…), Cambridge Fringe 2025, Tramlines Fringe 2022–26 **[snippet, clashfinder.com/s/… URLs]**; **no Edinburgh Fringe clashfinder surfaced** — plausibly because a 3,000-show open-access festival exceeds a hand-edited grid. Who runs it was not discoverable (no about/founder info in searches) — an anonymous/small UK operation.
- **Woov** (woov.com) — Amsterdam startup; official-partner festival companion platform (personal schedule, set-start notifications, map, find-your-friends); 600+ partner festivals in 41 countries / "1000+ events" claim; B2B revenue via organiser partnerships; €2M raised from Jägermeister's owners + MediaMonks founders. **[snippet]** — organizer-side, not a third-party planner.
- **Consumer set-time apps (crowded field, all music)**: Festival Dust (all US music-festival set times/lineups/maps in one app, group scheduling — "EDC, Ultra, Electric Forest", own site fetched) **[fetched]** https://www.festivaldust.com/; Headliners, Frontstage (100+ festivals), FestiPlannr, FestivPlanner, Festiveo, Festiverse, Lineup Finder — all discovered in two searches; Patchboard even runs a directory *of* festival apps. **[snippet]**
- **"Festival Scout"**: nothing found under that name (searches: `"Festival Scout" app music festival planner lineup`) — the results return the apps above instead. **Not a real product as far as we can tell.**
- **"Lineupning"**: nothing found (search: `Lineupning festival lineup tracking app`) — likewise resolves to the general category. **Not found.**
- **Songkick**: music-festival directory (songkick.com/festivals) + artist-tracking notifications, 15M users claim — and a public **Concerts and Festivals API** (songkick.com/developer), i.e. the machine-readable festival dataset that comedy lacks. **[snippet]** Rate Your Music: no festival-planner tooling surfaced.
- **Novelty tier**: Instafest (Spotify-history fantasy lineups), LineupSupply (poster photo → playlist). **[snippet]**

### B4. Generic trip/event planners
- Nothing genuinely relevant found. TripIt is generic email-forwarding travel itineraries with no festival features surfaced; Fever/DICE did not surface as festival planners (search: `"festival trip planner" app … "TripIt" OR "Fever" OR "DICE"`). **[snippet]** The only real "plan the festival trip" adjacents found are SXSW's party aggregators (Do512, RSVPATX), above.

- **What it does have**: (a) the **Comedy Diary** (https://www.chortle.co.uk/comedy-diary) — a gig-level live-comedy listings engine for UK/Ireland, filterable by region and date, where "Edinburgh Fringe" is one region among England/Scotland/Wales/…; listings are venue/promoter-submitted via an "Add a listing" form **[fetched]**; (b) per-festival show databases at /shows/, e.g. /shows/edinburgh_fringe_2026/ with per-show pages **[fetched, homepage links]**; (c) heavy editorial Fringe coverage (awards, reviews).
- **Machine-readability**: none exposed; HTML listings only.
- **Read for us**: Chortle is a listings+editorial destination, not a festival tracker — useful as a per-show data source for UK festivals, not for keeping a festival calendar current.

### 3. British Comedy Guide — comedy.co.uk
- **Access**: Cloudflare-blocked to both curl and WebFetch (403 "Just a moment…") **[fetched block page]** — everything below is **[snippet]**.
- **Directory**: BCG maintains a UK comedy festivals directory at https://www.comedy.co.uk/live/festivals/ ("UK comedy festivals — British Comedy Guide"), with per-festival pages (e.g. /live/festivals/write-on-comedy/), plus dedicated Edinburgh Fringe listings coverage at /fringe/ "since 2010". **[snippet]**
- **Who runs it**: BCG, launched 2003, ~500k uniques/month per Wikipedia's article on it. **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Comedy_Guide
- **Coverage/currency**: UK-only by design; per-festival detail level unverifiable from here (blocked).
- **Machine-readability**: none known; the block itself is a signal that scraping it would be contested.

### 4. Wikipedia
- **No list article exists**: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals is a 404. **[fetched]**
- **What exists**: Category:Comedy_festivals — 5 subcategories (by continent: 4, by country: 12, plus burlesque/improv) and only 2 direct pages **[fetched]**; and the "Comedy festival" article whose "Notable examples" section lists just ~19 festivals, unsourced-tagged since August 2010, alphabetical, no dates, with obvious gaps (no Netflix Is A Joke, no NY Comedy Festival, no Moontower). **[fetched]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_festival
- **Verdict**: usable as a seed of notable names via the category tree (individual articles carry dates of varying staleness); useless as a calendar.

### 5. World Fringe — worldfringe.com
- **Who runs it**: World Fringe, the fringe-festival network association (membership org — "Support World Fringe" membership page, World Fringe Congress, World Fringe Day). **[fetched]** https://worldfringe.com/
- **Directory offering**: "Fringe A-Z" member listings at https://worldfringe.com/members/ — searchable by ~32 countries (Austria…Taiwan) — plus a "Fringe Calendar" page (https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/, "Annual list of Fringe Festivals"), a Touring Directory, and Fringe Maps. **[fetched]**
- **Machine-readability: effectively none.** The member directory is rendered client-side by the Ultimate Member WordPress plugin over admin-ajax (the static HTML contains only the country filter and `{{filter.name}}` templates); the calendar page's static HTML contains no festival entries either — both are JS-loaded, so per-festival data (dates, links) is invisible to plain fetches and would need session/nonce-aware scraping. **[fetched, verified against raw HTML]**
- **Verdict**: authoritative for *which fringes exist* worldwide, weak as a data source; fringe-network only (no non-fringe comedy festivals).

### 6. Others checked
- **FilmFreeway** (filmfreeway.com): 12,000+ festivals/contests listed platform-wide **[snippet]**; comedy entries are overwhelmingly comedy *film* festivals and screenplay contests seeking submissions (LA Comedy Festival, All Comedy Short Film Festival…), though some live fests use it for performer submissions. Direct fetch is proxy-blocked here. A third-party Apify "FilmFreeway Festival Scraper" exists, confirming it is scrapeable in principle. **[snippet]** https://apify.com/hypebridge/filmfreeway-festival-scraper — submission-side directory, wrong lens for a visitor-facing calendar.
- **Everfest** (everfest.com): defunct — Wikipedia lists it defunct (2020); reporting says services shut down effective June 1, 2024. Domain rejected by our proxy (denial vs unreachable indistinguishable from here). **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest
- **FestivalNet** (festivalnet.com): 26,000+ US/Canada events but craft shows/art fairs/music, vendor-oriented; no comedy presence in its own homepage copy. **[fetched]**
- **MusicFestivalWizard** /comedy-festivals/ URL exists but is Cloudflare-blocked to bots; the site self-describes as a music-festival database — no documented comedy section found. **[fetched block page + snippet]**
- **Punchup.live**: "the platform that empowers comedians to connect directly with their fans" (its own meta description) — comedian profile/ticketing, not a festival tracker; zero festival mentions in its static page. **[fetched]**

---

## Part B — festival planners beyond Edinburgh

### B1. Per-festival third-party planners (the core question)

| Festival | Third-party planner found? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Melbourne Intl Comedy Festival (750+ shows) | **None found** | Search "MICF planner app third party schedule tool" returns only official program guide + city guides **[snippet]** |
| Adelaide Fringe | **None found** | Search returns the official app + on-site planner; the only third-party hits are *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Brighton Fringe | **None found** | Search returns official DabApps-built app; third-party hits again Edinburgh's Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Just For Laughs Montreal (~250 ticketed shows, ~25 venues) | **None found** | No attendee planner surfaced; official site schedule only **[snippet]** |
| SXSW | **None for the official programme**; a third-party ecosystem exists for *unofficial parties* | Official schedule.sxsw.com + SXSW GO; Do512's SX hub (2025.do512.com) and RSVPATX.com aggregate unofficial-party RSVPs; attendees resort to Google Docs for cross-source planning **[snippet]** |
| Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, 500+ performers, 35 LA venues, May 4–10 2026) | **None found — no official app either** | Schedule lives on NetflixIsAJokeFest.com; scale per Hollywood Reporter/Netflix Tudum **[snippet]** — the most Fringe-scale unserved festival found |
| SF Sketchfest | **None third-party; planning outsourced to Sched** | sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — generic event-SaaS with personal schedules + calendar sync **[snippet]** |

**Structural conclusion**: outside Edinburgh, no comedy festival has grown a third-party planner ecosystem. Multi-hundred-show festivals (MICF 750+, NIAJ 475+, Adelaide Fringe thousands) run on official sites/apps or rented SaaS. A well-executed generic planner would be first-in-category everywhere except Edinburgh.

### B2. Official apps as planners (one line each)
- **Adelaide Fringe**: official app (Apple id6499414523 / Google au.com.adelaidefringe, built with Katalyst Interactive) plus an on-site "My plan" planner (adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/plan) — wishlist, sort by time/day. **[snippet]**
- **Brighton Fringe**: official app built by agency DabApps — programme browsing, accounts, ticket purchase via festival APIs. **[snippet]** https://www.dabapps.com/work/clients/brighton-fringe-app/
- **SXSW**: SXSW GO official app, built on Eventbase (package com.xomodigital.sxswgo) — schedule building + networking; noted limitation: no custom events, no unofficial parties. **[snippet]** https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go
- **MICF**: no current official app found — the only trace is a 2010-era iPhone app (iTWire); no present-day store listing surfaced. **[snippet]**
- **SF Sketchfest**: no own app; Sched instance is the planner. **[snippet]**

### B3. Music-festival planner category (the structural analogue)
- **Clashfinder** (clashfinder.com) — the closest generic "schedule clash" tool. Free printable lineup grids "created by the community for the community" (some by organisers); collaborative editing with multiple admins; personal act highlighting with accounts; **data export in JSON, XML, iCalendar** (Excel with free account); Spotify playlist integration; Google Calendar sync; donation/premium model; active since ~2011 (Twitter join date). **[WebFetch of homepage + snippet]** Site is captcha-walled to plain curl. **Comedy/fringe coverage exists but is tiny and UK-local**: Exeter Comedy Festival 2025 & 2026 (real comedian grids — Wozniak, Duker, Watson…), Cambridge Fringe 2025, Tramlines Fringe 2022–26 **[snippet, clashfinder.com/s/… URLs]**; **no Edinburgh Fringe clashfinder surfaced** — plausibly because a 3,000-show open-access festival exceeds a hand-edited grid. Who runs it was not discoverable (no about/founder info in searches) — an anonymous/small UK operation.
- **Woov** (woov.com) — Amsterdam startup; official-partner festival companion platform (personal schedule, set-start notifications, map, find-your-friends); 600+ partner festivals in 41 countries / "1000+ events" claim; B2B revenue via organiser partnerships; €2M raised from Jägermeister's owners + MediaMonks founders. **[snippet]** — organizer-side, not a third-party planner.
- **Consumer set-time apps (crowded field, all music)**: Festival Dust (all US music-festival set times/lineups/maps in one app, group scheduling — "EDC, Ultra, Electric Forest", own site fetched) **[fetched]** https://www.festivaldust.com/; Headliners, Frontstage (100+ festivals), FestiPlannr, FestivPlanner, Festiveo, Festiverse, Lineup Finder — all discovered in two searches; Patchboard even runs a directory *of* festival apps. **[snippet]**
- **"Festival Scout"**: nothing found under that name (searches: `"Festival Scout" app music festival planner lineup`) — the results return the apps above instead. **Not a real product as far as we can tell.**
- **"Lineupning"**: nothing found (search: `Lineupning festival lineup tracking app`) — likewise resolves to the general category. **Not found.**
- **Songkick**: music-festival directory (songkick.com/festivals) + artist-tracking notifications, 15M users claim — and a public **Concerts and Festivals API** (songkick.com/developer), i.e. the machine-readable festival dataset that comedy lacks. **[snippet]** Rate Your Music: no festival-planner tooling surfaced.
- **Novelty tier**: Instafest (Spotify-history fantasy lineups), LineupSupply (poster photo → playlist). **[snippet]**

### B4. Generic trip/event planners
- Nothing genuinely relevant found. TripIt is generic email-forwarding travel itineraries with no festival features surfaced; Fever/DICE did not surface as festival planners (search: `"festival trip planner" app … "TripIt" OR "Fever" OR "DICE"`). **[snippet]** The only real "plan the festival trip" adjacents found are SXSW's party aggregators (Do512, RSVPATX), above.
