# Research report: comedy-festival trackers & festival planners beyond Edinburgh

Evidence labels: **[fetched]** = page retrieved via curl/WebFetch in this session and read directly; **[snippet]** = WebSearch result snippet, attributed to its publisher, not independently opened.

## Headline findings

1. **No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists anywhere.** The best global list is one journalist's hand-maintained newsletter page (~90 festivals for 2026, free-text dates, no feed). Wikipedia has no "List of comedy festivals" article at all (the URL 404s). Chortle has no festivals index (its /festivals URL 404s). A festival calendar for a "plan any festival" product would have to be assembled and maintained by us.
2. **The third-party festival-planner category is empty outside Edinburgh — verified festival by festival.** Nothing third-party found for MICF, Adelaide Fringe, Brighton Fringe, JFL Montreal, Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, no planner at all), SF Sketchfest, or SXSW's official programme. Searches for Adelaide/Brighton planners return *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe as the top hits — the category exists only there.
3. **Where planning tooling exists elsewhere, it is official or outsourced SaaS**: Sched (SF Sketchfest), Eventbase (SXSW GO), DabApps-built official app (Brighton), Katalyst-built official app + on-site MyFringe planner (Adelaide).
4. **In music festivals the planner category is crowded**: Clashfinder (crowdsourced grids, JSON/XML/iCal export — the closest structural cousin to us, and it already hosts a few small UK comedy/fringe events) plus a dozen consumer set-time apps and organizer-side platforms (Woov). The demand shape we serve is proven at scale in music, unserved in comedy.

---

## Part A — comedy-festival trackers & directories

### 1. From The Comic's Comic — fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (seed)
- **Who runs it**: Sean L. McCarthy, career comedy journalist (Boston Herald, NY Daily News; reviews for Decider since 2015; freelance NYT Weekend Arts live-listings curation; Daily Beast) — confirmed from his About page **[fetched]** https://fromthecomicscomic.com/about-me/
- **What it is**: a single WordPress.com-hosted page on his newsletter site (509 subscribers per the subscribe widget), listing festivals by month. **[fetched]**
- **Coverage**: ~90 festivals for 2026, mostly US plus the majors abroad (SF Sketchfest, Leicester, Adelaide Fringe, JFL Vancouver/Belgium/Montreal/Quebec/Toronto/Paris/Sydney/Singapore/Bermuda, MICF, Sydney, Brighton Fringe, NZICF, Netflix Is A Joke, Edinburgh, Dubai, Tokyo, Galway, NY Comedy Festival…), plus two 2027 entries. **[fetched]**
- **Currency**: current — full 2026 calendar with a stated inclusion rule: "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet". His archive shows he actively reviews Edinburgh each August (54 posts in Aug 2026). **[fetched]**
- **How maintained**: by hand, with email submissions — the older list at thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/ (now frozen at 2023, with a banner redirecting to the newsletter page) invites festivals to email thecomicscomic@gmail.com to be listed. **[fetched]** https://thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/
- **Machine-readability**: none — plain HTML, one outbound link per festival, dates as free text under month headings. Scrapeable but unstructured; a name/date parse would be needed and the format is one person's prose.

### 2. Chortle — chortle.co.uk
- **Who runs it**: Chortle, "The UK Comedy Guide" — the UK comedy trade site. **[fetched]** https://www.chortle.co.uk/
- **Festival calendar**: none. https://www.chortle.co.uk/festivals returns 404 (generic site frame). **[fetched]**
- **What it does have**: (a) the **Comedy Diary** (https://www.chortle.co.uk/comedy-diary) — a gig-level live-comedy listings engine for UK/Ireland, filterable by region and date, where "Edinburgh Fringe" is one region among England/Scotland/Wales/…; listings are venue/promoter-submitted via an "Add a listing" form **[fetched]**; (b) per-festival show databases at /shows/, e.g. /shows/edinburgh_fringe_2026/ with per-show pages **[fetched, homepage links]**; (c) heavy editorial Fringe coverage (awards, reviews).
- **Machine-readability**: none exposed; HTML listings only.
- **Read for us**: Chortle is a listings+editorial destination, not a festival tracker — useful as a per-show data source for UK festivals, not for keeping a festival calendar current.

### 3. British Comedy Guide — comedy.co.uk
- **Access**: Cloudflare-blocked to both curl and WebFetch (403 "Just a moment…") **[fetched block page]** — everything below is **[snippet]**.
- **Directory**: BCG maintains a UK comedy festivals directory at https://www.comedy.co.uk/live/festivals/ ("UK comedy festivals — British Comedy Guide"), with per-festival pages (e.g. /live/festivals/write-on-comedy/), plus dedicated Edinburgh Fringe listings coverage at /fringe/ "since 2010". **[snippet]**
- **Who runs it**: BCG, launched 2003, ~500k uniques/month per Wikipedia's article on it. **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Comedy_Guide
- **Coverage/currency**: UK-only by design; per-festival detail level unverifiable from here (blocked).
- **Machine-readability**: none known; the block itself is a signal that scraping it would be contested.

### 4. Wikipedia
- **No list article exists**: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals is a 404. **[fetched]**
- **What exists**: Category:Comedy_festivals — 5 subcategories (by continent: 4, by country: 12, plus burlesque/improv) and only 2 direct pages **[fetched]**; and the "Comedy festival" article whose "Notable examples" section lists just ~19 festivals, unsourced-tagged since August 2010, alphabetical, no dates, with obvious gaps (no Netflix Is A Joke, no NY Comedy Festival, no Moontower). **[fetched]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_festival
- **Verdict**: usable as a seed of notable names via the category tree (individual articles carry dates of varying staleness); useless as a calendar.

### 5. World Fringe — worldfringe.com
- **Who runs it**: World Fringe, the fringe-festival network association (membership org — "Support World Fringe" membership page, World Fringe Congress, World Fringe Day). **[fetched]** https://worldfringe.com/
- **Directory offering**: "Fringe A-Z" member listings at https://worldfringe.com/members/ — searchable by ~32 countries (Austria…Taiwan) — plus a "Fringe Calendar" page (https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/, "Annual list of Fringe Festivals"), a Touring Directory, and Fringe Maps. **[fetched]**
- **Machine-readability: effectively none.** The member directory is rendered client-side by the Ultimate Member WordPress plugin over admin-ajax (the static HTML contains only the country filter and `{{filter.name}}` templates); the calendar page's static HTML contains no festival entries either — both are JS-loaded, so per-festival data (dates, links) is invisible to plain fetches and would need session/nonce-aware scraping. **[fetched, verified against raw HTML]**
- **Verdict**: authoritative for *which fringes exist* worldwide, weak as a data source; fringe-network only (no non-fringe comedy festivals).

### 6. Others checked
- **FilmFreeway** (filmfreeway.com): 12,000+ festivals/contests listed platform-wide **[snippet]**; comedy entries are overwhelmingly comedy *film* festivals and screenplay contests seeking submissions (LA Comedy Festival, All Comedy Short Film Festival…), though some live fests use it for performer submissions. Direct fetch is proxy-blocked here. A third-party Apify "FilmFreeway Festival Scraper" exists, confirming it is scrapeable in principle. **[snippet]** https://apify.com/hypebridge/filmfreeway-festival-scraper — submission-side directory, wrong lens for a visitor-facing calendar.
- **Everfest** (everfest.com): defunct — Wikipedia lists it defunct (2020); reporting says services shut down effective June 1, 2024. Domain rejected by our proxy (denial vs unreachable indistinguishable from here). **[snippet]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest
- **FestivalNet** (festivalnet.com): 26,000+ US/Canada events but craft shows/art fairs/music, vendor-oriented; no comedy presence in its own homepage copy. **[fetched]**
- **MusicFestivalWizard** /comedy-festivals/ URL exists but is Cloudflare-blocked to bots; the site self-describes as a music-festival database — no documented comedy section found. **[fetched block page + snippet]**
- **Punchup.live**: "the platform that empowers comedians to connect directly with their fans" (its own meta description) — comedian profile/ticketing, not a festival tracker; zero festival mentions in its static page. **[fetched]**

---

## Part B — festival planners beyond Edinburgh

### B1. Per-festival third-party planners (the core question)

| Festival | Third-party planner found? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Melbourne Intl Comedy Festival (750+ shows) | **None found** | Search "MICF planner app third party schedule tool" returns only official program guide + city guides **[snippet]** |
| Adelaide Fringe | **None found** | Search returns the official app + on-site planner; the only third-party hits are *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Brighton Fringe | **None found** | Search returns official DabApps-built app; third-party hits again Edinburgh's Plan My Fringe **[snippet]** |
| Just For Laughs Montreal (~250 ticketed shows, ~25 venues) | **None found** | No attendee planner surfaced; official site schedule only **[snippet]** |
| SXSW | **None for the official programme**; a third-party ecosystem exists for *unofficial parties* | Official schedule.sxsw.com + SXSW GO; Do512's SX hub (2025.do512.com) and RSVPATX.com aggregate unofficial-party RSVPs; attendees resort to Google Docs for cross-source planning **[snippet]** |
| Netflix Is A Joke (475+ shows, 500+ performers, 35 LA venues, May 4–10 2026) | **None found — no official app either** | Schedule lives on NetflixIsAJokeFest.com; scale per Hollywood Reporter/Netflix Tudum **[snippet]** — the most Fringe-scale unserved festival found |
| SF Sketchfest | **None third-party; planning outsourced to Sched** | sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — generic event-SaaS with personal schedules + calendar sync **[snippet]** |

**Structural conclusion**: outside Edinburgh, no comedy festival has grown a third-party planner ecosystem. Multi-hundred-show festivals (MICF 750+, NIAJ 475+, Adelaide Fringe thousands) run on official sites/apps or rented SaaS. A well-executed generic planner would be first-in-category everywhere except Edinburgh.

### B2. Official apps as planners (one line each)
- **Adelaide Fringe**: official app (Apple id6499414523 / Google au.com.adelaidefringe, built with Katalyst Interactive) plus an on-site "My plan" planner (adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/plan) — wishlist, sort by time/day. **[snippet]**
- **Brighton Fringe**: official app built by agency DabApps — programme browsing, accounts, ticket purchase via festival APIs. **[snippet]** https://www.dabapps.com/work/clients/brighton-fringe-app/
- **SXSW**: SXSW GO official app, built on Eventbase (package com.xomodigital.sxswgo) — schedule building + networking; noted limitation: no custom events, no unofficial parties. **[snippet]** https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go
- **MICF**: no current official app found — the only trace is a 2010-era iPhone app (iTWire); no present-day store listing surfaced. **[snippet]**
- **SF Sketchfest**: no own app; Sched instance is the planner. **[snippet]**

### B3. Music-festival planner category (the structural analogue)
- **Clashfinder** (clashfinder.com) — the closest generic "schedule clash" tool. Free printable lineup grids "created by the community for the community" (some by organisers); collaborative editing with multiple admins; personal act highlighting with accounts; **data export in JSON, XML, iCalendar** (Excel with free account); Spotify playlist integration; Google Calendar sync; donation/premium model; active since ~2011 (Twitter join date). **[WebFetch of homepage + snippet]** Site is captcha-walled to plain curl. **Comedy/fringe coverage exists but is tiny and UK-local**: Exeter Comedy Festival 2025 & 2026 (real comedian grids — Wozniak, Duker, Watson…), Cambridge Fringe 2025, Tramlines Fringe 2022–26 **[snippet, clashfinder.com/s/… URLs]**; **no Edinburgh Fringe clashfinder surfaced** — plausibly because a 3,000-show open-access festival exceeds a hand-edited grid. Who runs it was not discoverable (no about/founder info in searches) — an anonymous/small UK operation.
- **Woov** (woov.com) — Amsterdam startup; official-partner festival companion platform (personal schedule, set-start notifications, map, find-your-friends); 600+ partner festivals in 41 countries / "1000+ events" claim; B2B revenue via organiser partnerships; €2M raised from Jägermeister's owners + MediaMonks founders. **[snippet]** — organizer-side, not a third-party planner.
- **Consumer set-time apps (crowded field, all music)**: Festival Dust (all US music-festival set times/lineups/maps in one app, group scheduling — "EDC, Ultra, Electric Forest", own site fetched) **[fetched]** https://www.festivaldust.com/; Headliners, Frontstage (100+ festivals), FestiPlannr, FestivPlanner, Festiveo, Festiverse, Lineup Finder — all discovered in two searches; Patchboard even runs a directory *of* festival apps. **[snippet]**
- **"Festival Scout"**: nothing found under that name (searches: `"Festival Scout" app music festival planner lineup`) — the results return the apps above instead. **Not a real product as far as we can tell.**
- **"Lineupning"**: nothing found (search: `Lineupning festival lineup tracking app`) — likewise resolves to the general category. **Not found.**
- **Songkick**: music-festival directory (songkick.com/festivals) + artist-tracking notifications, 15M users claim — and a public **Concerts and Festivals API** (songkick.com/developer), i.e. the machine-readable festival dataset that comedy lacks. **[snippet]** Rate Your Music: no festival-planner tooling surfaced.
- **Novelty tier**: Instafest (Spotify-history fantasy lineups), LineupSupply (poster photo → playlist). **[snippet]**

### B4. Generic trip/event planners
- Nothing genuinely relevant found. TripIt is generic email-forwarding travel itineraries with no festival features surfaced; Fever/DICE did not surface as festival planners (search: `"festival trip planner" app … "TripIt" OR "Fever" OR "DICE"`). **[snippet]** The only real "plan the festival trip" adjacents found are SXSW's party aggregators (Do512, RSVPATX), above.

## Festival Dates & Location

The Roundhouse Comedy Festival runs from August 1st to 18th, 2026 at the landmark circular building in Camden.

## Main Line-up

The lineup includes headliners such as Joe Lycett, Katherine Ryan, Sam Campbell, Ed Gamble, Sara Pascoe, and Vittorio Angelone, along with solo shows from Bob's Burgers star Kristen Schaal and Big Boys creator Jack Rooke, plus live podcasts with Adam Buxton and Alexei Sayle.

The festival opens on August 1st with a night headlined by Frank Skinner, alongside Phil Wang, Rosie Jones, Celya AB and Saturday Night Live UK's Paddy Young.

## Additional Programming

The festival features emerging talent such as stars of Saturday Night Live UK Ayoade Bamgboye and Paddy Young, and last year's Edinburgh Comedy Award winner Sam Nicoresti. The Roundhouse and Berk's Nest offer 30 £5 tickets for every show to audiences aged 30 and under.

---

# Comedy festival research: Canada (non-JFL) + rest of world

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl this session; **[S]** = WebSearch snippet (attributed to its publisher). All claims carry their source inline.

**Cross-cutting findings**
- **GOCF is the confirmed music-festival-shaped contrast case** — and stronger than hypothesized: it is not even a serial tour but a *franchise running parallel city productions on shared weekends* (Edmonton + Winnipeg both July 17–19 2026; Calgary + Vancouver Aug 28–30 + Spokane Aug 29–30) [F gocf site, F wcf site].
- **CBC TV production visibly shapes the two legacy Canadian fests**: venue choice ("Mega Shows require a large venue for cameras, cast, crew" → Ticketmaster-contracted Burton Cummings Theatre) [F wcf FAQ]; content (PG rating when cameras roll; Halifax demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings due to CanCon broadcast rules) [F wcf FAQ, F hfx apply]; format (celebrity host + 6 comics per gala); and the broadcast audience (2M+ viewers) dwarfs the live one [F wcf about].
- **Ticketing vendor map**: Tixr (GOCF *and* Halifax ComedyFest), Showpass (Grindstone), Eventbrite (WTF), own Salesforce-hosted box office (TOsketchfest), 3Common + Ticketmaster split (Winnipeg), Platinumlist + per-venue boxes (Dubai), Fienta (Tokyo), own museum system (LBCF). No festival here offers an official planner app — all are "browse the schedule" sites; several sell passes/bundles instead.

---

## 1. Winnipeg Comedy Festival (Apr 20–26 2026, Winnipeg MB)
- **Organizer**: produced by the Gas Station Arts Centre (GSAC), a nonprofit arts centre in Osborne Village; festival revenue funds GSAC's year-round programming. Founded 2002 by Lara Rae and CBC Radio's Tom Anniko in partnership with GSAC. Presented by Manitoba Liquor Mart. [F https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us, /news/post/105]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 25th anniversary in 2026; 2027 dates already posted (Apr 26–May 2). [F homepage]
- **Scale**: "30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics. One city." 7 days; 7 shows sold out on launch day. Attendance not published; TV reach "over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated comedy festival series". [F /news/post/105, /about-us]
- **Show model**: one-night curated shows. Five recorded-for-broadcast "Mega Shows" at Burton Cummings Theatre (celebrity host + 6 comics, $40, filmed for CBC TV/Gem, PG); The Debaters CBC Radio taping; nightly "edgy, experimental" shows at GSAC; free noon programming (Millennium Library, Fairmont lobby); pay-what-you-can family finale. [F /news/post/105, /faqs]
- **TV shaping (the asked question)**: TV dictates the venue (big theatre for cameras → forces Ticketmaster), the rating (PG while taping, "spicy between takes"), the format (gala tapings = the flagship product), and the economics (the broadcast is the national product; the live fest is its studio audience + a local fringe around it). [F /faqs]
- **Venue geography**: 9 venues citywide — Burton Cummings Theatre (downtown), GSAC hub (Osborne Village), Good Neighbour Brewing, Jubilee Place, Fairmont lobby, Millennium Library etc.; drivable-spread, not walkable-dense. [F /faqs, /news]
- **Clash reality**: mild — Mega Shows are sequential (6:30/9:15) in one theatre while GSAC runs its own nightly slate; 2–3 parallel rooms at peak. Lineup-picking, not a clash grid. [F /news/post/105]
- **Ticketing**: split-vendor by venue: 3Common (local Winnipeg ticketer) for all shows except Ticketmaster-contracted venues (Burton Cummings). [F /faqs]
- **Data reachability**: custom server-rendered site, fully curl-readable; show listing at `/shows` with category-filter URLs (`/shows/show/search-results?category=N`). No API seen. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing significant that week — Tourism Winnipeg lists WCF as the anchor late-April event. [S tourismwinnipeg.com]
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a broadcaster-anchored gala festival with a small venue-run fringe attached.

## 2. Halifax ComedyFest (May 5–9 2026, Halifax NS)
- **Organizer**: CBC-sponsored (CBC tapes and broadcasts sets as TV specials) [S en.wikipedia.org]; produced/run by Premiere Entertainment Group [S halifamous.ca — sole source found]. Site self-describes as "one of only three major comedy festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a six-episode series". [F halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest]
- **Recurrence**: annual each spring since 1995 (32 years in 2027); Season 28 of the TV series is on YouTube. [F about-the-fest, homepage]
- **Scale**: "multiple shows in various venues across the city" — 2026 specifics no longer on the off-season site; NOT FOUND (site now points at 2027). [F homepage]
- **Show model**: one-night curated TV-taping showcases (2026: Opening Night Gala May 6, All Star Show May 7, both recorded for CBC TV/Gem at Light House Arts Centre) + The Debaters radio tapings; open submissions with an explicitly TV-shaped bar: "corporate clean" 8–10 min tape required, international slots "limited due to Canadian content rules for television programming". [S lighthouseartscentre.ca; S en.wikipedia.org; F /apply]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Halifax venues; historically Casino Nova Scotia's Schooner Showroom [S en.wikipedia.org], 2026 galas at Light House Arts Centre (1800 Argyle St) [S lighthouseartscentre.ca]. Walkable downtown cluster.
- **Clash reality**: minimal — roughly one taping bill per night plus club shows; lineup-picking.
- **Ticketing**: per-venue pages resolving to **Tixr** (`tixr.com/groups/hfxcomedyfest`). [F lighthouseartscentre.ca event page]
- **Data reachability**: Weebly-built static site [F — editmysite.com assets]; schedule exists only in-season, so the durable machine surface is the Tixr group. NOT FOUND: any API.
- **Concurrent**: none found in Halifax in early May. (GOCF's Halifax stop is a separate August event, same city — see below.)
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — substantially a television production pipeline with a live festival wrapped around it.

## 3. Grindstone Comedy Festival (July 2–12 2026, Edmonton AB)
- **Organizer**: Grindstone Theatre Society — nonprofit founded 2012; opened the Grindstone Comedy Theatre & Bistro venue in 2018 (up to 14 independent shows/week year-round). Festival is the venue's own production (Executive/Artistic Director Byron Martin); also manages Orange Hub theatres. [F grindstonecomedyfest.com/about-grindstone]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 7th edition in 2026, same home venue. [F about; S cfweradio.ca]
- **Scale**: 11 days (July 2–12) [S cfweradio.ca, exploreedmonton.com]; ~44 scheduled events extracted from the site's schedule [F /schedule]; attendance NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: mostly one-night curated showcases (clown/sketch/improv/magic/drag/stand-up) + one-night headliners (Shaun Majumder, K. Trevor Wilson, DJ Demers, Chris Locke, Sterling Scott, Dakota Ray Hebert) + open-entry competition pipelines feeding the fest (King of the Hill improv; Stand-Up Stand-Off, 5 weekly prelim rounds → finals at the festival) + industry panel/networking + open mic. [F /schedule, /festivalinfo]
- **Venue geography**: hub-and-spokes, all Edmonton: Grindstone Comedy Theatre + Bistro/patio (hub), Orange Hub Theatre/Lobby, Howl & Roar Outdoor Stage, Metro Cinema, Kinshi Rinji, Blackdog Freehouse. [F /schedule] The about page's "five days… two stages" text is stale boilerplate contradicted by the 2026 schedule and press. [F /about-grindstone vs S cfweradio.ca]
- **Clash reality**: real but small — 2–4 rooms in play at the same hour on peak nights. [F /schedule]
- **Ticketing**: **Showpass** (site's buy-links go to `showpass.com/s/events/all/?search_string=gcf2026`), plus in-person box office; 4-show bundle = 20% off. [F homepage, /schedule]
- **Data reachability**: Wix site but the schedule text is present in served HTML (curl-extractable); Showpass has a public events API behind the search URL — the most machine-readable of the Canadian set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: overlaps Calgary Stampede (province-wide draw) and Edmonton's July festival season; Edmonton Street Performers Festival runs mid-July [S en.wikipedia.org] — not checked show-by-show. GOCF's Edmonton stop follows a week later (July 17–19). [F gocf site]
- **Planner/app**: none; a "digital program" PDF. [F /festivalinfo]
- **Verdict**: hybrid — venue-run, community/competition-fed and fringe-spirited, but curated single-tickets showcase in shape.

## 4a. Toronto Sketch Comedy Festival (Mar 4–15 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: registered Canadian charity (#824216808 RR 0001) founded 2005 by Toronto comedians; year-round programs (monthly cabaret, Comedy Country series, Sketch Comedy Project Fund). [F torontosketchfest.com/about, /2026-festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: annual every March since 2005 ("Toronto's longest running comedy festival"); 12 days, "dozens of shows" across 2 venues: The Theatre Centre (West Queen West) + Comedy Bar Bloor. [F homepage FAQ]
- **Show model**: curated troupe lineups, sketch/clown/musical comedy; single tickets + festival passes. Submissions process NOT FOUND this pass. [F homepage, /about]
- **Ticketing/data**: own box office on a Salesforce-hosted SPA (`tosketchfest.my.salesforce-sites.com/ticket/#/` — PatronManager pattern); hash-routed JS app, not curl-readable; WordPress marketing site is. [F]
- **Clash**: two rooms, staggered slots — lineup-picking. **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-major in March; Toronto's JFL is in autumn.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like with fringe texture (multi-show pass browsing across a 12-day slate).

## 4b. WHAT THE FESTIVAL! (Sept 24–27 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: tiny independent team (org est. 2022; directors Byron & Alicia per testimonials); clown/puppet/drag/burlesque "live theatre festival". [F wtfestival.ca]
- **Scale**: 3rd annual; 3 feature shows + 2 cabarets + a puppetry workshop + a talk (~8 events) over 4 days in 3 small rooms (Small World Music, Sweet Action Theatre, Social Arts Studio Space); staggered times, zero clash. New in 2026: multi-show passes ($75/3, $110/5). [F /whats-on]
- **Ticketing/data**: Eventbrite per show + an Eventbrite collection; Squarespace site, fully curl-readable. [F /whats-on]
- **Concurrent — the finding**: its entire run sits inside JFL Toronto (Sept 24–Oct 3 2026, Pete Davidson/John Cleese/Tiffany Haddish) [S exclaim.ca] — a micro-festival deliberately living under a mega-festival's dates. (JFL Toronto is another agent's beat.)
- **Verdict**: micro curated showcase (closer to an indie theatre mini-fest than either pole).

## 5. Great Outdoors Comedy Festival (Vancouver stop Aug 28–30 2026) — THE STRUCTURAL CASE
- **Operator**: Trixstar LIVE / Trixstar Entertainment, an Edmonton-based promoter; footer links trixstar.com. [F greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about; S dailyhive.com]
- **The roving pattern (2026)**: 7 stops — Edmonton July 17–19 (Kinsmen Park) [S exploreedmonton.com], Winnipeg July 17–19 (Assiniboine Park) [F winnipegcomedyfestival.com homepage], Halifax Aug 6–9 (Garrison Grounds) [S exclaim.ca; S tixr.com], Calgary Aug 28–30 (Prince's Island Park), Vancouver Aug 28–30 (Stanley Park, Brockton Point), Spokane WA Aug 29–30 (One Spokane Stadium), Mississauga Sept 11–13 (Erindale Park) [F homepage]. 2027 already on sale: Edmonton + Winnipeg July 16–18, Halifax Aug 6–8. [F homepage] **Same-weekend twin stops prove parallel productions, not one touring caravan.** Past cities also include Ottawa and London ON. [F /about]
- **History/scale**: originated 2021 in Edmonton; cumulative "400,000+ attendees, 176+ performers, $800,000 community donations since 2021"; full 2021–2025 lineup archive on-site (Kevin Hart, Seinfeld, Burr, Mulaney, Schumer, Segura…). [F /about] Vancouver permit: max 10,000 guests/day at Brockton Fields (2023 Park Board filing). [F dailyhive.com]
- **Show model**: one stage per city; 2 shows/day (2:00 pm matinee + 7:30 pm evening), each a one-off bill of ~2–5 touring headliners (e.g. Vancouver: Bill Burr Fri; Jeselnik/Davidson/Holmes/Jensen Sat eve; Matt Rife Sun eve); grounds cleared between shows; explicitly **no open submissions** ("we do not have an application process"). [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Music-festival mechanics**: GA / GA+ / VIP Club / VIP Table tiers, weekend passes, BYO camping chair rules, food trucks, licensed grounds, no re-entry, 18+/19+ no minors, rain or shine, on-site cannabis in AB, 50/50 for local charities. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Ticketing**: **Tixr only** (`tixr.com/groups/gocf`) — "tickets will only be available online through Tixr"; Spokane support via TicketsWest (stadium's vendor). Not Ticketmaster. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Data reachability**: Webflow marketing site, fully server-rendered and curl-readable (cities, dates, show cards all in HTML); Tixr event pages are JS apps (Tixr exposes JSON endpoints). [F]
- **Clash reality**: none by design — one stage, sequential shows. The scheduling constraint is *which city you're in*.
- **Planner/app**: none (SMS marketing line instead). [F homepage]
- **Verdict**: the anti-fringe pole — a promoter-owned, music-festival-shaped touring/franchise comedy product (few stages, one show per act, roving cities).

## 6. Dubai Comedy Festival (Oct 9–18 2026, Dubai)
- **Organizer**: government-backed promoter consortium. BRAG (Dubai event agency): "In 2020, Brag partnered with DTCM [Dubai's tourism department] and Live Nation to bring back the Dubai Comedy Festival after a long hiatus" [F brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival]; recent editions "presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME Events and DXB Live" [S katchinternational.com]; official site footer links dubaicalendar.com and brag.ae [F dubaicomedyfest.ae].
- **Recurrence**: 7th edition (of the revived run) in 2026; grew from 4 days (2020) to 10. Annual, same city, rotating prime venues. [F /about; F brag.world]
- **Scale**: 10 days, "50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"; attendance only as "thousands of festival-goers every year". [F homepage; F brag.world]
- **Show model**: one-night (occasionally two) international touring acts — Mo Gilligan, Katherine Ryan, Zarna Garg, Vir Das, Munawar Faruqui, Jamie Lever — many "presented by" third-party promoters under the festival umbrella (AlQaiser Events, AJ Entertainment, Facepalm Comedy); deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Russian; historically also Tagalog and French). Plus "Comedy Bizarre", BRAG's own fringe-calendar sidebar for up-and-comers. [F /shows; F brag.world]
- **Venue geography**: spread across the car-scale city: Dubai Opera (Downtown), New Covent Garden Theatre (Mall of the Emirates), Coca-Cola Arena (City Walk), Pepperoni Comedy Club, Emirates Theatre (Jumeirah). Arena + theatres, not walkable. [F homepage, /about, /shows]
- **Clash reality**: 2–3 shows per evening across distant venues (e.g. Oct 16: Shane Todd 6pm + Abbas Bukhari 9pm at NCGT, Zarna Garg at Dubai Opera) — lineup-picking with traffic, not a fringe grid. [F /shows]
- **Ticketing**: per-show multi-vendor: **Platinumlist** (nearly every show, plus an aggregating microsite dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net [S platinumlist.net]), Dubai Opera's own box office, Ticketmaster.ae for some, Coca-Cola Arena's site for arena shows. Prices from AED 125–250. [F /shows]
- **Data reachability**: Squarespace, server-rendered — the /shows page carries every show's date, venue, language, from-price and vendor links in plain HTML; easiest large-festival page to read mechanically in this whole set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: GITEX Global moved to Dec 7–11 2026 (Expo City), so no mega-event clash; October carries mid-size trade shows (WETEX Oct 20–22, Dubai AI Festival Oct 26–27). [S gitex.com, mediaoffice.ae, khaleejtimes.com]
- **Planner/app**: none of its own; Dubai Calendar and Platinumlist serve as listings layers.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a destination-marketing umbrella over one-night touring acts (with a small fringe sidebar).

## 7. Tokyo International Comedy Festival (Sept 17–27 2026, Tokyo) — brief
- **Organizer**: Tokyo Comedy Bar (Shibuya club, "home for stand-up in Japan… English & Japanese, since 2022"; operating company Stand-Up Tokyo GK), co-presented with Baird Brewing. Venue-run, commercial. [F tokyocomedybar.com/festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: 3rd edition; 11 days, "120+ shows", self-billed "East Asia's largest stand-up comedy festival"; attendance NOT FOUND. [F /festival]
- **Show model**: club-scale mix — solo shows, improv, roast battles ("Roastfest", 4th edition), live podcasts, workshops; two competitions: King of Kanto (English) and Tokyo Comedy Grand Prix (Japanese); international acts (Sammy Obeid, Emily Catalano) alongside the local Eng/JP scene. [F /festival; S tokyocheapo.com, timeout.com]
- **Venue geography**: TCB as hub plus small satellites: Mame Romantic, DecaBar Super, The Millennials Shibuya, Baird taprooms (Nakameguro, Bashamichi) — Shibuya-centred, mostly walkable/train-trivial. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Clash reality**: modest — sequential slots at the small hub with some satellite parallelism; 120 shows in 11 days implies ~11/day across ~6 tiny rooms.
- **Ticketing**: **Fienta** per show (fienta.com links on the festival page). [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: Wix; the headline facts are server-rendered but the lineup grid is client-rendered (empty via curl) — the practical machine surface is Fienta's per-event pages. [F /festlineup]
- **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-significant found; general Tokyo autumn events only. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Verdict**: fringe-ish energy at club scale, but curated venue-run showcase in structure.

## 8. Lucille Ball Comedy Festival (Aug 6–9 2026, Jamestown NY) — brief
- **Organizer**: the National Comedy Center — "the nation's official cultural institution dedicated to comedy" (museum + national archive) with the Lucille Ball Desi Arnaz Museum; the institution-anchored model. [F comedycenter.org/festival]
- **Recurrence**: annual since 1991 (35 years per Post-Journal), held each August around Ball's Aug 6 birthday in her hometown. [S post-journal.com]
- **Scale**: "over 50 live events, over 15,000 attendees annually from nearly every state" [F /festival]; "over 10,000 visitors" per regional press [S tourchautauqua.com/post-journal snippets].
- **Show model**: arena headliners (2026: Jerry Seinfeld Thu, Bert Kreischer Sat, Seth Meyers Sun at Northwest Arena; mainstage Stand-Up Showcase Fri) + Lucy nostalgia programming, museum talks, block parties, kids' comedy, late-night club showcases — comedy-as-heritage wrapped around touring names. [F /lbcf-2026 press release; F /festival]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Jamestown cluster — the Center, the Lucy Desi Museum, Northwest Arena, clubs; small-town walkable. [F /festival]
- **Clash reality**: real parallelism at peak (museum programs + showcases + arena) but built so the headliner slots dominate; membership presale manages demand. [F /festival]
- **Ticketing**: the Center's own system (`tickets.comedycenter.org`, Gateway-style .aspx museum ticketing); members get presale. [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: WordPress, server-rendered and curl-friendly; ticketing system is legacy-web, no API seen; festival page currently in "see you in 2027" mode. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing found in Jamestown; coincidentally shares its exact dates with GOCF Halifax (different country/market).
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: institution-anchored destination showcase — a museum using one-night headliners to power comedy-heritage tourism.

---

## Sources
**Fetched (curl)**: winnipegcomedyfestival.com (/, /about-us, /faqs, /shows, /news/post/105/april-20-26-2026) · halifaxcomedyfest.ca (/, /about-the-fest.html, /apply.html) · lighthouseartscentre.ca/events/halifax-comedy-festival-all-star-show · en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_Comedy_Festival · halifamous.ca/series/halifax-comedyfest-2026 · grindstonecomedyfest.com (/, /festivalinfo, /schedule, /about-grindstone) · torontosketchfest.com (/, /about/, /2026-festival) · wtfestival.ca (/, /whats-on) · greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com (/, /about, /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs) · dailyhive.com/vancouver/the-great-outdoors-comedy-festival-proposal-stanley-park · dubaicomedyfest.ae (/, /about, /shows) · brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival · tokyocomedybar.com (/festival, /festlineup) · comedycenter.org (/festival/, /lbcf-2026/)

**Search snippets (publisher attributed)**: cfweradio.ca (Grindstone July 2–12) · exploreedmonton.com (Grindstone; GOCF Edmonton July 17–19) · exclaim.ca (GOCF 2026 six-city lineup, Halifax Aug 6–9; JFL Toronto Sept 24–Oct 3 2026) · tixr.com/groups/gocf & /groups/hfxcomedyfest (vendor confirmation) · tokyocheapo.com, timeout.com/tokyo, tokyoweekender.com (TICF venues/competitions) · katchinternational.com (DCF producer consortium) · platinumlist.net (DCF microsite) · gitex.com + mediaoffice.ae + khaleejtimes.com (GITEX moved to Dec 2026) · tourismwinnipeg.com (April Winnipeg calendar) · post-journal.com (LBCF 35 years) · tourchautauqua.com (LBCF attendance) · en.wikipedia.org (Edmonton Street Performers Festival; Prince's Island Park)

**Not found / honest gaps**: Halifax 2026 total show/venue count and producer confirmation beyond Halifamous; Grindstone and Tokyo attendance figures; TOsketchfest submissions process; per-stop GOCF attendance (only the cumulative 400k+ and Vancouver's 10k/day permit cap).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the SXSW Comedy Festival 2026:

**Event Dates & Overview:**
The 2026 SXSW Comedy Festival is set to take place in Austin, TX from March 13-16 amid the broader SXSW festival, and the 19th edition of SXSW Comedy will see the festival play host to stand-up showcases, improv, game shows, live podcast recordings, and more.

**Venues:**
Anyone who has registered at SXSW can attend shows at The Creek and The Cave and at Esther's Follies.

**Showcase Highlights:**

- **The Stand Comedy Showcase at Esther's Follies:** The Stand presents a special SXSW showcase at Esther's Follies, bringing its signature mix of killer lineups, top-tier talent, and unmistakable New York energy to Austin.

- **Cracked Comedy Club:** Cracked Comedy Club has an Official Showcase at SXSW 2026.

- **Gotham Comedy Showcase:** Gotham Comedy Club has been one of New York's top stand-up venues for nearly 30 years, and now that coveted stage comes to SXSW, bringing its signature showcase to festival audiences.

**Badge Access:**
The festival is open to all badge holders, though one standout show, the Dropout Improv Show, is only open to Platinum badgeholders and people who purchase tickets independently of SXSW.

# Comedy festival research: Canada (non-JFL) + rest of world

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl this session; **[S]** = WebSearch snippet (attributed to its publisher). All claims carry their source inline.

**Cross-cutting findings**
- **GOCF is the confirmed music-festival-shaped contrast case** — and stronger than hypothesized: it is not even a serial tour but a *franchise running parallel city productions on shared weekends* (Edmonton + Winnipeg both July 17–19 2026; Calgary + Vancouver Aug 28–30 + Spokane Aug 29–30) [F gocf site, F wcf site].
- **CBC TV production visibly shapes the two legacy Canadian fests**: venue choice ("Mega Shows require a large venue for cameras, cast, crew" → Ticketmaster-contracted Burton Cummings Theatre) [F wcf FAQ]; content (PG rating when cameras roll; Halifax demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings due to CanCon broadcast rules) [F wcf FAQ, F hfx apply]; format (celebrity host + 6 comics per gala); and the broadcast audience (2M+ viewers) dwarfs the live one [F wcf about].
- **Ticketing vendor map**: Tixr (GOCF *and* Halifax ComedyFest), Showpass (Grindstone), Eventbrite (WTF), own Salesforce-hosted box office (TOsketchfest), 3Common + Ticketmaster split (Winnipeg), Platinumlist + per-venue boxes (Dubai), Fienta (Tokyo), own museum system (LBCF). No festival here offers an official planner app — all are "browse the schedule" sites; several sell passes/bundles instead.

---

## 1. Winnipeg Comedy Festival (Apr 20–26 2026, Winnipeg MB)
- **Organizer**: produced by the Gas Station Arts Centre (GSAC), a nonprofit arts centre in Osborne Village; festival revenue funds GSAC's year-round programming. Founded 2002 by Lara Rae and CBC Radio's Tom Anniko in partnership with GSAC. Presented by Manitoba Liquor Mart. [F https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us, /news/post/105]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 25th anniversary in 2026; 2027 dates already posted (Apr 26–May 2). [F homepage]
- **Scale**: "30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics. One city." 7 days; 7 shows sold out on launch day. Attendance not published; TV reach "over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated comedy festival series". [F /news/post/105, /about-us]
- **Show model**: one-night curated shows. Five recorded-for-broadcast "Mega Shows" at Burton Cummings Theatre (celebrity host + 6 comics, $40, filmed for CBC TV/Gem, PG); The Debaters CBC Radio taping; nightly "edgy, experimental" shows at GSAC; free noon programming (Millennium Library, Fairmont lobby); pay-what-you-can family finale. [F /news/post/105, /faqs]
- **TV shaping (the asked question)**: TV dictates the venue (big theatre for cameras → forces Ticketmaster), the rating (PG while taping, "spicy between takes"), the format (gala tapings = the flagship product), and the economics (the broadcast is the national product; the live fest is its studio audience + a local fringe around it). [F /faqs]
- **Venue geography**: 9 venues citywide — Burton Cummings Theatre (downtown), GSAC hub (Osborne Village), Good Neighbour Brewing, Jubilee Place, Fairmont lobby, Millennium Library etc.; drivable-spread, not walkable-dense. [F /faqs, /news]
- **Clash reality**: mild — Mega Shows are sequential (6:30/9:15) in one theatre while GSAC runs its own nightly slate; 2–3 parallel rooms at peak. Lineup-picking, not a clash grid. [F /news/post/105]
- **Ticketing**: split-vendor by venue: 3Common (local Winnipeg ticketer) for all shows except Ticketmaster-contracted venues (Burton Cummings). [F /faqs]
- **Data reachability**: custom server-rendered site, fully curl-readable; show listing at `/shows` with category-filter URLs (`/shows/show/search-results?category=N`). No API seen. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing significant that week — Tourism Winnipeg lists WCF as the anchor late-April event. [S tourismwinnipeg.com]
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a broadcaster-anchored gala festival with a small venue-run fringe attached.

## 2. Halifax ComedyFest (May 5–9 2026, Halifax NS)
- **Organizer**: CBC-sponsored (CBC tapes and broadcasts sets as TV specials) [S en.wikipedia.org]; produced/run by Premiere Entertainment Group [S halifamous.ca — sole source found]. Site self-describes as "one of only three major comedy festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a six-episode series". [F halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest]
- **Recurrence**: annual each spring since 1995 (32 years in 2027); Season 28 of the TV series is on YouTube. [F about-the-fest, homepage]
- **Scale**: "multiple shows in various venues across the city" — 2026 specifics no longer on the off-season site; NOT FOUND (site now points at 2027). [F homepage]
- **Show model**: one-night curated TV-taping showcases (2026: Opening Night Gala May 6, All Star Show May 7, both recorded for CBC TV/Gem at Light House Arts Centre) + The Debaters radio tapings; open submissions with an explicitly TV-shaped bar: "corporate clean" 8–10 min tape required, international slots "limited due to Canadian content rules for television programming". [S lighthouseartscentre.ca; S en.wikipedia.org; F /apply]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Halifax venues; historically Casino Nova Scotia's Schooner Showroom [S en.wikipedia.org], 2026 galas at Light House Arts Centre (1800 Argyle St) [S lighthouseartscentre.ca]. Walkable downtown cluster.
- **Clash reality**: minimal — roughly one taping bill per night plus club shows; lineup-picking.
- **Ticketing**: per-venue pages resolving to **Tixr** (`tixr.com/groups/hfxcomedyfest`). [F lighthouseartscentre.ca event page]
- **Data reachability**: Weebly-built static site [F — editmysite.com assets]; schedule exists only in-season, so the durable machine surface is the Tixr group. NOT FOUND: any API.
- **Concurrent**: none found in Halifax in early May. (GOCF's Halifax stop is a separate August event, same city — see below.)
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — substantially a television production pipeline with a live festival wrapped around it.

## 3. Grindstone Comedy Festival (July 2–12 2026, Edmonton AB)
- **Organizer**: Grindstone Theatre Society — nonprofit founded 2012; opened the Grindstone Comedy Theatre & Bistro venue in 2018 (up to 14 independent shows/week year-round). Festival is the venue's own production (Executive/Artistic Director Byron Martin); also manages Orange Hub theatres. [F grindstonecomedyfest.com/about-grindstone]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 7th edition in 2026, same home venue. [F about; S cfweradio.ca]
- **Scale**: 11 days (July 2–12) [S cfweradio.ca, exploreedmonton.com]; ~44 scheduled events extracted from the site's schedule [F /schedule]; attendance NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: mostly one-night curated showcases (clown/sketch/improv/magic/drag/stand-up) + one-night headliners (Shaun Majumder, K. Trevor Wilson, DJ Demers, Chris Locke, Sterling Scott, Dakota Ray Hebert) + open-entry competition pipelines feeding the fest (King of the Hill improv; Stand-Up Stand-Off, 5 weekly prelim rounds → finals at the festival) + industry panel/networking + open mic. [F /schedule, /festivalinfo]
- **Venue geography**: hub-and-spokes, all Edmonton: Grindstone Comedy Theatre + Bistro/patio (hub), Orange Hub Theatre/Lobby, Howl & Roar Outdoor Stage, Metro Cinema, Kinshi Rinji, Blackdog Freehouse. [F /schedule] The about page's "five days… two stages" text is stale boilerplate contradicted by the 2026 schedule and press. [F /about-grindstone vs S cfweradio.ca]
- **Clash reality**: real but small — 2–4 rooms in play at the same hour on peak nights. [F /schedule]
- **Ticketing**: **Showpass** (site's buy-links go to `showpass.com/s/events/all/?search_string=gcf2026`), plus in-person box office; 4-show bundle = 20% off. [F homepage, /schedule]
- **Data reachability**: Wix site but the schedule text is present in served HTML (curl-extractable); Showpass has a public events API behind the search URL — the most machine-readable of the Canadian set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: overlaps Calgary Stampede (province-wide draw) and Edmonton's July festival season; Edmonton Street Performers Festival runs mid-July [S en.wikipedia.org] — not checked show-by-show. GOCF's Edmonton stop follows a week later (July 17–19). [F gocf site]
- **Planner/app**: none; a "digital program" PDF. [F /festivalinfo]
- **Verdict**: hybrid — venue-run, community/competition-fed and fringe-spirited, but curated single-tickets showcase in shape.

## 4a. Toronto Sketch Comedy Festival (Mar 4–15 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: registered Canadian charity (#824216808 RR 0001) founded 2005 by Toronto comedians; year-round programs (monthly cabaret, Comedy Country series, Sketch Comedy Project Fund). [F torontosketchfest.com/about, /2026-festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: annual every March since 2005 ("Toronto's longest running comedy festival"); 12 days, "dozens of shows" across 2 venues: The Theatre Centre (West Queen West) + Comedy Bar Bloor. [F homepage FAQ]
- **Show model**: curated troupe lineups, sketch/clown/musical comedy; single tickets + festival passes. Submissions process NOT FOUND this pass. [F homepage, /about]
- **Ticketing/data**: own box office on a Salesforce-hosted SPA (`tosketchfest.my.salesforce-sites.com/ticket/#/` — PatronManager pattern); hash-routed JS app, not curl-readable; WordPress marketing site is. [F]
- **Clash**: two rooms, staggered slots — lineup-picking. **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-major in March; Toronto's JFL is in autumn.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like with fringe texture (multi-show pass browsing across a 12-day slate).

## 4b. WHAT THE FESTIVAL! (Sept 24–27 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: tiny independent team (org est. 2022; directors Byron & Alicia per testimonials); clown/puppet/drag/burlesque "live theatre festival". [F wtfestival.ca]
- **Scale**: 3rd annual; 3 feature shows + 2 cabarets + a puppetry workshop + a talk (~8 events) over 4 days in 3 small rooms (Small World Music, Sweet Action Theatre, Social Arts Studio Space); staggered times, zero clash. New in 2026: multi-show passes ($75/3, $110/5). [F /whats-on]
- **Ticketing/data**: Eventbrite per show + an Eventbrite collection; Squarespace site, fully curl-readable. [F /whats-on]
- **Concurrent — the finding**: its entire run sits inside JFL Toronto (Sept 24–Oct 3 2026, Pete Davidson/John Cleese/Tiffany Haddish) [S exclaim.ca] — a micro-festival deliberately living under a mega-festival's dates. (JFL Toronto is another agent's beat.)
- **Verdict**: micro curated showcase (closer to an indie theatre mini-fest than either pole).

## 5. Great Outdoors Comedy Festival (Vancouver stop Aug 28–30 2026) — THE STRUCTURAL CASE
- **Operator**: Trixstar LIVE / Trixstar Entertainment, an Edmonton-based promoter; footer links trixstar.com. [F greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about; S dailyhive.com]
- **The roving pattern (2026)**: 7 stops — Edmonton July 17–19 (Kinsmen Park) [S exploreedmonton.com], Winnipeg July 17–19 (Assiniboine Park) [F winnipegcomedyfestival.com homepage], Halifax Aug 6–9 (Garrison Grounds) [S exclaim.ca; S tixr.com], Calgary Aug 28–30 (Prince's Island Park), Vancouver Aug 28–30 (Stanley Park, Brockton Point), Spokane WA Aug 29–30 (One Spokane Stadium), Mississauga Sept 11–13 (Erindale Park) [F homepage]. 2027 already on sale: Edmonton + Winnipeg July 16–18, Halifax Aug 6–8. [F homepage] **Same-weekend twin stops prove parallel productions, not one touring caravan.** Past cities also include Ottawa and London ON. [F /about]
- **History/scale**: originated 2021 in Edmonton; cumulative "400,000+ attendees, 176+ performers, $800,000 community donations since 2021"; full 2021–2025 lineup archive on-site (Kevin Hart, Seinfeld, Burr, Mulaney, Schumer, Segura…). [F /about] Vancouver permit: max 10,000 guests/day at Brockton Fields (2023 Park Board filing). [F dailyhive.com]
- **Show model**: one stage per city; 2 shows/day (2:00 pm matinee + 7:30 pm evening), each a one-off bill of ~2–5 touring headliners (e.g. Vancouver: Bill Burr Fri; Jeselnik/Davidson/Holmes/Jensen Sat eve; Matt Rife Sun eve); grounds cleared between shows; explicitly **no open submissions** ("we do not have an application process"). [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Music-festival mechanics**: GA / GA+ / VIP Club / VIP Table tiers, weekend passes, BYO camping chair rules, food trucks, licensed grounds, no re-entry, 18+/19+ no minors, rain or shine, on-site cannabis in AB, 50/50 for local charities. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Ticketing**: **Tixr only** (`tixr.com/groups/gocf`) — "tickets will only be available online through Tixr"; Spokane support via TicketsWest (stadium's vendor). Not Ticketmaster. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Data reachability**: Webflow marketing site, fully server-rendered and curl-readable (cities, dates, show cards all in HTML); Tixr event pages are JS apps (Tixr exposes JSON endpoints). [F]
- **Clash reality**: none by design — one stage, sequential shows. The scheduling constraint is *which city you're in*.
- **Planner/app**: none (SMS marketing line instead). [F homepage]
- **Verdict**: the anti-fringe pole — a promoter-owned, music-festival-shaped touring/franchise comedy product (few stages, one show per act, roving cities).

## 6. Dubai Comedy Festival (Oct 9–18 2026, Dubai)
- **Organizer**: government-backed promoter consortium. BRAG (Dubai event agency): "In 2020, Brag partnered with DTCM [Dubai's tourism department] and Live Nation to bring back the Dubai Comedy Festival after a long hiatus" [F brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival]; recent editions "presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME Events and DXB Live" [S katchinternational.com]; official site footer links dubaicalendar.com and brag.ae [F dubaicomedyfest.ae].
- **Recurrence**: 7th edition (of the revived run) in 2026; grew from 4 days (2020) to 10. Annual, same city, rotating prime venues. [F /about; F brag.world]
- **Scale**: 10 days, "50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"; attendance only as "thousands of festival-goers every year". [F homepage; F brag.world]
- **Show model**: one-night (occasionally two) international touring acts — Mo Gilligan, Katherine Ryan, Zarna Garg, Vir Das, Munawar Faruqui, Jamie Lever — many "presented by" third-party promoters under the festival umbrella (AlQaiser Events, AJ Entertainment, Facepalm Comedy); deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Russian; historically also Tagalog and French). Plus "Comedy Bizarre", BRAG's own fringe-calendar sidebar for up-and-comers. [F /shows; F brag.world]
- **Venue geography**: spread across the car-scale city: Dubai Opera (Downtown), New Covent Garden Theatre (Mall of the Emirates), Coca-Cola Arena (City Walk), Pepperoni Comedy Club, Emirates Theatre (Jumeirah). Arena + theatres, not walkable. [F homepage, /about, /shows]
- **Clash reality**: 2–3 shows per evening across distant venues (e.g. Oct 16: Shane Todd 6pm + Abbas Bukhari 9pm at NCGT, Zarna Garg at Dubai Opera) — lineup-picking with traffic, not a fringe grid. [F /shows]
- **Ticketing**: per-show multi-vendor: **Platinumlist** (nearly every show, plus an aggregating microsite dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net [S platinumlist.net]), Dubai Opera's own box office, Ticketmaster.ae for some, Coca-Cola Arena's site for arena shows. Prices from AED 125–250. [F /shows]
- **Data reachability**: Squarespace, server-rendered — the /shows page carries every show's date, venue, language, from-price and vendor links in plain HTML; easiest large-festival page to read mechanically in this whole set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: GITEX Global moved to Dec 7–11 2026 (Expo City), so no mega-event clash; October carries mid-size trade shows (WETEX Oct 20–22, Dubai AI Festival Oct 26–27). [S gitex.com, mediaoffice.ae, khaleejtimes.com]
- **Planner/app**: none of its own; Dubai Calendar and Platinumlist serve as listings layers.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a destination-marketing umbrella over one-night touring acts (with a small fringe sidebar).

## 7. Tokyo International Comedy Festival (Sept 17–27 2026, Tokyo) — brief
- **Organizer**: Tokyo Comedy Bar (Shibuya club, "home for stand-up in Japan… English & Japanese, since 2022"; operating company Stand-Up Tokyo GK), co-presented with Baird Brewing. Venue-run, commercial. [F tokyocomedybar.com/festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: 3rd edition; 11 days, "120+ shows", self-billed "East Asia's largest stand-up comedy festival"; attendance NOT FOUND. [F /festival]
- **Show model**: club-scale mix — solo shows, improv, roast battles ("Roastfest", 4th edition), live podcasts, workshops; two competitions: King of Kanto (English) and Tokyo Comedy Grand Prix (Japanese); international acts (Sammy Obeid, Emily Catalano) alongside the local Eng/JP scene. [F /festival; S tokyocheapo.com, timeout.com]
- **Venue geography**: TCB as hub plus small satellites: Mame Romantic, DecaBar Super, The Millennials Shibuya, Baird taprooms (Nakameguro, Bashamichi) — Shibuya-centred, mostly walkable/train-trivial. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Clash reality**: modest — sequential slots at the small hub with some satellite parallelism; 120 shows in 11 days implies ~11/day across ~6 tiny rooms.
- **Ticketing**: **Fienta** per show (fienta.com links on the festival page). [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: Wix; the headline facts are server-rendered but the lineup grid is client-rendered (empty via curl) — the practical machine surface is Fienta's per-event pages. [F /festlineup]
- **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-significant found; general Tokyo autumn events only. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Verdict**: fringe-ish energy at club scale, but curated venue-run showcase in structure.

## 8. Lucille Ball Comedy Festival (Aug 6–9 2026, Jamestown NY) — brief
- **Organizer**: the National Comedy Center — "the nation's official cultural institution dedicated to comedy" (museum + national archive) with the Lucille Ball Desi Arnaz Museum; the institution-anchored model. [F comedycenter.org/festival]
- **Recurrence**: annual since 1991 (35 years per Post-Journal), held each August around Ball's Aug 6 birthday in her hometown. [S post-journal.com]
- **Scale**: "over 50 live events, over 15,000 attendees annually from nearly every state" [F /festival]; "over 10,000 visitors" per regional press [S tourchautauqua.com/post-journal snippets].
- **Show model**: arena headliners (2026: Jerry Seinfeld Thu, Bert Kreischer Sat, Seth Meyers Sun at Northwest Arena; mainstage Stand-Up Showcase Fri) + Lucy nostalgia programming, museum talks, block parties, kids' comedy, late-night club showcases — comedy-as-heritage wrapped around touring names. [F /lbcf-2026 press release; F /festival]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Jamestown cluster — the Center, the Lucy Desi Museum, Northwest Arena, clubs; small-town walkable. [F /festival]
- **Clash reality**: real parallelism at peak (museum programs + showcases + arena) but built so the headliner slots dominate; membership presale manages demand. [F /festival]
- **Ticketing**: the Center's own system (`tickets.comedycenter.org`, Gateway-style .aspx museum ticketing); members get presale. [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: WordPress, server-rendered and curl-friendly; ticketing system is legacy-web, no API seen; festival page currently in "see you in 2027" mode. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing found in Jamestown; coincidentally shares its exact dates with GOCF Halifax (different country/market).
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: institution-anchored destination showcase — a museum using one-night headliners to power comedy-heritage tourism.

Five recorded-for-broadcast "Mega Shows" at Burton Cummings Theatre (celebrity host + 6 comics, $40, filmed for CBC TV/Gem, PG); The Debaters CBC Radio taping; nightly "edgy, experimental" shows at GSAC; free noon programming (Millennium Library, Fairmont lobby); pay-what-you-can family finale. [F /news/post/105, /faqs]
- **TV shaping (the asked question)**: TV dictates the venue (big theatre for cameras → forces Ticketmaster), the rating (PG while taping, "spicy between takes"), the format (gala tapings = the flagship product), and the economics (the broadcast is the national product; the live fest is its studio audience + a local fringe around it). [F /faqs]
- **Venue geography**: 9 venues citywide — Burton Cummings Theatre (downtown), GSAC hub (Osborne Village), Good Neighbour Brewing, Jubilee Place, Fairmont lobby, Millennium Library etc.; drivable-spread, not walkable-dense. [F /faqs, /news]

## 2. Halifax ComedyFest (May 5–9 2026, Halifax NS)
- **Organizer**: CBC-sponsored (CBC tapes and broadcasts sets as TV specials) [S en.wikipedia.org]; produced/run by Premiere Entertainment Group [S halifamous.ca — sole source found]. Site self-describes as "one of only three major comedy festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a six-episode series". [F halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest]
- **Recurrence**: annual each spring since 1995 (32 years in 2027); Season 28 of the TV series is on YouTube. [F about-the-fest, homepage]
- **Scale**: "multiple shows in various venues across the city" — 2026 specifics no longer on the off-season site; NOT FOUND (site now points at 2027). [F homepage]
- **Show model**: one-night curated TV-taping showcases (2026: Opening Night Gala May 6, All Star Show May 7, both recorded for CBC TV/Gem at Light House Arts Centre) + The Debaters radio tapings; open submissions with an explicitly TV-shaped bar: "corporate clean" 8–10 min tape required, international slots "limited due to Canadian content rules for television programming". [S lighthouseartscentre.ca; S en.wikipedia.org; F /apply]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Halifax venues; historically Casino Nova Scotia's Schooner Showroom [S en.wikipedia.org], 2026 galas at Light House Arts Centre (1800 Argyle St) [S lighthouseartscentre.ca]. Walkable downtown cluster.

- **Data reachability**: Weebly-built static site [F — editmysite.com assets]; schedule exists only in-season, so the durable machine surface is the Tixr group. NOT FOUND: any API.
- **Concurrent**: none found in Halifax in early May. (GOCF's Halifax stop is a separate August event, same city — see below.)

## 3. Grindstone Comedy Festival (July 2–12 2026, Edmonton AB)
- **Organizer**: Grindstone Theatre Society — nonprofit founded 2012; opened the Grindstone Comedy Theatre & Bistro venue in 2018 (up to 14 independent shows/week year-round). Festival is the venue's own production (Executive/Artistic Director Byron Martin); also manages Orange Hub theatres. [F grindstonecomedyfest.com/about-grindstone]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 7th edition in 2026, same home venue. [F about; S cfweradio.ca]
- **Scale**: 11 days (July 2–12) [S cfweradio.ca, exploreedmonton.com]; ~44 scheduled events extracted from the site's schedule [F /schedule]; attendance NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: mostly one-night curated showcases (clown/sketch/improv/magic/drag/stand-up) + one-night headliners (Shaun Majumder, K. Trevor Wilson, DJ Demers, Chris Locke, Sterling Scott, Dakota Ray Hebert) + open-entry competition pipelines feeding the fest (King of the Hill improv; Stand-Up Stand-Off, 5 weekly prelim rounds → finals at the festival) + industry panel/networking + open mic. [F /schedule, /festivalinfo]
- **Venue geography**: hub-and-spokes, all Edmonton: Grindstone Comedy Theatre + Bistro/patio (hub), Orange Hub Theatre/Lobby, Howl & Roar Outdoor Stage, Metro Cinema, Kinshi Rinji, Blackdog Freehouse. [F /schedule] The about page's "five days… two stages" text is stale boilerplate contradicted by the 2026 schedule and press. [F /about-grindstone vs S cfweradio.ca]

- **Ticketing**: **Showpass** (site's buy-links go to `showpass.com/s/events/all/?search_string=gcf2026`), plus in-person box office; 4-show bundle = 20% off. [F homepage, /schedule]

- **Concurrent**: overlaps Calgary Stampede (province-wide draw) and Edmonton's July festival season; Edmonton Street Performers Festival runs mid-July [S en.wikipedia.org] — not checked show-by-show. GOCF's Edmonton stop follows a week later (July 17–19). [F gocf site]

## 4a. Toronto Sketch Comedy Festival (Mar 4–15 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: registered Canadian charity (#824216808 RR 0001) founded 2005 by Toronto comedians; year-round programs (monthly cabaret, Comedy Country series, Sketch Comedy Project Fund). [F torontosketchfest.com/about, /2026-festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: annual every March since 2005 ("Toronto's longest running comedy festival"); 12 days, "dozens of shows" across 2 venues: The Theatre Centre (West Queen West) + Comedy Bar Bloor. [F homepage FAQ]
- **Show model**: curated troupe lineups, sketch/clown/musical comedy; single tickets + festival passes. Submissions process NOT FOUND this pass. [F homepage, /about]

## 4b. WHAT THE FESTIVAL! (Sept 24–27 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: tiny independent team (org est. 2022; directors Byron & Alicia per testimonials); clown/puppet/drag/burlesque "live theatre festival". [F wtfestival.ca]
- **Scale**: 3rd annual; 3 feature shows + 2 cabarets + a puppetry workshop + a talk (~8 events) over 4 days in 3 small rooms (Small World Music, Sweet Action Theatre, Social Arts Studio Space); staggered times, zero clash. New in 2026: multi-show passes ($75/3, $110/5). [F /whats-on]

## 5. Great Outdoors Comedy Festival (Vancouver stop Aug 28–30 2026) — THE STRUCTURAL CASE
- **Operator**: Trixstar LIVE / Trixstar Entertainment, an Edmonton-based promoter; footer links trixstar.com. [F greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about; S dailyhive.com]
- **The roving pattern (2026)**: 7 stops — Edmonton July 17–19 (Kinsmen Park) [S exploreedmonton.com], Winnipeg July 17–19 (Assiniboine Park) [F winnipegcomedyfestival.com homepage], Halifax Aug 6–9 (Garrison Grounds) [S exclaim.ca; S tixr.com], Calgary Aug 28–30 (Prince's Island Park), Vancouver Aug 28–30 (Stanley Park, Brockton Point), Spokane WA Aug 29–30 (One Spokane Stadium), Mississauga Sept 11–13 (Erindale Park) [F homepage]. 2027 already on sale: Edmonton + Winnipeg July 16–18, Halifax Aug 6–8. [F homepage] **Same-weekend twin stops prove parallel productions, not one touring caravan.** Past cities also include Ottawa and London ON. [F /about]
- **History/scale**: originated 2021 in Edmonton; cumulative "400,000+ attendees, 176+ performers, $800,000 community donations since 2021"; full 2021–2025 lineup archive on-site (Kevin Hart, Seinfeld, Burr, Mulaney, Schumer, Segura…). [F /about] Vancouver permit: max 10,000 guests/day at Brockton Fields (2023 Park Board filing). [F dailyhive.com]
- **Show model**: one stage per city; 2 shows/day (2:00 pm matinee + 7:30 pm evening), each a one-off bill of ~2–5 touring headliners (e.g. Vancouver: Bill Burr Fri; Jeselnik/Davidson/Holmes/Jensen Sat eve; Matt Rife Sun eve); grounds cleared between shows; explicitly **no open submissions** ("we do not have an application process"). [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Music-festival mechanics**: GA / GA+ / VIP Club / VIP Table tiers, weekend passes, BYO camping chair rules, food trucks, licensed grounds, no re-entry, 18+/19+ no minors, rain or shine, on-site cannabis in AB, 50/50 for local charities. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Ticketing**: **Tixr only** (`tixr.com/groups/gocf`) — "tickets will only be available online through Tixr"; Spokane support via TicketsWest (stadium's vendor). Not Ticketmaster. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Data reachability**: Webflow marketing site, fully server-rendered and curl-readable (cities, dates, show cards all in HTML); Tixr event pages are JS apps (Tixr exposes JSON endpoints). [F]
- **Clash reality**: none by design — one stage, sequential shows. The scheduling constraint is *which city you're in*.
- **Planner/app**: none (SMS marketing line instead). [F homepage]
- **Verdict**: the anti-fringe pole — a promoter-owned, music-festival-shaped touring/franchise comedy product (few stages, one show per act, roving cities).

## 6. Dubai Comedy Festival (Oct 9–18 2026, Dubai)
- **Organizer**: government-backed promoter consortium. BRAG (Dubai event agency): "In 2020, Brag partnered with DTCM [Dubai's tourism department] and Live Nation to bring back the Dubai Comedy Festival after a long hiatus" [F brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival]; recent editions "presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME Events and DXB Live" [S katchinternational.com]; official site footer links dubaicalendar.com and brag.ae [F dubaicomedyfest.ae].
- **Recurrence**: 7th edition (of the revived run) in 2026; grew from 4 days (2020) to 10. Annual, same city, rotating prime venues. [F /about; F brag.world]
- **Scale**: 10 days, "50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"; attendance only as "thousands of festival-goers every year". [F homepage; F brag.world]
- **Show model**: one-night (occasionally two) international touring acts — Mo Gilligan, Katherine Ryan, Zarna Garg, Vir Das, Munawar Faruqui, Jamie Lever — many "presented by" third-party promoters under the festival umbrella (AlQaiser Events, AJ Entertainment, Facepalm Comedy); deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Russian; historically also Tagalog and French). - **Venue geography**: spread across the car-scale city: Dubai Opera (Downtown), New Covent Garden Theatre (Mall of the Emirates), Coca-Cola Arena (City Walk), Pepperoni Comedy Club, Emirates Theatre (Jumeirah). Arena + theatres, not walkable. [F homepage, /about, /shows]

- **Data reachability**: Squarespace, server-rendered — the /shows page carries every show's date, venue, language, from-price and vendor links in plain HTML; easiest large-festival page to read mechanically in this whole set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: GITEX Global moved to Dec 7–11 2026 (Expo City), so no mega-event clash; October carries mid-size trade shows (WETEX Oct 20–22, Dubai AI Festival Oct 26–27). [S gitex.com, mediaoffice.ae, khaleejtimes.com]
- **Planner/app**: none of its own; Dubai Calendar and Platinumlist serve as listings layers.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a destination-marketing umbrella over one-night touring acts (with a small fringe sidebar).

## 7. Tokyo International Comedy Festival (Sept 17–27 2026, Tokyo) — brief
- **Organizer**: Tokyo Comedy Bar (Shibuya club, "home for stand-up in Japan… English & Japanese, since 2022"; operating company Stand-Up Tokyo GK), co-presented with Baird Brewing. Venue-run, commercial. [F tokyocomedybar.com/festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: 3rd edition; 11 days, "120+ shows", self-billed "East Asia's largest stand-up comedy festival"; attendance NOT FOUND. [F /festival]
- **Show model**: club-scale mix — solo shows, improv, roast battles ("Roastfest", 4th edition), live podcasts, workshops; two competitions: King of Kanto (English) and Tokyo Comedy Grand Prix (Japanese); international acts (Sammy Obeid, Emily Catalano) alongside the local Eng/JP scene. [F /festival; S tokyocheapo.com, timeout.com]
- **Venue geography**: TCB as hub plus small satellites: Mame Romantic, DecaBar Super, The Millennials Shibuya, Baird taprooms (Nakameguro, Bashamichi) — Shibuya-centred, mostly walkable/train-trivial. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Clash reality**: modest — sequential slots at the small hub with some satellite parallelism; 120 shows in 11 days implies ~11/day across ~6 tiny rooms.
- **Ticketing**: **Fienta** per show (fienta.com links on the festival page). [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: Wix; the headline facts are server-rendered but the lineup grid is client-rendered (empty via curl) — the practical machine surface is Fienta's per-event pages. [F /festlineup]
- **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-significant found; general Tokyo autumn events only. [S tokyocheapo.com]
- **Verdict**: fringe-ish energy at club scale, but curated venue-run showcase in structure.

## 8. Lucille Ball Comedy Festival (Aug 6–9 2026, Jamestown NY) — brief
- **Organizer**: the National Comedy Center — "the nation's official cultural institution dedicated to comedy" (museum + national archive) with the Lucille Ball Desi Arnaz Museum; the institution-anchored model. [F comedycenter.org/festival]
- **Recurrence**: annual since 1991 (35 years per Post-Journal), held each August around Ball's Aug 6 birthday in her hometown. [S post-journal.com]
- **Scale**: "over 50 live events, over 15,000 attendees annually from nearly every state" [F /festival]; "over 10,000 visitors" per regional press [S tourchautauqua.com/post-journal snippets].
- **Show model**: arena headliners (2026: Jerry Seinfeld Thu, Bert Kreischer Sat, Seth Meyers Sun at Northwest Arena; mainstage Stand-Up Showcase Fri) + Lucy nostalgia programming, museum talks, block parties, kids' comedy, late-night club showcases — comedy-as-heritage wrapped around touring names. [F /lbcf-2026 press release; F /festival]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Jamestown cluster — the Center, the Lucy Desi Museum, Northwest Arena, clubs; small-town walkable. [F /festival]
- **Clash reality**: real parallelism at peak (museum programs + showcases + arena) but built so the headliner slots dominate; membership presale manages demand. [F /festival]
- **Ticketing**: the Center's own system (`tickets.comedycenter.org`, Gateway-style .aspx museum ticketing); members get presale. [F /festival]
- **Data reachability**: WordPress, server-rendered and curl-friendly; ticketing system is legacy-web, no API seen; festival page currently in "see you in 2027" mode. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing found in Jamestown; coincidentally shares its exact dates with GOCF Halifax (different country/market).
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: institution-anchored destination showcase — a museum using one-night headliners to power comedy-heritage tourism.

Based on the search results, here's what happened with SF Sketchfest during the COVID-19 pandemic:

The festival was last held in February 2020, right before COVID-19 lockdowns. It was canceled in 2021. A 2022 event was briefly scheduled in 2022 before it was postponed last fall and replaced with a virtual season.

COVID-19 caused cancellation of the 2021 festival and postponement of the 2022 event until early 2023. The 20th annual SF Sketchfest was rescheduled for 2023 due to safety concerns from the COVID-19 pandemic, with new dates for the live sketch-comedy event set for Jan. 20 through Feb. 5 of that year.

On a pandemic-related hiatus since 2020, SF Sketchfest 2023 returned for Jan. 20 through Feb. 5, with each day's lineup featuring dozens shows and comics in 11 venues.

input.old_string:
# Competitor landscape

How people discover and schedule Edinburgh Fringe shows today, and how each
existing tool handles — or ignores — the two questions EdFringeNow is built
around: *"what can I actually make right now?"* (the home site, Fringe Discover)
and *"which of my favourites can I actually catch, on which dates?"* (the planner
at `/plan`). Compiled once, refined in place.

The field is not one field. The live/in-the-moment side has essentially one
incumbent; the planning side is crowded, and got noticeably more crowded for
2026.
