# Comedy festival research: Canada (non-JFL) + rest of world

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl this session; **[S]** = WebSearch snippet (attributed to its publisher). All claims carry their source inline.

**Cross-cutting findings**
- **GOCF is the confirmed music-festival-shaped contrast case** — and stronger than hypothesized: it is not even a serial tour but a *franchise running parallel city productions on shared weekends* (Edmonton + Winnipeg both July 17–19 2026; Calgary + Vancouver Aug 28–30 + Spokane Aug 29–30) [F gocf site, F wcf site].
- **CBC TV production visibly shapes the two legacy Canadian fests**: venue choice ("Mega Shows require a large venue for cameras, cast, crew" → Ticketmaster-contracted Burton Cummings Theatre) [F wcf FAQ]; content (PG rating when cameras roll; Halifax demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings due to CanCon broadcast rules) [F wcf FAQ, F hfx apply]; format (celebrity host + 6 comics per gala); and the broadcast audience (2M+ viewers) dwarfs the live one [F wcf about].
- **Ticketing vendor map**: Tixr (GOCF *and* Halifax ComedyFest), Showpass (Grindstone), Eventbrite (WTF), own Salesforce-hosted box office (TOsketchfest), 3Common + Ticketmaster split (Winnipeg), Platinumlist + per-venue boxes (Dubai), Fienta (Tokyo), own museum system (LBCF). No festival here offers an official planner app — all are "browse the schedule" sites; several sell passes/bundles instead.

---

## 1. Winnipeg Comedy Festival (Apr 20–26 2026, Winnipeg MB)
- **Organizer**: produced by the Gas Station Arts Centre (GSAC), a nonprofit arts centre in Osborne Village; festival revenue funds GSAC's year-round programming. Founded 2002 by Lara Rae and CBC Radio's Tom Anniko in partnership with GSAC. Presented by Manitoba Liquor Mart. [F https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us, /news/post/105]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 25th anniversary in 2026; 2027 dates already posted (Apr 26–May 2). [F homepage]
- **Scale**: "30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics. One city." 7 days; 7 shows sold out on launch day. Attendance not published; TV reach "over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated comedy festival series". [F /news/post/105, /about-us]
- **Show model**: one-night curated shows. Five recorded-for-broadcast "Mega Shows" at Burton Cummings Theatre (celebrity host + 6 comics, $40, filmed for CBC TV/Gem, PG); The Debaters CBC Radio taping; nightly "edgy, experimental" shows at GSAC; free noon programming (Millennium Library, Fairmont lobby); pay-what-you-can family finale. [F /news/post/105, /faqs]
- **TV shaping (the asked question)**: TV dictates the venue (big theatre for cameras → forces Ticketmaster), the rating (PG while taping, "spicy between takes"), the format (gala tapings = the flagship product), and the economics (the broadcast is the national product; the live fest is its studio audience + a local fringe around it). [F /faqs]
- **Venue geography**: 9 venues citywide — Burton Cummings Theatre (downtown), GSAC hub (Osborne Village), Good Neighbour Brewing, Jubilee Place, Fairmont lobby, Millennium Library etc.; drivable-spread, not walkable-dense. [F /faqs, /news]
- **Clash reality**: mild — Mega Shows are sequential (6:30/9:15) in one theatre while GSAC runs its own nightly slate; 2–3 parallel rooms at peak. Lineup-picking, not a clash grid. [F /news/post/105]
- **Ticketing**: split-vendor by venue: 3Common (local Winnipeg ticketer) for all shows except Ticketmaster-contracted venues (Burton Cummings). [F /faqs]
- **Data reachability**: custom server-rendered site, fully curl-readable; show listing at `/shows` with category-filter URLs (`/shows/show/search-results?category=N`). No API seen. [F]
- **Concurrent**: nothing significant that week — Tourism Winnipeg lists WCF as the anchor late-April event. [S tourismwinnipeg.com]
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a broadcaster-anchored gala festival with a small venue-run fringe attached.

## 2. Halifax ComedyFest (May 5–9 2026, Halifax NS)
- **Organizer**: CBC-sponsored (CBC tapes and broadcasts sets as TV specials) [S en.wikipedia.org]; produced/run by Premiere Entertainment Group [S halifamous.ca — sole source found]. Site self-describes as "one of only three major comedy festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a six-episode series". [F halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest]
- **Recurrence**: annual each spring since 1995 (32 years in 2027); Season 28 of the TV series is on YouTube. [F about-the-fest, homepage]
- **Scale**: "multiple shows in various venues across the city" — 2026 specifics no longer on the off-season site; NOT FOUND (site now points at 2027). [F homepage]
- **Show model**: one-night curated TV-taping showcases (2026: Opening Night Gala May 6, All Star Show May 7, both recorded for CBC TV/Gem at Light House Arts Centre) + The Debaters radio tapings; open submissions with an explicitly TV-shaped bar: "corporate clean" 8–10 min tape required, international slots "limited due to Canadian content rules for television programming". [S lighthouseartscentre.ca; S en.wikipedia.org; F /apply]
- **Venue geography**: downtown Halifax venues; historically Casino Nova Scotia's Schooner Showroom [S en.wikipedia.org], 2026 galas at Light House Arts Centre (1800 Argyle St) [S lighthouseartscentre.ca]. Walkable downtown cluster.
- **Clash reality**: minimal — roughly one taping bill per night plus club shows; lineup-picking.
- **Ticketing**: per-venue pages resolving to **Tixr** (`tixr.com/groups/hfxcomedyfest`). [F lighthouseartscentre.ca event page]
- **Data reachability**: Weebly-built static site [F — editmysite.com assets]; schedule exists only in-season, so the durable machine surface is the Tixr group. NOT FOUND: any API.
- **Concurrent**: none found in Halifax in early May. (GOCF's Halifax stop is a separate August event, same city — see below.)
- **Planner/app**: none.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — substantially a television production pipeline with a live festival wrapped around it.

## 3. Grindstone Comedy Festival (July 2–12 2026, Edmonton AB)
- **Organizer**: Grindstone Theatre Society — nonprofit founded 2012; opened the Grindstone Comedy Theatre & Bistro venue in 2018 (up to 14 independent shows/week year-round). Festival is the venue's own production (Executive/Artistic Director Byron Martin); also manages Orange Hub theatres. [F grindstonecomedyfest.com/about-grindstone]
- **Recurrence**: annual, 7th edition in 2026, same home venue. [F about; S cfweradio.ca]
- **Scale**: 11 days (July 2–12) [S cfweradio.ca, exploreedmonton.com]; ~44 scheduled events extracted from the site's schedule [F /schedule]; attendance NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: mostly one-night curated showcases (clown/sketch/improv/magic/drag/stand-up) + one-night headliners (Shaun Majumder, K. Trevor Wilson, DJ Demers, Chris Locke, Sterling Scott, Dakota Ray Hebert) + open-entry competition pipelines feeding the fest (King of the Hill improv; Stand-Up Stand-Off, 5 weekly prelim rounds → finals at the festival) + industry panel/networking + open mic. [F /schedule, /festivalinfo]
- **Venue geography**: hub-and-spokes, all Edmonton: Grindstone Comedy Theatre + Bistro/patio (hub), Orange Hub Theatre/Lobby, Howl & Roar Outdoor Stage, Metro Cinema, Kinshi Rinji, Blackdog Freehouse. [F /schedule] The about page's "five days… two stages" text is stale boilerplate contradicted by the 2026 schedule and press. [F /about-grindstone vs S cfweradio.ca]
- **Clash reality**: real but small — 2–4 rooms in play at the same hour on peak nights. [F /schedule]
- **Ticketing**: **Showpass** (site's buy-links go to `showpass.com/s/events/all/?search_string=gcf2026`), plus in-person box office; 4-show bundle = 20% off. [F homepage, /schedule]
- **Data reachability**: Wix site but the schedule text is present in served HTML (curl-extractable); Showpass has a public events API behind the search URL — the most machine-readable of the Canadian set. [F]
- **Concurrent**: overlaps Calgary Stampede (province-wide draw) and Edmonton's July festival season; Edmonton Street Performers Festival runs mid-July [S en.wikipedia.org] — not checked show-by-show. GOCF's Edmonton stop follows a week later (July 17–19). [F gocf site]
- **Planner/app**: none; a "digital program" PDF. [F /festivalinfo]
- **Verdict**: hybrid — venue-run, community/competition-fed and fringe-spirited, but curated single-tickets showcase in shape.

## 4a. Toronto Sketch Comedy Festival (Mar 4–15 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: registered Canadian charity (#824216808 RR 0001) founded 2005 by Toronto comedians; year-round programs (monthly cabaret, Comedy Country series, Sketch Comedy Project Fund). [F torontosketchfest.com/about, /2026-festival]
- **Recurrence/scale**: annual every March since 2005 ("Toronto's longest running comedy festival"); 12 days, "dozens of shows" across 2 venues: The Theatre Centre (West Queen West) + Comedy Bar Bloor. [F homepage FAQ]
- **Show model**: curated troupe lineups, sketch/clown/musical comedy; single tickets + festival passes. Submissions process NOT FOUND this pass. [F homepage, /about]
- **Ticketing/data**: own box office on a Salesforce-hosted SPA (`tosketchfest.my.salesforce-sites.com/ticket/#/` — PatronManager pattern); hash-routed JS app, not curl-readable; WordPress marketing site is. [F]
- **Clash**: two rooms, staggered slots — lineup-picking. **Concurrent**: nothing comedy-major in March; Toronto's JFL is in autumn.
- **Verdict**: showcase-like with fringe texture (multi-show pass browsing across a 12-day slate).

## 4b. WHAT THE FESTIVAL! (Sept 24–27 2026, Toronto) — brief
- **Organizer**: tiny independent team (org est. 2022; directors Byron & Alicia per testimonials); clown/puppet/drag/burlesque "live theatre festival". [F wtfestival.ca]
- **Scale**: 3rd annual; 3 feature shows + 2 cabarets + a puppetry workshop + a talk (~8 events) over 4 days in 3 small rooms (Small World Music, Sweet Action Theatre, Social Arts Studio Space); staggered times, zero clash. New in 2026: multi-show passes ($75/3, $110/5). [F /whats-on]
- **Ticketing/data**: Eventbrite per show + an Eventbrite collection; Squarespace site, fully curl-readable. [F /whats-on]
- **Concurrent — the finding**: its entire run sits inside JFL Toronto (Sept 24–Oct 3 2026, Pete Davidson/John Cleese/Tiffany Haddish) [S exclaim.ca] — a micro-festival deliberately living under a mega-festival's dates. (JFL Toronto is another agent's beat.)
- **Verdict**: micro curated showcase (closer to an indie theatre mini-fest than either pole).

## 5. Great Outdoors Comedy Festival (Vancouver stop Aug 28–30 2026) — THE STRUCTURAL CASE
- **Operator**: Trixstar LIVE / Trixstar Entertainment, an Edmonton-based promoter; footer links trixstar.com. [F greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about; S dailyhive.com]
- **The roving pattern (2026)**: 7 stops — Edmonton July 17–19 (Kinsmen Park) [S exploreedmonton.com], Winnipeg July 17–19 (Assiniboine Park) [F winnipegcomedyfestival.com homepage], Halifax Aug 6–9 (Garrison Grounds) [S exclaim.ca; S tixr.com], Calgary Aug 28–30 (Prince's Island Park), Vancouver Aug 28–30 (Stanley Park, Brockton Point), Spokane WA Aug 29–30 (One Spokane Stadium), Mississauga Sept 11–13 (Erindale Park) [F homepage]. 2027 already on sale: Edmonton + Winnipeg July 16–18, Halifax Aug 6–8. [F homepage] **Same-weekend twin stops prove parallel productions, not one touring caravan.** Past cities also include Ottawa and London ON. [F /about]
- **History/scale**: originated 2021 in Edmonton; cumulative "400,000+ attendees, 176+ performers, $800,000 community donations since 2021"; full 2021–2025 lineup archive on-site (Kevin Hart, Seinfeld, Burr, Mulaney, Schumer, Segura…). [F /about] Vancouver permit: max 10,000 guests/day at Brockton Fields (2023 Park Board filing). [F dailyhive.com]
- **Show model**: one stage per city; 2 shows/day (2:00 pm matinee + 7:30 pm evening), each a one-off bill of ~2–5 touring headliners (e.g. Vancouver: Bill Burr Fri; Jeselnik/Davidson/Holmes/Jensen Sat eve; Matt Rife Sun eve); grounds cleared between shows; explicitly **no open submissions** ("we do not have an application process"). [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]
- **Music-festival mechanics**: GA / GA+ / VIP Club / VIP Table tiers, weekend passes, BYO camping chair rules, food trucks, licensed grounds, no re-entry, 18+/19+ no minors, rain or shine, on-site cannabis in AB, 50/50 for local charities. [F /cities/vancouver, /gocf-faqs]

- **Data reachability**: Webflow marketing site, fully server-rendered and curl-readable (cities, dates, show cards all in HTML); Tixr event pages are JS apps (Tixr exposes JSON endpoints). [F]
- **Clash reality**: none by design — one stage, sequential shows. The scheduling constraint is *which city you're in*.
- **Planner/app**: none (SMS marketing line instead). [F homepage]
- **Verdict**: the anti-fringe pole — a promoter-owned, music-festival-shaped touring/franchise comedy product (few stages, one show per act, roving cities).

## 6. Dubai Comedy Festival (Oct 9–18 2026, Dubai)
- **Organizer**: government-backed promoter consortium. - **Venue geography**: spread across the car-scale city: Dubai Opera (Downtown), New Covent Garden Theatre (Mall of the Emirates), Coca-Cola Arena (City Walk), Pepperoni Comedy Club, Emirates Theatre (Jumeirah). Arena + theatres, not walkable. [F homepage, /about, /shows]

Two caveats on how strong that reads. The gallery blurbs are the only evidence —
nobody here has used these tools, and the gallery may simply be stale. And a
cross-festival tool would not necessarily be *listed* there, since the API is not
the only source. Treat "the cross-festival claim is unclaimed" as the current
best reading, not a settled finding.

## The field beyond Edinburgh (empty, and verified empty)

Researched 2026-09-01, festival by festival, for the widened product direction.
The finding is stark: **outside Edinburgh, the third-party festival-planner
category does not exist.** Searches for an Adelaide Fringe or Brighton Fringe
planner return *Edinburgh's* Plan My Fringe as the top hits; nothing third-party
was found for [Melbourne International Comedy Festival](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/2026-program-guide/)
(750+ shows), [Just For Laughs Montreal](https://www.mtl.org/en/experience/just-for-laughs-festival),
[Netflix Is A Joke](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/netflix-is-a-joke-festival-2026-lineup-schedule-los-angeles-1236478031/)
(475+ shows across 35 LA venues, per The Hollywood Reporter — and no official
app either), [SF Sketchfest](https://sfsketchfest2026.sched.com/), or SXSW's
official programme. Where planning tooling exists at all, it is official or
rented SaaS:

- **[Sched](https://sfsketchfest2026.sched.com/)** — SF Sketchfest outsources
  its schedule to a generic event-SaaS instance (personal schedules, calendar
  sync).
- **[SXSW GO](https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go)** — the official app, built on
  Eventbase; schedule building and networking, with a documented gap (no
  custom/unofficial events) that a third-party ecosystem fills only for
  *parties*, via [Do512](https://2025.do512.com/) and
  [RSVPATX](https://rsvpatx.com/rsvp-list) RSVP aggregators.
- **[Adelaide Fringe's official app](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/our-app)**
  (built by Katalyst) plus an on-site
  ["My plan" web planner](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/my-fringe/plan) —
  wishlist and sort-by-day, the closest official analogue to `/plan` found
  anywhere.
- **[Brighton Fringe's official app](https://www.dabapps.com/work/clients/brighton-fringe-app/)**
  (built by agency DabApps, buying tickets through the festival's own APIs).
- **MICF has no current official app found at all** — the only trace is a
  [2010-era iPhone app](https://itwire.com/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html).

The structural analogue where the category *is* proven: **music festivals.**
[Clashfinder](https://clashfinder.com/) is the closest cousin to what a
generalized EdFringeNow would be — free, crowdsourced lineup-clash grids for
hundreds of festivals, personal act highlighting, and **JSON, XML and iCalendar
export**; it already hosts a few tiny UK comedy events
([Exeter Comedy Festival](https://clashfinder.com/s/ecf26/),
[Cambridge Fringe](https://clashfinder.com/m/cambridgefringe2025/)) but has
no Edinburgh Fringe grid — plausibly because a 3,000-show open-access festival
exceeds what a hand-edited grid can carry. Around it sit a dozen consumer
set-time apps ([Festival Dust](https://www.festivaldust.com/),
[Headliners](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/headliners-festival-planner/id6478820193),
[Frontstage](https://www.frontstagefestivals.com/app), …), the organizer-side
platform [Woov](https://woov.com/) (600+ partner festivals, B2B), and
[Songkick's festivals directory and public API](https://www.songkick.com/developer)
— the machine-readable festival dataset comedy entirely lacks. The read for the
product: the planning-demand shape is proven at scale in music, unserved in
comedy, and first-in-category open everywhere except Edinburgh.

Based on the search results, here's information about the Boston Comedy Festival:

## Founder and History

The Boston Comedy Festival was founded by comedian Jim McCue and is stewarded by festival director Helen DiMarzio. For 25 years, the Boston Comedy Festival has been a launchpad for top stand-up talent. Jim McCue never imagined reaching such a milestone, as no one is more surprised to see the festival reach 25 years than its founder.

## Stand-Up Contest Format

The contest pits 96 rising comics from across the country for a $10,000 prize and the chance to headline at comedy clubs nationwide. The contest continues through preliminary and semifinal rounds throughout the week, until only 8 aspiring comedians remain for the BCF finals gala. The judges in the eight-round preliminaries and four-round semifinals could include a booker from a local or regional club, someone who books cruise lines or military tours, or scouts from television networks, as they each look for different things.

## Venues

The multi-venue event turns Boston, Cambridge, and Somerville into a comedy circuit, mixing star headliners with sharp new voices. It was in spaces such as The Burren, The Rockwell and the Somerville Theater in Davis Square that the festival grew in size and prestige. Beloved venues include City Winery, the Comedy Studio, the Rockwell, and the Berklee Performance Center.

Record Growth and Huge Crowds for Sydney Comedy Festival  by themovieboards - Editor  •  18/05/2026 On Sunday 17th May, the Sydney Comedy Festival wrapped for 2026 with a bang! Firmly cementing its place as one of the country’s biggest cultural events, the 2026 Festival delivered packed rooms, sold‑out outdoor festivals and a larger program, presenting 411 shows with close to 1000 performances across Sydney. In this milestone year, the Sydney Comedy Festival doubled its number of stages in partnership with Destination NSW, and now spans an impressive 57 venues across Sydney, transforming the entire city into one epic comedy playground.  “Through our work with Destination NSW, we’re playing to the strengths of this city, driving visitation into the CBD while also bringing Festival hubs to the doorsteps of our outer suburbs – from Bondi to Penrith, from Sutherland to Chatswood… and sharing stories across cultures, languages and communities. Even with the evolving fuel crisis impacting visitation and consumer confidence, the Festival is proud to have not only met, but smashed its overall attendance goals this year, welcoming more than 175,000 attendees in 2026 and seeing a stronger than ever growth in visitation” Chief Operating Officer, Sam Nardo commented. A highlight of the 2026 program was Great Laugh in the Park and Gala on the Green, two major outdoor showcases at Darling Harbour’s Tumbalong Park, where the Festival played host to sold-out crowds of more than 7,000 people.

input.body:
Closes #567

Owner-directed research pass over the comedy-festival list at https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/, making the product-wiki ready for EdFringeNow's widened direction: a festival-planning product, not an Edinburgh-only one. Scope is `product-wiki/` only (nothing under `product-requirements/`).

Landed so far:

- **competitor-landscape** — the egress block that had forced second-hand competitor reading has lifted, so all five outstanding 2026 rivals were verified first-hand: planmyfestivals.com's scope **answered** (an Edinburgh *cross-festival* planner — its bundle carries Tattoo/Book/International/Art/Jazz), FringePlan's availability question **answered** (pulls availability colours automatically), Fringe Finder's official-pilot claim verified as asserted on-page with walking-time-aware planning, Plan Your Fringe found performer-built, email-gated, promoting a previously unrecorded app (**FringePal**) and teasing live "near me now". Plus a new section for the widened direction: **outside Edinburgh, no third-party comedy-festival planner exists** — verified festival by festival; official/rented SaaS (Sched, Eventbase, Katalyst, DabApps) fills the space, and the crowded music-festival planner category (Clashfinder, Woov, Songkick's API) proves the unserved demand shape.
- **market-and-audience** — scope note: the page stays the Edinburgh evidence base; the wider market moves to the new page.

Still to land on this branch (research agents reporting):

- **comedy-festival-circuit** (new wiki page) — the 85-festival 2026 census with computed run lengths, the fringe-shaped ↔ showcase-shaped taxonomy, per-festival dossiers (organizer, recurrence, scale, show model, venues, ticketing platform, data reachability, concurrent festivals), annual-vs-one-off map, and the festival-tracker list.
- Cross-links from the wiki index and festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh.

input.new_string:
## Festival trackers

Sources that track the circuit itself — what a future multi-festival product
would use to keep a festival calendar current. The 2026-09-01 sweep's headline
is negative and load-bearing: **no machine-readable comedy-festival calendar
exists anywhere.** The best global list is one journalist's hand-maintained
page; Wikipedia has no list article at all
([the URL 404s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals)); the
UK trade press keeps gig listings, not a festival calendar. A festival
calendar for a multi-festival product would have to be assembled and
maintained by us.

- **[From The Comic's Comic — Comedy Festivals](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/)**
  — the seed list above, and the best tracker found. Kept by
  [Sean L. McCarthy](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/about-me/), a career
  comedy journalist (Boston Herald, NY Daily News, Decider reviews since
  2015), on his WordPress.com newsletter site: ~90 festivals for 2026 by
  month, one line and one link each, a stated only-if-confirmed policy, and
  email submissions from festivals (the
  [frozen pre-2024 list](https://thecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/) on his
  old domain still carries the submission address). Hand-maintained prose —
  scrapeable HTML, but unstructured. Two link defects found on the 2026-09-01
  fetch are worth knowing when reusing it: its Melbourne International Comedy
  Festival link points at the festival's stale `/2024` page, and its "Dublin
  Comedy Festival" entry links to `dublinwestcomedyfest.ie` — a different,
  smaller festival than the label suggests (untangled in the dossiers below).
- **[Chortle](https://www.chortle.co.uk/)** — the UK comedy trade site. No
  festival calendar (its `/festivals` URL 404s); what it has is the
  [Comedy Diary](https://www.chortle.co.uk/comedy-diary), a venue-submitted
  **gig-level** listings engine for the UK and Ireland in which "Edinburgh
  Fringe" is one region filter, plus per-festival show databases and heavy
  Fringe editorial. A per-show data source for UK festivals, not a circuit
  tracker.
- **[British Comedy Guide](https://www.comedy.co.uk/live/festivals/)** — a UK
  comedy festivals directory with per-festival pages, per its own indexed
  pages; the site Cloudflare-blocks non-browser fetches, so coverage depth is
  unverified here — and the block itself signals that scraping it would be
  contested.
- **[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_festival)** — no "List of
  comedy festivals" article exists; the Comedy festival article's "notable
  examples" section lists ~19 festivals, tagged unsourced since 2010, with
  obvious gaps (no Netflix Is A Joke, no New York Comedy Festival, no
  Moontower). The
  [category tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Comedy_festivals) is
  usable as a seed of notable names, useless as a calendar.
- **[World Fringe](https://worldfringe.com/)** — the fringe-network
  association's member directory (
  [Fringe A-Z](https://worldfringe.com/members/), a
  [festival calendar page](https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/), maps,
  a touring directory) — authoritative for *which fringes exist*, ~32
  countries, but fringe-network-only and effectively not machine-readable:
  both directory and calendar render client-side through a WordPress
  members plugin, so plain fetches see empty templates.
- **Submission-side and defunct**: [FilmFreeway](https://filmfreeway.com/)
  lists thousands of "comedy festivals" but they are overwhelmingly comedy
  *film* festivals and contests seeking submissions — the performer-side
  lens, not a visitor calendar; Everfest, once the big festival directory,
  [shut down in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest);
  [FestivalNet](https://festivalnet.com/) (26,000+ events) is craft-fair and
  music-vendor territory with no comedy presence.

+
+The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
+and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
+This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
+EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is

+the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data

+## Festival trackers
+

+would use to keep a festival calendar current. The 2026-09-01 sweep's headline
+is negative and load-bearing: **no machine-readable comedy-festival calendar
+exists anywhere.** The best global list is one journalist's hand-maintained
+page; Wikipedia has no list article at all
+([the URL 404s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_comedy_festivals)); the
+UK trade press keeps gig listings, not a festival calendar. A festival
+calendar for a multi-festival product would have to be assembled and
+maintained by us.

+  — the seed list above, and the best tracker found. Kept by

+  comedy journalist (Boston Herald, NY Daily News, Decider reviews since
+  2015), on his WordPress.com newsletter site: ~90 festivals for 2026 by

+  Festival link points at the festival's stale `/2024` page, and its "Dublin
+  Comedy Festival" entry links to `dublinwestcomedyfest.ie` — a different,

+  Fringe" is one region filter, plus per-festival show databases and heavy
+  Fringe editorial. A per-show data source for UK festivals, not a circuit
+  tracker.

+  comedy festivals directory with per-festival pages, per its own indexed
+  pages; the site Cloudflare-blocks non-browser fetches, so coverage depth is
+  unverified here — and the block itself signals that scraping it would be
+  contested.

+  comedy festivals" article exists; the Comedy festival article's "notable
+  examples" section lists ~19 festivals, tagged unsourced since 2010, with

+  Moontower). The
+  [category tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Comedy_festivals) is

+  association's member directory (

+  [festival calendar page](https://worldfringe.com/festival-calendar/), maps,
+  a touring directory) — authoritative for *which fringes exist*, ~32
+  countries, but fringe-network-only and effectively not machine-readable:

+  members plugin, so plain fetches see empty templates.

+  lists thousands of "comedy festivals" but they are overwhelmingly comedy

+  lens, not a visitor calendar; Everfest, once the big festival directory,
+  [shut down in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everfest);

+  music-vendor territory with no comedy presence.

+

+
+## Open questions
+
+- PLACEHOLDER-OPEN

+

input.new_string:
## The fringe-shaped tier: dossiers

PLACEHOLDER-FRINGE-TIER

## The showcase majors: dossiers

PLACEHOLDER-SHOWCASE-MAJORS

### Dubai Comedy Festival — the destination-marketing umbrella

- **Organizer**: a government-backed promoter consortium — [BRAG "partnered
  with DTCM (Dubai's tourism department) and Live Nation to bring back the
  festival" in 2020](https://brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival); recent editions
  are presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME
  Events and DXB Live (per [Katch International](https://katchinternational.com/)).
  Annual since the 2020 revival, 7th edition in 2026, grown from 4 days to 10.
- **Scale & model**: ["50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/about)
  over 10 days — one-night international touring acts (Mo Gilligan, Katherine
  Ryan, Vir Das…), many "presented by" third-party promoters under the
  festival umbrella, deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu,
  Russian), plus a small up-and-comers sidebar ("Comedy Bizarre").
- **Venues & clash**: spread across a car-scale city — Dubai Opera, Coca-Cola
  Arena, Mall of the Emirates theatre, clubs; 2–3 shows per evening across
  distant venues. Lineup-picking with traffic, not a schedule grid.
- **Ticketing & data**: per-show, multi-vendor — mostly
  [Platinumlist](https://dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net/) (which runs an
  aggregating microsite), plus venue box offices and Ticketmaster.ae for some
  shows. The [shows page](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/shows) is
  server-rendered Squarespace carrying every show's date, venue, language,
  price and vendor link in plain HTML — the easiest large-festival page to
  read mechanically in the whole census.

## The structural exhibits

Festivals that mark out the edges of the taxonomy — none is a planner market,
and each pins down one shape the census keeps producing.

### Great Outdoors Comedy Festival — the music-festival pole, confirmed

The hypothesis the census raised, confirmed and then some: GOCF is not even a
serial tour but a **franchise running parallel one-stage city productions on
shared weekends** — [seven 2026 stops](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/):
Edmonton *and* Winnipeg both 17–19 July, Calgary *and* Vancouver 28–30 August
with Spokane the same weekend, Halifax 6–9 August, Mississauga 11–13
September; 2027 dates already on sale. Owned and run by
[Trixstar](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about), an Edmonton
promoter; since 2021 it claims 400,000+ cumulative attendees. One outdoor
stage per city (Vancouver's Stanley Park permit caps at
[10,000/day](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/the-great-outdoors-comedy-festival-proposal-stanley-park)),
two shows a day (matinee + evening), each a one-off bill of touring headliners
(Bill Burr, Matt Rife, Pete Davidson tiers), grounds cleared between shows,
explicitly [no application process](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/gocf-faqs)
for performers, GA/VIP tiers, no re-entry, 18+/19+. Ticketing is
[Tixr-only](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/cities/vancouver); the
Webflow site is fully server-rendered. **Scheduling problem: none by design —
the only decision is which city you are in.** This is what "comedy festival"
means when the shape is literally a music festival's.

### The TV-taping festivals — Winnipeg and Halifax

Canada's two legacy festivals are shaped end to end by broadcast production,
and they show what a "festival" is when its real product is television:

- **[Winnipeg Comedy Festival](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us)**
  (annual since 2002, produced by the nonprofit Gas Station Arts Centre):
  ["30+ shows. 9 venues. 85 comics"](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/news/post/105)
  over 7 days, anchored by five "Mega Shows" **recorded for CBC** at the
  Burton Cummings Theatre — celebrity host + six comics, PG while cameras
  roll, in a venue chosen for camera/crew needs (which forces Ticketmaster;
  everything else sells through local ticketer 3Common, per
  [its FAQ](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/faqs)). The broadcast
  audience ("over 2 million viewers annually — CBC Television's highest-rated
  comedy festival series") dwarfs the live one. 2–3 parallel rooms at peak;
  lineup-picking.
- **[Halifax ComedyFest](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/about-the-fest.html)**
  (annual since 1995): self-described as "one of only three major comedy
  festivals broadcast nationally in prime time on CBC Television… as a
  six-episode series"; [its application page](https://www.halifaxcomedyfest.ca/apply.html)
  demands "corporate clean" audition tapes and caps international bookings
  because of Canadian-content broadcast rules — the clearest possible case of
  TV shaping the programme. Galas tape at the
  [Light House Arts Centre](https://lighthouseartscentre.ca/); ticketing via
  [Tixr](https://tixr.com/groups/hfxcomedyfest).

### The month-long touring competitions

The [San Francisco Comedy Competition](https://sanfranciscocomedycompetition.com/)
("across the Bay Area") and [Seattle International Comedy
Competition](https://seattlecomedycompetition.org/) (November, "all month
across Western Washington") are a third structure: one bill of competitors
playing a different regional venue each night for weeks. A visitor intersects
one night; there is nothing to plan.

### The institution anchor — Lucille Ball Comedy Festival

Run by the [National Comedy Center](https://comedycenter.org/festival/) (the
US comedy museum and archive) in Lucille Ball's hometown of Jamestown NY each
August since 1991: 50+ events, ~15,000 attendees, arena headliners (2026:
Seinfeld, Kreischer, Meyers) wrapped in museum programming, sold through the
museum's own ticketing. Comedy-as-heritage powering small-town destination
tourism — a shape no other census entry has.

### The club-hub festivals — Tokyo and Grindstone

The smallest recurring structure: a comedy venue programming its own
multi-week takeover. [Tokyo International Comedy Festival](https://www.tokyocomedybar.com/festival)
(3rd edition, "120+ shows" in 11 days, self-billed East Asia's largest) is run
by the Tokyo Comedy Bar club with small Shibuya satellites, ticketed per-show
on Fienta; [Grindstone Comedy Festival](https://www.grindstonecomedyfest.com/about-grindstone)
in Edmonton (7th edition, ~44 events in 11 days) is the Grindstone Theatre's
own production — one-night curated showcases plus competition pipelines,
ticketed on [Showpass](https://www.showpass.com/s/events/all/?search_string=gcf2026),
2–4 rooms at peak. Fringe-ish energy, showcase mechanics, club scale.

### The nested micro-festival

Toronto's [WHAT THE FESTIVAL!](https://www.wtfestival.ca/whats-on) (3rd
edition: ~8 clown/puppet/drag events, 3 small rooms, Eventbrite) runs its
entire 24–27 September slate **inside JFL Toronto's dates** — a
micro-festival deliberately sheltering under a mega-festival's visitor draw.
The concurrency pattern in miniature.

## 1. Melbourne International Comedy Festival (MICF)

- **Organizer**: The festival's own org (board + staff, festival-director-led); site describes itself as "one of the three largest comedy festivals in the world, alongside Edinburgh Festival Fringe and Montreal's Just for Laughs" **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/about-us/. Launched 1987 by Barry Humphries and Peter Cook; "Australia's largest ticketed cultural event" **[F]** (same page). Stability: Susan Provan AO retired in 2026 after 32 years as Festival Director (since 1994) **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/; Dylan Cole appointed new CEO/Festival Director (news item on site) **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/melbourne-international-comedy-festival-appoints-dylan-cole-as-new-ceofestival-director/. A leadership hand-over, no ownership drama. Legal-entity name/structure (Ltd vs Inc): NOT FOUND on fetched pages.
- **Recurrence**: Annual since 1987, always Melbourne, "each autumn, for three and a half weeks" centred on Melbourne Town Hall **[F]** /about-us/. 2026: 25 Mar – 19 Apr **[S]** [melbz.com.au guide](https://melbz.com.au/events/melbourne-comedy-festival-2026/); 2027 already announced: 24 Mar – 18 Apr 2027 **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/.
- **Scale (2026, DELIVERED — festival's own wrap, 16 Jul 2026)**: 796,975 attendees (+13% YoY); A$26.6M box office (+16%); **803 shows and events; 9,164 performances; 26 days**; 124 free performances; average paid ticket $38.20 **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/. Launch figure was "over 750 shows" **[S]** [melbz.com.au](https://melbz.com.au/events/melbourne-comedy-festival-2026/) — so ~50 more shows landed after launch. The site's own API still serves 826 show records for 2026 **[F]** (searchShows endpoint, below).
- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style seasons — one show = the same hour repeated across the run. Sampled from the API: runs of 7–24 performances (e.g. "26 Mar–19 Apr, 23 shows" in one room) **[F]** searchShows JSON. Previews are cheaper first-few-nights, exactly the Edinburgh pattern **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/festival-info/faqs/. Participation is **registration-based (open entry)**: "For Performers — Registering a Show; registrations… will open in early October", with independent venues found via a Venue Finder, plus an application/EOI layer for Festival Managed Venues **[F]** https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/.
- **Venue geography**: 143 venue buildings in the venues API: 66 CBD, 31 North, 29 South, 9 East, 8 West **[F]** /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues. Rooms are finer-grained than buildings (show records name rooms like "Melb Town Hall — Powder Room / Flag Room") **[F]**. Hub: Melbourne Town Hall "and surrounding precincts" **[F]** /about-us/. Walkable CBD core with a substantial suburban tail (Northcote, Box Hill etc.) **[F]** venues JSON. Largest room capacity 2,896 **[F]**.
- **Scheduling clash reality**: 9,164 performances / 26 days ≈ **~350 performances a day** **[F]** (derived from the wrap article). Genuinely fringe-like: "which of tonight's hundreds can I make" is the visitor's real problem.
- **Ticketing**: Central: comedyfestival.com.au is its own box office — the site has a full cart/basket API (`/umbraco/api/basketapi/addTickets`, `getcartsummary`, promo codes, vouchers) and account with My Tickets **[F]** (extracted from /build/app.*.js). One basket across shows. Exception: some shows at external venues link out to "the authorised ticketing provider for that event… Ticketmaster, Ticketek, Arts Centre Melbourne etc" **[F]** /festival-info/faqs/; a Ticketek MICF2026 sales page exists **[S]** [premier.ticketek.com.au](https://premier.ticketek.com.au/shows/show.aspx?sh=MICF2026). Underlying ticketing engine behind the basket: NOT FOUND (no vendor strings in the JS). Booking-fee amounts: NOT FOUND on the FAQ page.
- **Data reachability**: **Best-in-set. Named JSON endpoints, no auth**: `POST https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/umbraco/api/searchapi/searchShows` (body `{"query":"","page":1}`) returns paged JSON — 826 items, 42 pages, with show name, run dates, performance count, venue rooms, image URLs **[F]**; `GET /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues` returns all 143 venues with address, suburb, capacity, accessibility flags **[F]**. Each show page embeds a `sessionData = [...]` JSON array: per-performance sessionId, date, time, status ("On Sale"), preview/tightArse/soldout/cancelled flags **[F]** e.g. https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/browse-shows/the-cave/. Sitemap lists all 827 show URLs **[F]** /sitemap.xml. CMS is Umbraco (.NET) **[F]**. A scrape would target searchShows + per-show sessionData.
- **Concurrent festivals**: Melbourne Food & Wine Festival and the Melbourne International Flower & Garden Show (25–29 Mar 2026) overlap, and the AFL season (from early March, MCG/Marvel) runs throughout **[S]** [melbournetourism.org calendar](https://www.melbournetourism.org/melbourne-events-and-festivals-calendar/), [discovermelbourne.au](https://discovermelbourne.au/events/annual-festivals/).
- **Official planner/app**: The site itself is the planner — native account **Favourites** (`favouritesApi/ModifyShowInFavourites`, `ModifyPerformanceInFavourites`, share-favourites URL endpoint) **[F]** app JS. A dedicated official iPhone planning app existed in 2010 **[S]** [iTWire](https://itwire.com/reviews-sp-288/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html); no evidence of a current (2025/26) standalone app — NOT FOUND. Third-party planners: none found.

## 2. Sydney Comedy Festival

- **Organizer**: **Century Entertainment / Century Venues** — "the producing company for the Sydney & Perth Comedy Festivals", launched Sydney in 2005 **[S]** [century.com.au](https://www.century.com.au/about/). Century is a commercial venue operator (Enmore Theatre, Metro Theatre, The Comedy Store, Factory Theatre, The Concourse…) **[S]** same page. The festival site is a WordPress multisite on `corewp.century.com.au` **[F]** (asset URLs on event pages). So: promoter/venue-group-run, not a nonprofit. Stable — 21 editions since 2005 **[F]** https://www.sydneycomedyfest.com.au/about/.
- **Recurrence**: Annual, "every April and May", Sydney; followed by a national **Showcase Tour May–December** (regional one-nighters continuing into 2026-27 right now) **[F]** /about/ and event listings.
- **Scale (2026)**: DELIVERED (festival wrap, 18 May 2026): **411 shows, close to 1,000 performances, 57 venues, 175,000+ attendees**; venue count doubled this year via a Destination NSW partnership; two 7,000-person outdoor galas at Tumbalong Park **[F]** https://www.themovieboards.net/2026/05/18/record-growth-and-huge-crowds-for-sydney-comedy-festival/ (festival press-release text; COO Sam Nardo quoted). LAUNCH figure was "more than 400 shows" **[S]** [Destination NSW newsroom](https://www.destinationnsw.com.au/newsroom/sydney-comedy-festival-unveils-2026-lineup). Run 13 Apr – 17 May 2026 (≈35 days) **[S]** [eventsinsydney.com](https://www.eventsinsydney.com/things-to-do/sydney-comedy-festival/).
- **Show model**: Mixed, tilting showcase: 411 shows ÷ ~1,000 performances ≈ **2.4 performances per show** (derived from the wrap **[F]**) — mostly short seasons (a weekend at one venue) plus galas/showcases, vs MICF's 11.4. Curated: **application-based** — "Applications for the 2026 Sydney Comedy Festival are now closed… all will be reviewed and responded to" **[F]** https://www.sydneycomedyfest.com.au/artist-applications-2/.
- **Venue geography**: 57 venues spread citywide — hubs "from Bondi to Penrith, from Sutherland to Chatswood" **[F]** wrap article; core is Century's Enmore Theatre (Newtown) + Factory Theatre (Marrickville) + Comedy Store, with galas at Sydney Opera House, The Concourse Chatswood, Riverside Parramatta etc. **[F]** /about/ + **[S]** [Destination NSW](https://www.destinationnsw.com.au/newsroom/sydney-comedy-festival-unveils-2026-lineup). Not a walkable core — a metro-area constellation.
- **Scheduling clash reality**: ~1,000 performances / 35 days ≈ ~29/day average, weekend-weighted across 57 scattered venues — parallel choice exists but is an order of magnitude below MICF; picking a venue hub first is the visitor's real move.
- **Ticketing**: **Per-venue, no central basket.** The festival site lists shows; each show's BUY button deep-links to that venue's seller — Century venues sell on **TicketSearch** (`https://AUCENTURY.sales.ticketsearch.com/sales/salesevent/…`) **[F]** event page for "Daniel Connell — Encore"; tour/other venues use their own (e.g. Cairns council's TicketLINK) **[F]** showcase-tour-cairns event page. FAQ: buy online at sydneycomedyfest.com.au or at venue box offices **[F]** /faqs/. Booking fees: NOT FOUND.
- **Data reachability**: Server-rendered WordPress; events at `/event/<slug>/` with session date/time in the HTML (`<ul class='sessions'>` + `btn-buy` href) **[F]**; listing filterable by query params (`/?s=&event_date=&venue=…`) **[F]**. The `event` custom post type is **not** exposed in the WP REST API (`/wp-json/wp/v2/types` lists only standard types) **[F]**. A scrape would target the HTML listing + event pages.
- **Concurrent festivals**: Sydney Royal Easter Show 2–13 Apr 2026; Sydney Writers' Festival within the window; Vivid Sydney starts 22 May (just after) **[S]** [sydneyexpert.com April](https://sydneyexpert.com/sydney-in-april/), [May](https://sydneyexpert.com/sydney-in-may/), [sydneytravelguide.com.au Vivid](https://www.sydneytravelguide.com.au/vivid-sydney-guide-dates-lights-walk-events-tips/).
- **Official planner/app**: None found. Site has only a "My Recent Events" recently-viewed widget **[F]** (site template). NOT FOUND for favourites/app; no third-party planners found.

## 3. New Zealand International Comedy Festival (NZICF)

- **Organizer**: **The New Zealand Comedy Trust** — "a not-for-profit charitable organisation", running the festival "since 1995" **[F]** https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/the-new-zealand-comedy-trust/; the festival itself started 1993 at Auckland's Watershed Theatre as "three weeks of open slather comedy" **[F]** https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/new-zealand-international-comedy-festival/. Stable; 2026 was the 33rd Auckland edition **[F]** (launch news, below).
- **Recurrence**: Annual, every May, always **Auckland + Wellington** (2026: plus "a cheeky Gala toe-dip in Christchurch") **[F]** https://comedyfestival.co.nz/news-feed/be-in-on-the-laughs-this-may-at-the-2026-nz-international-comedy-festival-with-best-foods-mayo/. 2026: 1–24 May (24 days) **[F]** same page. Wellington leg marked 30 years in 2026 **[F]** same page.
- **The two-city model**: One festival window, one programme, region-filtered — the site's nav and show search split **Auckland | Wellington | Rest of NZ** **[F]** homepage/find-a-show. Both cities run simultaneously (not sequential legs); each city has its own venue set (Auckland: Q Theatre, Basement, The Classic, Covert, plus Aotea Centre/Town Hall/Civic/Bruce Mason for headliners **[S]** [aucklandnz.com](https://www.aucklandnz.com/events/all-events/nz-intl-comedy-festival-2026); Wellington: BATS (3 rooms), Te Auaha, Hannah Playhouse, Cavern Club, Fringe Bar **[F]** /venues/ + **[S]** [wellington.scoop.co.nz](https://wellington.scoop.co.nz/?p=178242)). Some acts play both cities in sequence within the window (e.g. STAMPTOWN "hits Q Theatre before tearing into The Hannah in Wellington"), others one city only **[S]** [wellington.scoop.co.nz](https://wellington.scoop.co.nz/?p=178242).
- **Scale**: Trust's own steady-state description: "over 120 show seasons, over 600 performances, around 200 comedians"; 2025 attendance 75,000+ **[F]** /about-us/new-zealand-international-comedy-festival/. 2026 LAUNCH: "more than 150 [artists]… across more than 550 performances" **[F]** launch news. (Wikipedia says "over 200 shows… total attendance of over 100,000" — older/looser figures **[F]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_International_Comedy_Festival.) 2026 DELIVERED totals: NOT FOUND (no wrap release located).
- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style **"show seasons"** (the Trust's own term) — short runs, ~5 performances per show on the averages above **[F]** /about-us/. Participation: "Apply to perform" routes to a performer/producer account registration portal (`/account/register`, "Producers Hub") **[F]** site nav/footer — registration-flavoured like a fringe, but whether anything is refused (open-access vs vetted): NOT FOUND.

No JSON API found. A scrape would target the find-a-show HTML per region + show pages (which link out per-agent for tickets).
- **Concurrent festivals**: May in Auckland is congested: NZ Music Month (all month) + Auckland Writers Festival (12–17 May 2026, 220+ artists/170+ events) + NZICF — The Spinoff: "Auckland has a problem. Everything awesome is happening in May, all at once" **[S]** [thespinoff.co.nz](https://thespinoff.co.nz/pop-culture/06-05-2026/auckland-has-a-problem-everything-awesome-is-happening-in-may-all-at-once).
- **Official planner/app**: "View calendar / Download calendar" — a downloadable timetable PDF (e.g. `AKL-Timetable-220426.pdf`) **[F]** homepage. No favourites, no app found — NOT FOUND; no third-party planners found.

## 4. Adelaide Fringe (targeted questions only)

- **(a) Ticketing platform**: **FringeTIX — Adelaide Fringe's own system**, first used 1998 ("its own especially developed ticketing system") **[F]** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_Fringe. Today it is not a separate vendor product but the adelaidefringe.com.au site itself: a Rails/Hotwire app (Turbo frames, Stimulus controllers namespaced `fringetix/*`, CloudFront release assets) with a **central cart** (`cart--header` turbo-frame) and a "My Fringe" account (`/my-fringe/sign-in`) **[F]** https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringetix — i.e., one basket across all shows/venues, festival-run. Bonus: the org markets its own platform, **AVR** — "the best solution for collating and managing open access festivals and events" — to other festivals **[F]** https://adelaidefringe.com.au/about-us (footer).

- Exists and is distinct from FRINGE WORLD: "Perth's biggest annual comedy event. Every April and May" **[F]** https://www.perthcomedyfestival.com/about/. Run by **Century Entertainment** (same producer as Sydney — "the producing company for the Sydney & Perth Comedy Festivals" **[S]** [century.com.au](https://www.century.com.au/about/)); the site is the same Century WordPress template as Sydney's (identical genre taxonomy, "My Recent Events" widget) **[F]** homepage/about. - 2026: 20 Apr – 17 May, "4 weeks. 5 venues. Over 70 gigs" — Regal Theatre, Astor Theatre, Freo Social, The Rechabite, State Theatre Centre of WA **[S]** [Broadsheet](https://www.broadsheet.com.au/perth/event/perth-comedy-festival-2026). ## Verdicts: fringe-like ↔ showcase-like

| Festival | Verdict | Deciding facts |
|---|---|---|
| **MICF** | **Fully fringe-like** (Edinburgh's closest southern analogue) | 803 shows × avg ~11 perfs each over 26 days (~350/day); open show registration; central one-basket box office with per-performance preview/cheap-night flags |
| **Sydney** | **Hybrid, showcase-leaning** | Curated by application; 411 shows but only ~2.4 perfs/show; per-venue ticketing (TicketSearch et al.), venues scattered Bondi→Penrith |
| **NZICF** | **Small fringe-like, split across two cities** | Trust's own "120+ show seasons" language, ~5 perfs/season; but multi-agent per-venue ticketing and ~12–15 parallel shows per city per night |
| **Adelaide Fringe** | **Fully fringe-like** (already in wiki; ticketing angle new) | Open access, 1,500+ shows, and — unlike every other AU festival here — a festival-owned central-basket platform (FringeTIX/AVR) like Edinburgh's |
| **Perth** | **Fully showcase-like** | 5 venues, ~70 gigs in 4 weeks (2–3/night), promoter-curated touring acts |

**Cross-cutting notes for the product**: (1) MICF is the standout scrape target — an unauthenticated JSON search API, a venues API with capacities, and per-show embedded session JSON with sold-out/preview/cheap-Tuesday flags that map almost 1:1 onto EdFringeNow's data model. (2) The two Century festivals (Sydney, Perth) share one WP codebase — one adapter would cover both. (3) Only MICF and Adelaide have central baskets; NZ and Sydney hand visitors to per-venue sellers, which makes a cross-show planner *more* valuable there, not less.

## Verdicts: fringe-like ↔ showcase-like

| Festival | Verdict | Deciding facts |
|---|---|---|
| **MICF** | **Fully fringe-like** (Edinburgh's closest southern analogue) | 803 shows × avg ~11 perfs each over 26 days (~350/day); open show registration; central one-basket box office with per-performance preview/cheap-night flags |
| **Sydney** | **Hybrid, showcase-leaning** | Curated by application; 411 shows but only ~2.4 perfs/show; per-venue ticketing (TicketSearch et al.), venues scattered Bondi→Penrith |
| **NZICF** | **Small fringe-like, split across two cities** | Trust's own "120+ show seasons" language, ~5 perfs/season; but multi-agent per-venue ticketing and ~12–15 parallel shows per city per night |
| **Adelaide Fringe** | **Fully fringe-like** (already in wiki; ticketing angle new) | Open access, 1,500+ shows, and — unlike every other AU festival here — a festival-owned central-basket platform (FringeTIX/AVR) like Edinburgh's |
| **Perth** | **Fully showcase-like** | 5 venues, ~70 gigs in 4 weeks (2–3/night), promoter-curated touring acts |

**Cross-cutting notes for the product**: (1) MICF is the standout scrape target — an unauthenticated JSON search API, a venues API with capacities, and per-show embedded session JSON with sold-out/preview/cheap-Tuesday flags that map almost 1:1 onto EdFringeNow's data model. (2) The two Century festivals (Sydney, Perth) share one WP codebase — one adapter would cover both. (3) Only MICF and Adelaide have central baskets; NZ and Sydney hand visitors to per-venue sellers, which makes a cross-show planner *more* valuable there, not less.

# US Majors — Comedy Festival Research Dossiers

**Evidence key:** *(fetched)* = page retrieved by curl/WebFetch and read directly; *(snippet)* = WebSearch result attributed to its publisher. Today = 2026-09-01.

## Cross-festival findings (the headlines)

- **No US major is fringe-shaped.** Every festival here is one-night curated events, not repeated runs. The fringe-like elements that do exist are partial: Moontower's badge club-binge, DCM's marathon badge, Skankfest's compound pass.
- **November is the US comedy-festival pile-up**: NYCF (Nov 6–15), 312 Chicago (Nov 5–15), Boston (Nov 10–14), Skankfest New Orleans (Nov 13–15) all overlap in 2026 — different cities, same touring headliners circulating.
- **Central discovery, fragmented purchase is the US norm**: even corporate-run Netflix Is A Joke routes its 498 listed events to 12+ different ticket vendors (counted from its own schedule payload, fetched).
- **Netflix Is A Joke is biennial, not annual** — 2022, 2024, 2026; no 2023 or 2025 edition (Wikipedia; the prompt's "2025 edition" premise is wrong — netflixisajoke2025.com is a third-party resale SEO site).
- **Data reachability is generally good**: 4 of the 5 majors serve server-rendered HTML with structured data (Netflix inlines its full event dataset; NYCF exposes a live WordPress REST API). SF Sketchfest is the exception (captcha-walled).

---

## 1. SF Sketchfest — San Francisco, Jan 15–Feb 1 2026

- **Organizer**: Independent — founded 2001 by David Owen, Cole Stratton and Janet Varney as a showcase for six Bay Area sketch groups; same founders still run it (snippet: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SF_Sketchfest, podnews.net press release). Stability: 23 editions across 25 years.
- **Recurrence**: Annual in SF each Jan/Feb since 2002, with a COVID gap: last pre-pandemic edition Feb 2020; 2021 canceled; Jan 2022 postponed for Omicron; returned Jan 20–Feb 5 2023 as the 20th annual (snippets: sfgate.com, ktvu.com, localnewsmatters.org). 2026 = 23rd edition (snippet: deadline.com).
- **Scale**: 200+ shows, 500+ performers, 13 venues, 18 days (Jan 15–Feb 1) (snippets: deadline.com, brooklynvegan.com, sfchronicle.com). Attendance: NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: One-night curated specials — reunions and tributes that structurally can't repeat (Kids in the Hall *Brain Candy* 30th anniversary, "The Women of SNL", Futurama Live, a Nickelodeon *Doug* 35th reunion), plus stand-up, podcasts, improv (snippet: brooklynvegan.com). Curated, not open-submission. NOT FOUND: any repeated-run programming.
- **Venue geography**: 13 venues spread across San Francisco — Cobb's (North Beach), Punch Line (FiDi), Great American Music Hall (Tenderloin), Sydney Goldstein Theater (Civic Center area) (snippet: brooklynvegan.com). A transit/rideshare spread, not one walkable cluster — but SF is compact vs LA.
- **Clash reality**: ~200 shows / 18 days ≈ 11/day average — clashes exist on weekends but it's mostly a pick-your-events problem; the one-off reunion format makes each clash unresolvable (no second chance).
- **Ticketing**: Single tickets per show via **Eventbrite** — official SF Sketchfest organizer account, "124 upcoming events" at announcement time (snippet: eventbrite.com/o/sf-sketchfest-57967098043; organizer page itself fetched, 200, but events are client-loaded — JSON-LD carries only Organization/ProfilePage). No badge/pass found.
- **Data reachability**: **sfsketchfest.com is curl-hostile** — SiteGround captcha (`sg-captcha: challenge`, HTTP 202 meta-refresh to `/.well-known/sgcaptcha/`) on every path incl. sitemap.xml (fetched); WebFetch also returns empty. Schedule lives on **Sched**: sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — 403 to curl too (Cloudflare). Practical path: Eventbrite organizer listing.
- **Concurrent festivals**: None found in the Jan window.
- **Official planner**: Sched instance (sfsketchfest2026.sched.com) — Sched provides per-user agendas/sync; a yearly instance exists (2023 one confirmed via snippet).
- **Verdict**: **Showcase-like at fringe breadth** — 200+ shows over 18 days but every one a curated one-off with per-show Eventbrite tickets; nothing runs twice, nothing is open-entry.

## 2. Netflix Is A Joke Fest — Los Angeles, May 4–10 2026

- **Organizer**: Netflix (corporate); promoted with Live Nation involvement historically. Produced by Netflix per Wikipedia (snippet).
- **Recurrence**: **Biennial** — announced for spring 2020, canceled for COVID (snippet: hollywoodreporter.com); debut Apr–May 2022; editions 2022, 2024, 2026; **no 2023 or 2025 edition** (snippet: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Is_a_Joke_Festival). 2026 edition confirmed delivered — ran May 4–10 (snippet: netflix.com/tudum "2026 Is Underway"). Growth: 130 comedians/25 venues (2022) → "500+ shows" 2024 (snippets: Wikipedia, variety.com) → 2026 below. 2022 reportedly sold 260,000+ tickets (snippet, origin claim Netflix).
- **Scale**: Official meta description (fetched): "**475+ Shows 500+ artists 45+ venues May 4-10. The largest comedy event in history**". The site's own schedule payload carries **498 dated events referencing 116 distinct venue slugs** (fetched, counted); press said 35 venues / 350+ events at January announcement (snippets: hollywoodreporter.com, timeout.com) — the count grew to fest time; "45+" is the official venue figure, 116 includes rooms/pop-ups.
- **Show model**: One-night showcases, galas, arena/amphitheater headliners (Hollywood Bowl, Greek Theatre, Intuit Dome), live podcast tapings, table reads, live tapings of Netflix specials (fetched meta + snippet: hollywoodreporter.com). Curated; no submissions. Some comedians play multiple nights/venues, but as distinct events, not runs.

- **Show model**: Headliner one-nighters at theatres (Ziwe, Marc Maron, Daniel Sloss; Stand Up for Heroes 20th-anniversary gala with Springsteen/Stewart at David Geffen Hall) + club showcases; some tours do 2 nights (Ms. Pat, Jess Hilarious ×2–4, fetched homepage/sitemap). **Open submissions exist** for three curated showcase slots: The Breakouts, Creators to Watch, New York's Funniest Stand-Ups (deadline Sep 16; fetched submissions page).
- **Venue geography**: 39 venues in the venue sitemap (fetched) — Beacon Theatre, Town Hall, David Geffen Hall, Kings Theatre (Brooklyn), Tribeca PAC, Hard Rock's Venue on Music Row, plus ~30 comedy clubs from Harlem to Astoria (QED) to Bushwick (Tiny Cupboard). "All five boroughs" claimed (FAQ, fetched); the sitemap's borough taxonomy lists only Manhattan as a populated archive (fetched). Subway-linked spread, not walkable as one cluster.
- **Clash reality**: 150+ shows / 10 days ≈ 15/day, mostly evening-stacked — a real same-night choice problem on weekends, but marquee-driven: fans buy their headliner, clubs absorb the rest.
- **Ticketing**: No central platform — homepage Buy Tickets links go per-venue (fetched): Ticketmaster (12 distinct events counted), ATG Tickets (Kings Theatre), Tribeca PAC's own system; club shows on club systems. No badge/pass found.
- **Data reachability**: Good — WordPress, server-rendered; sitemaps enumerate lineup (204 URLs), venues (39), boroughs (fetched); **live REST API**: `/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup?per_page=2` returns 200 with JSON (fetched). Scrapable without a browser.
- **Concurrent festivals**: 312 (Chicago) and Boston overlap the same week; within NYC itself nothing found.
- **Official planner/app**: None found — website lineup + venue pages only.
- **Verdict**: **Showcase-like** — a curated headliner umbrella over per-venue ticketing; the deciding facts are one-night theatre bills on Ticketmaster/ATG/house systems and no pass, with submissions confined to three contest-style showcases.

## 4. Moontower Comedy Festival — Austin, Apr 8–19 2026

- **Organizer**: Nonprofit venue — "produced by the Paramount Theatre" (official site, fetched); the Paramount & State Theatres are run by the Austin Theatre Alliance. Stable: 2026 = 14th year (snippet: kxan.com), founded 2012.
- **Recurrence**: Annual each April in downtown Austin; ran through COVID era with disruptions (not detailed on-page). 2026: Apr 8–19 full window (snippet: do512.com; official page confirms "TWO-WEEK... every April", fetched), with the **4-day Club Binge Apr 15–18** (official FAQ, fetched).
- **Scale**: "Over 150 of the world's top and emerging comedians"; Club Binge: "Over 100 comedians... at 10+ walkable comedy clubs" (official, fetched). Show count and attendance: NOT FOUND (likely 100+ club shows; not published as a number).
- **Show model**: Two-tier: (a) headliner one-nighters across two weeks at Paramount/State (single tickets); (b) 4-day badge-driven club programming — curated showcases ("New York's Finest", "Cheers Queers", "The Internationals"), podcasts, one-person shows, nightly parties (FAQ, fetched). Club comedians play multiple showcase slots across the binge. Curated; no public submissions found.
- **Venue geography**: The walkable exception — Paramount, State, Antone's, The Creek & The Cave, Velveeta Room, Higbies, Sunset Strip, Rozco's, Vulcan Gas Company, Fallout Theater, all downtown; one outlier, Cap City Comedy Club at The Domain (~10 mi north, needs pre-requested tickets) (FAQ, fetched).
- **Clash reality**: During the binge, 10+ rooms run simultaneously nightly — genuinely fringe-like grazing: badge-holders walk in anywhere, "No tickets or reservations necessary" (FAQ, fetched). Room-capacity risk replaces ticket clashes.
- **Ticketing**: The hybrid that matters: **badge** (club binge all-access + headliner presale priority) + **single tickets** for theatres; **daily wristbands**; club single tickets sold but "do not guarantee entry — badges and wristbands [may] fill a venue, resulting in... refunds" (FAQ, fetched). Platform: **Tessitura** on the venue's own tickets.austintheatre.org (fingerprinted in page source, fetched). Badge prices: NOT FOUND (page shows "see you next year"; a "Full Moon Badge" tier existed, page now 404, fetched).
- **Data reachability**: Good — WordPress (wp-json present) with server-rendered pages: /moontower-comedy/comics/, /theatreschedule/, /faq/ (all curl-clean, fetched); event detail on Tessitura pages, server-rendered (fetched a sample). No public JSON API identified beyond standard wp-json.
- **Concurrent festivals**: Nothing in Austin in April (SXSW is March); note the Nashville fest runs the near-identical Apr 9–19 window in 2026 — competing for the same touring headliners, not the same audience.
- **Official planner/app**: NOT FOUND for 2026 — schedule pages + daily fest emails with "programmer picks" (FAQ, fetched). (Historical Moontower apps existed; nothing current found.)
- **Verdict**: **The closest thing to a fringe in the US majors — but only its badge half**: turn-up-and-graze entry at 10+ walkable downtown clubs with no reservations is fringe mechanics; the two-week headliner layer on Tessitura single tickets is a standard showcase series.

## 5. SXSW Comedy — Austin, Mar 13–16 2026 (within SXSW Mar 12–18)

- **Organizer**: SXSW, LLC (corporate; majority-owned by Penske Media since 2021 — background knowledge, unverified here). Comedy track "since 2008 — 20 years" (official page, fetched).
- **Recurrence**: Annual within SXSW; 19th edition in 2026 (snippet: deadline.com). 2027 already scheduled: comedy Mar 17–20 within SXSW Mar 15–21 (official page, fetched).
- **Scale**: Tiny inside the giant — official 2027 stats block (fetched): "**4 Nights, 2 Venues, 65+ Performers, 30 Shows, 6 Types of showcases**". 2026 matched the shape: The Creek and The Cave + Esther's Follies (snippet: deadline.com).
- **Show model**: Curated showcases fronted by club brands (The Stand, Gotham, Cracked Comedy Club showcases), stand-up, improv, game shows, podcast tapings; alumni pipeline framing (Schumer 2011, Nanjiani 2013, Kroll 2017) (fetched page + deadline.com snippet). No open submissions for comedy (PanelPicker is for conference sessions).
- **Venue geography**: 2 venues, downtown Austin; SXSW's own FAQ: "Once you are downtown, most everything is within walking, pedicab or shuttle distance" (fetched).
- **Clash reality**: Comedy barely clashes with itself (2 rooms) — it clashes with **everything else at SXSW**: film premieres, 1,000+ music showcases, conference tracks, all on one credential. The purest "the city is the draw" case: comedy is a track you graze between other festivals.
- **Ticketing**: Badge-only access — comedy is included for all badge holders ("Open to all badge holders", fetched); 2027 badge tiers: Platinum $1,395 / Innovation $895 / Film & TV $775 / Music $550 (fetched). Exceptions exist (2026 Dropout Improv show: Platinum badges + separately sold tickets, snippet: deadline.com). No per-show tickets otherwise; secondary single-ticket sales are not the model.
- **Data reachability**: schedule.sxsw.com is a client-rendered SPA (Vite/JS bundle; shell HTML only, fetched) — no public JSON endpoint identified without executing JS; sxsw.com marketing pages are server-rendered and curl-clean (fetched). sitemap.xml present (fetched).
- **Concurrent festivals**: SXSW *is* the case study — Interactive + Film & TV + Music + Comedy under one badge, one week, one downtown.
- **Official planner/app**: **SXSW GO** — the flagship of festival schedule builders: browse the full lineup, star "My Favorites", sync across devices, toggle full schedule vs My Schedule, badge upload, attendee networking; iOS + Android (developer: Xomo Digital), paired with the schedule.sxsw.com web planner (official sxsw.com/mobile + app-store listings, snippets).
- **Verdict**: **Badge-showcase hybrid where the badge buys the city, not the comedy** — 30 curated shows in 2 walkable venues inside a 4-figure-badge multi-festival; the deciding facts are "open to all badge holders" access and a 2-venue footprint dwarfed by its host.

# Just For Laughs (JFL) empire — research report (2026-09-01)

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl/WebFetch and read directly; **[S]** = search-snippet evidence (not opened; attribute to the named publisher). All dates below verified against at least one tagged source.

## 1. Ownership story — who owns JFL and how stable is it

Timeline:

- **1983** — first Montreal festival; founded by Gilbert Rozon; grew into "the world's largest comedy festival" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **2017–2018** — Rozon (majority stakeholder) resigns amid sexual-misconduct allegations; company put up for sale. **Mar–Jun 2018**: Howie Mandel + ICM Partners, joined by Bell Media and Groupe CH (owner of evenko/L'Équipe Spectra/Bell Centre), acquire Groupe Juste pour rire (https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-and-groupe-ch-join-howie-mandel-and-icm-partners-in-just-for-laughs-ownership-group/ [S], https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/bell-media-just-for-laughs-1.4697493 [S]).
- **Mar 5, 2024** — Groupe Juste pour rire files for creditor protection; the 2024 Montreal **and Toronto** festivals are cancelled outright. Blamed: COVID revenue losses, inflation, shrinking network/streamer spending. Later revealed: **$22.5M in debt plus $3.4M owed to creditors**, and **$800K lost to an email-phishing scheme in 2023** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F], citing CBC; https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **May 29 – Jun 2024** — **ComediHa!** (Quebec City entertainment group founded 1997 by Sylvain Parent-Bédard) acquires the assets — brands Juste pour rire, Just For Laughs, ZooFest, ComedyPro, the Gags, and the audiovisual catalogue — with Quebec Superior Court endorsement (https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/comediha-acquires-assets-of-just-for-laughs-811817974.html [S], https://playbackonline.ca/2024/05/30/comediha-to-acquire-select-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **Since then** — the parent group has been renamed **Groupe Juste pour divertir**, HQ in Quebec City; site footers read "©2026 Juste Pour Divertir" (https://www.hahaha.com/fr/public/le-groupe/a-propos-377/ [F]; rename reported by https://sorstu.ca/le-comediha-fest-quebec-devient-le-festival-juste-pour-rire-quebec/ [S]). ComediHa!'s own 25-year-old Quebec City festival was folded into the JPR brand (see Quebec City below); Parent-Bédard keeps ComediHa! as the TV/scripted brand (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **Summer 2024** — no Montreal festival, but ComediHa staged a stopgap outdoor event, "ComediHa! salue Montréal", with JFL-branded events at Place des Festivals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]). Satellites restarted first (Sydney, Bermuda, Vancouver) (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-comedy-festival-return-australia-bermuda-bankruptcy-1235980376/ [S]).
- **2025 Montreal** — comeback edition **Jul 16–27, 2025** (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-returns-2025-1236069413/ [S]). Wikipedia describes it as smaller and "without the usual televised galas" [F]; Montreal Rocks reports gala tapings returned with hosts Fortune Feimster, Roy Wood Jr., Michelle Buteau, Mikey Day (https://montrealrocks.ca/just-for-laughs-returns-with-its-2025-lineup/ [S]) — a "Fortune Feimster Gala" photo from 2025 appears in The Main's 2026 guide (https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide [F]). Official wrap claim: total budget "more than $45 million invested in culture and the economy", sold-out venues, across Montreal + Quebec City (https://quebec.hahaha.com/page/detail/news/juste-pour-rire--just-for-laughs-quebec--announces-2026-festival-dates-74/ [F]).
- **2026 Montreal** — **44th edition, Jul 15–26, back "at full volume": 250 shows, 25 venues, 800+ artists** (The Main [F]) — full detail in §3.

**Stability verdict:** the brand survived receivership intact and is past the danger zone: a full-scale 2026 Montreal edition ran, the 2026 dates were announced a year ahead by press release [F], government partners are visible (Loto-Québec collaboration, Canada/Québec/City-of-Montreal messages on the official site [F]), and 2027 satellite dates are already published (Bermuda Feb 17–20, 2027 [F]; Namur Mar 15–21, 2027 [F]). It is now a regional-champion-owned company (Quebec City, private) rather than a media-conglomerate portfolio piece. Treat Montreal as a durable annual anchor again, with one caveat: the owner is 2 years into the turnaround and audited attendance/scale figures are its own marketing claims.
