## 3. Montreal flagship dossier

**Scale & shape (2026, 44th edition, Jul 15–26 — 12 days):** ~250 ticketed shows across ~25 downtown venues, "hundreds" of free outdoor performances, 800+ artists in both official languages (The Main [F]); Place des Arts' page claims ~1,700 artists from 19 countries and "nearly two million visitors" (https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival [F] — marketing copy; the 2M figure includes free outdoor crowds). Jerry Seinfeld added to the 2026 edition (https://deadline.com/2026/05/just-for-laughs-new-shows-jerry-seinfeld-2026-edition-1236882104/ [S]).

**The model — three tiers [all F: The Main, Cult MTL, Place des Arts]:**
1. **Galas**: TV-taping showcase galas at Théâtre Maisonneuve (Place des Arts), host + curated lineup — the festival's signature product.
2. **Ticketed indoor shows**: mostly **curated multi-night showcase runs**, not fringe runs — e.g. The Culture Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19, 7pm), The Nasty Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19+21, 9:30pm), Brit(ish) (Le Gesù, Jul 21–25), Midnight Surprise (Studio TD, Jul 22–25, midnight), plus premium one-offs (An Evening with David Letterman + Will Arnett, Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, Jul 21, $148–$550) (Cult MTL [F]). Typical run: 1–5 nights.
3. **Free outdoor**: Place des Festivals site open daily from 4pm; 2026's "world's largest comedy cabaret" — DJ at 7, free headline show at 9 nightly (SNL's Sarah Sherman hosting Comedy All-Stars; a free "Weird Al" Yankovic concert) (The Main, Cult MTL [F]).

**Two festivals in one:** francophone **Juste pour rire** and anglophone **Just For Laughs** programming run simultaneously under one org and one website; PdA phrases it "performances in both English and French (under Juste pour rire)" [F]; the official release brands it "Juste pour rire / Just for Laughs" and claims French+English+Spanish programming [F]. The site itself defaults French with an EN toggle; PWA name "JPR Montréal" [F].

**OFF-JFL / Zoofest:** Zoofest (est. 2009, ~125 shows/yr, the emerging-talent/fringe-ish wing; brand acquired in the 2024 sale) has been relaunched as **OFF-JPR** ("OFF JFL" in English media): zoofest.com now lands on the OFFJPR site (https://zoofest.com/ [S-redirect], https://www.offjpr.com/ [F], https://www.mtl.org/en/what-to-do/festivals-and-events/zoofest-alternative-multidisciplinary-festival [S]). 2026 OFF shows ran Jul 16–25 at The Comedy Nest, Café Cléopâtre and Théâtre Sainte-Catherine at $24–32, mostly **one-night** solo/variety sets (Cult MTL [F]). Industry side: **ComedyPRO** conference Jul 22–25 with the **New Faces** showcases (47 performers in 2026) (https://www.thenorwester.ca/just-for-laughs-unveils-2026-new-faces-lineup-as-montreal-festival-showcases-emerging-comedy-talent/ [S]).

**Venue geography:** heavily concentrated in/around the **Quartier des Spectacles**: Place des Festivals (outdoor), Place des Arts halls (Wilfrid-Pelletier, Maisonneuve), Club Soda, Le Gesù, Olympia, MTELUS, Le National, Théâtre St-Denis/Studio St-Denis, Studio TD, Café Cléopâtre, Théâtre Sainte-Catherine — with The Comedy Nest (2313 Ste-Catherine W.) the notable outlier ~3km west (The Main's venue list + Cult MTL addresses [F]).

**Clash reality at peak:** with ~250 shows over 12 days across ~25 venues, peak evenings stack 7:00pm / 9:30pm / midnight slots plus the free 9pm outdoor headliner — real but modest clash density compared to a fringe (tens of simultaneous shows, not hundreds). The repeated 3–5-night runs materially reduce clash pain (a missed showcase usually repeats the next night). 2026 also collided with the FIFA World Cup final (Jul 19) mid-festival (The Main [F]).

## 4. Per-city notes (beyond the table)

- **Vancouver**: launched 2016 as JFL NorthWest out of a partnership with the local NorthWest Comedy Fest, rebranded JFL Vancouver (~2024) [S: BC Creates, vancouversbestplaces]. 10 days, 100+ shows spanning stand-up/sketch/magic/podcasts; programmed by JFL's own talent team [F: Daily Hive]. jflvancouver.com itself is bot-gated (403 to curl and WebFetch) [F-attempted].
- **Toronto**: JFL42 (2012–2019, "42 shows" concept) → JFL Toronto (2021–2023) → 2024 cancelled in the bankruptcy → relaunched Sep 2025 with Comedy Bar as hub; 2025 headliners Iglesias, Bamford, Funches; big rooms (Meridian Hall, Elgin, Scotiabank Arena) plus clubs [S: Exclaim, Deadline, NEXT]. 2026: Sep 24–Oct 3; on-sale live now on toronto.hahaha.com [F].
- **Sydney**: tour-stop showcase model — mostly 1–2 nights per act; Opera House cluster + Century Venues rooms; "festival" umbrella stretches from late Sep to mid-Dec around the Nov 9–22 core [F: site schedule]. All-Star Gala at the Opera House Concert Hall Nov 21 [F].
- **Quebec City**: the 25-year-old ComediHa! Fest-Québec was renamed **Festival Juste pour rire – Québec** from 2025 ("Le ComediHa! Fest est mort, vive Juste pour rire – Québec!", https://www.lequotidien.com/arts/humour/2024/10/17/... [S]); first JPR edition Aug 6–17, 2025 [S: sorstu.ca]; 2026 moved to Jul 22–Aug 2 to run **concurrently** with Montreal as "two distinct yet complementary events" [F: official release]. Site now shows "Merci! À l'année prochaine" [F].
- **Belgium / Singapore / Bermuda**: see table — all partner-run, small (4 nights to a week), showcase-format.

## 5. Ticketing

- **hahaha.com family (Montreal, Quebec, Toronto, OFF-JPR, Roadshow)**: sells on its **own platform** — the Nova CMS ships `cart.js`/`checkout.js` with **Stripe** references, per-site accounts ("My JFL"), and a wishlist/favourites feature; show pages carry on-site Buy buttons [F: JS assets + session page]. Single basket **per city site** (each subdomain is its own store); no evidence of a cross-city basket. Caveat: I could not observe a live Montreal purchase end-to-end (listings emptied post-festival), and whether arena/Place-des-Arts headliners route to external box offices was **not verified**.
- **Sydney**: explicitly **no central ticketing** — "Buy only from the official agent listed on each show"; Book-Now links fan out to sydneyoperahouse.com (12 shows), ticketmaster.com.au (9), premier.ticketek.com.au (5), Century Venues' ticketsearch.com (5), seymourcentre.com (4), factorytheatre.com.au (1) [F: counted from justforlaughs.sydney HTML].
- **Singapore**: SISTIC [F: bohmpresents.com]. **Toronto**: own site plus a Ticketmaster CA "Just For Laughs Toronto" artist page [S]. **Vancouver**: platform not verified (site bot-gated).

## 6. Data reachability (montreal.hahaha.com)

- The whole hahaha.com family runs on a proprietary CMS ("**Nova**", assets served from `nova.justepourdivertir.com`, vendor origin `nova.melliom.com`) [F].
- **Server-rendered shell, client-loaded programme**: the shows/lineup page (`/fr/public/spectacles-1061/`, Toronto `/en/public/shows-87/`) arrives with an **empty** gallery container — `<div data-nova-module='shows' data-nova-filters-options='{...,"pagesize":16,"paginationStyle":"loadmore",...}'>` — populated by JS after load [F].
- **Endpoints (named, all observed in the shipped JS [F])**: pagination `GET {site}/{lang}/templates/{account}/{section}/{page}/{perpage}/{sectionid}/{contentid}/` returning **JSON-wrapped HTML fragments** `{html, pagination}` — not structured data; utility JSON: `/json/getvenue/{id}`, `/json/getspeaker/{id}`, `/json/getvariant/{variant}/{0|1}`, `/json/getmodalcontent/{id}` (verified live: `getmodalcontent/search` returns `{html:...}`; bare `getvenue/` returns `[]`).
- `sitemap.xml` → **503** ("ERREUR : Le système est actuellement indisponible") [F]. Show **detail** pages are fully server-rendered but huge (a Toronto session page: 2.7MB HTML) [F].
- **Listings are ephemeral**: Montreal and Quebec pages were emptied within weeks of the festival ending ("Merci ! À l'année prochaine") — any programme capture must happen **during** the on-sale window. Each site also ships a PWA `/manifest` [F].
- Net: no public structured-data API; programme extraction would mean parsing HTML fragments per city site. (No scraper built, per instructions.)

## 7. Concurrent festivals

- **Montreal, Jul 15–26**: **Fantasia International Film Festival** Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026 (30th) — near-total overlap [S: Wikipedia]; **Nuits d'Afrique** Jul 7–19 (40th, 120+ shows, mostly free) — overlaps the first JFL weekend [S: Cult MTL]; **Montréal Complètement Cirque** Jul 2–12 ends just before [S: mtl.org]; Jazz Fest ends ~Jul 4 (per task brief; not re-verified). Plus the World Cup final Jul 19, 2026 [F: The Main].
- **Toronto, Sep 24–Oct 3**: **TIFF** is Sep 10–20, 2026 [S: Wikipedia] — **no overlap**; JFL Toronto has the city's festival calendar largely to itself.
- **Vancouver, Feb 12–22**: **PuSh Festival** Jan 22–Feb 8, 2026 ends just before [S: pushfestival.ca]; **Chutzpah!** has moved off winter (2026 dates TBC) [S: Stir/vancouversbestplaces] — effectively clash-free.

## 8. Official planner/app

- **No current official mobile app found** for the ComediHa-era festivals (searches surface only websites and listings — NOT FOUND is the finding). What exists instead [F]: each hahaha.com site is an installable **PWA** (`/manifest`, "JPR Montréal") with a logged-in **favourites/wishlist** feature (`novaLoadWishlist()`, "Mes favoris") — i.e., a light on-site planner. Sydney/Singapore sites have no planner at all (mailing-list + external ticket links) [F].
- **Third-party planners**: none found; the gap is filled by editorial guides (The Main, Cult MTL picks) and local listing sites (do604's JFL Vancouver hub, Miss604's schedule posts) [S].

## Fringe-like ↔ showcase-like verdicts

- **Montreal**: firmly **showcase-like** — curated galas, 1–5-night showcase runs and free outdoor headliners concentrated in one district — with OFF-JPR as a small fringe-like annex (~one-night $25 club sets); it is a "pick your nights" festival, not an Edinburgh-style open-access run grid.
- **Satellites (all cities)**: pure **showcase/tour-stop** presenting models — one-to-three nights per act on venue ticketing (Sydney/Singapore fully external), tens not hundreds of shows; planner/clash value is modest everywhere except possibly Vancouver (100+ shows/10 days).

# Just For Laughs (JFL) empire — research report (2026-09-01)

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl/WebFetch and read directly; **[S]** = search-snippet evidence (not opened; attribute to the named publisher). All dates below verified against at least one tagged source.

## 1. Ownership story — who owns JFL and how stable is it

Timeline:

- **1983** — first Montreal festival; founded by Gilbert Rozon; grew into "the world's largest comedy festival" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **2017–2018** — Rozon (majority stakeholder) resigns amid sexual-misconduct allegations; company put up for sale. **Mar–Jun 2018**: Howie Mandel + ICM Partners, joined by Bell Media and Groupe CH (owner of evenko/L'Équipe Spectra/Bell Centre), acquire Groupe Juste pour rire (https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-and-groupe-ch-join-howie-mandel-and-icm-partners-in-just-for-laughs-ownership-group/ [S], https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/bell-media-just-for-laughs-1.4697493 [S]).
- **Mar 5, 2024** — Groupe Juste pour rire files for creditor protection; the 2024 Montreal **and Toronto** festivals are cancelled outright. Blamed: COVID revenue losses, inflation, shrinking network/streamer spending. Later revealed: **$22.5M in debt plus $3.4M owed to creditors**, and **$800K lost to an email-phishing scheme in 2023** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F], citing CBC; https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **May 29 – Jun 2024** — **ComediHa!** (Quebec City entertainment group founded 1997 by Sylvain Parent-Bédard) acquires the assets — brands Juste pour rire, Just For Laughs, ZooFest, ComedyPro, the Gags, and the audiovisual catalogue — with Quebec Superior Court endorsement (https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/comediha-acquires-assets-of-just-for-laughs-811817974.html [S], https://playbackonline.ca/2024/05/30/comediha-to-acquire-select-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **Since then** — the parent group has been renamed **Groupe Juste pour divertir**, HQ in Quebec City; site footers read "©2026 Juste Pour Divertir" (https://www.hahaha.com/fr/public/le-groupe/a-propos-377/ [F]; rename reported by https://sorstu.ca/le-comediha-fest-quebec-devient-le-festival-juste-pour-rire-quebec/ [S]). ComediHa!'s own 25-year-old Quebec City festival was folded into the JPR brand (see Quebec City below); Parent-Bédard keeps ComediHa! as the TV/scripted brand (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **Summer 2024** — no Montreal festival, but ComediHa staged a stopgap outdoor event, "ComediHa! salue Montréal", with JFL-branded events at Place des Festivals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]). Satellites restarted first (Sydney, Bermuda, Vancouver) (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-comedy-festival-return-australia-bermuda-bankruptcy-1235980376/ [S]).
- **2025 Montreal** — comeback edition **Jul 16–27, 2025** (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-returns-2025-1236069413/ [S]). Wikipedia describes it as smaller and "without the usual televised galas" [F]; Montreal Rocks reports gala tapings returned with hosts Fortune Feimster, Roy Wood Jr., Michelle Buteau, Mikey Day (https://montrealrocks.ca/just-for-laughs-returns-with-its-2025-lineup/ [S]) — a "Fortune Feimster Gala" photo from 2025 appears in The Main's 2026 guide (https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide [F]). Official wrap claim: total budget "more than $45 million invested in culture and the economy", sold-out venues, across Montreal + Quebec City (https://quebec.hahaha.com/page/detail/news/juste-pour-rire--just-for-laughs-quebec--announces-2026-festival-dates-74/ [F]).
- **2026 Montreal** — **44th edition, Jul 15–26, back "at full volume": 250 shows, 25 venues, 800+ artists** (The Main [F]) — full detail in §3.

**Stability verdict:** the brand survived receivership intact and is past the danger zone: a full-scale 2026 Montreal edition ran, the 2026 dates were announced a year ahead by press release [F], government partners are visible (Loto-Québec collaboration, Canada/Québec/City-of-Montreal messages on the official site [F]), and 2027 satellite dates are already published (Bermuda Feb 17–20, 2027 [F]; Namur Mar 15–21, 2027 [F]). It is now a regional-champion-owned company (Quebec City, private) rather than a media-conglomerate portfolio piece. Treat Montreal as a durable annual anchor again, with one caveat: the owner is 2 years into the turnaround and audited attendance/scale figures are its own marketing claims.

The site itself defaults French with an EN toggle; PWA name "JPR Montréal" [F].

**Venue geography:** heavily concentrated in/around the **Quartier des Spectacles**: Place des Festivals (outdoor), Place des Arts halls (Wilfrid-Pelletier, Maisonneuve), Club Soda, Le Gesù, Olympia, MTELUS, Le National, Théâtre St-Denis/Studio St-Denis, Studio TD, Café Cléopâtre, Théâtre Sainte-Catherine — with The Comedy Nest (2313 Ste-Catherine W.) the notable outlier ~3km west (The Main's venue list + Cult MTL addresses [F]).

## 1. Ownership story — who owns JFL and how stable is it

Timeline:

- **1983** — first Montreal festival; founded by Gilbert Rozon; grew into "the world's largest comedy festival" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **2017–2018** — Rozon (majority stakeholder) resigns amid sexual-misconduct allegations; company put up for sale. **Mar–Jun 2018**: Howie Mandel + ICM Partners, joined by Bell Media and Groupe CH (owner of evenko/L'Équipe Spectra/Bell Centre), acquire Groupe Juste pour rire (https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-and-groupe-ch-join-howie-mandel-and-icm-partners-in-just-for-laughs-ownership-group/ [S], https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/bell-media-just-for-laughs-1.4697493 [S]).
- **Mar 5, 2024** — Groupe Juste pour rire files for creditor protection; the 2024 Montreal **and Toronto** festivals are cancelled outright. Blamed: COVID revenue losses, inflation, shrinking network/streamer spending. Later revealed: **$22.5M in debt plus $3.4M owed to creditors**, and **$800K lost to an email-phishing scheme in 2023** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F], citing CBC; https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **May 29 – Jun 2024** — **ComediHa!** (Quebec City entertainment group founded 1997 by Sylvain Parent-Bédard) acquires the assets — brands Juste pour rire, Just For Laughs, ZooFest, ComedyPro, the Gags, and the audiovisual catalogue — with Quebec Superior Court endorsement (https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/comediha-acquires-assets-of-just-for-laughs-811817974.html [S], https://playbackonline.ca/2024/05/30/comediha-to-acquire-select-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **Since then** — the parent group has been renamed **Groupe Juste pour divertir**, HQ in Quebec City; site footers read "©2026 Juste Pour Divertir" (https://www.hahaha.com/fr/public/le-groupe/a-propos-377/ [F]; rename reported by https://sorstu.ca/le-comediha-fest-quebec-devient-le-festival-juste-pour-rire-quebec/ [S]). ComediHa!'s own 25-year-old Quebec City festival was folded into the JPR brand (see Quebec City below); Parent-Bédard keeps ComediHa! as the TV/scripted brand (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **Summer 2024** — no Montreal festival, but ComediHa staged a stopgap outdoor event, "ComediHa! salue Montréal", with JFL-branded events at Place des Festivals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]). Satellites restarted first (Sydney, Bermuda, Vancouver) (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-comedy-festival-return-australia-bermuda-bankruptcy-1235980376/ [S]).
- **2025 Montreal** — comeback edition **Jul 16–27, 2025** (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-returns-2025-1236069413/ [S]). Wikipedia describes it as smaller and "without the usual televised galas" [F]; Montreal Rocks reports gala tapings returned with hosts Fortune Feimster, Roy Wood Jr., Michelle Buteau, Mikey Day (https://montrealrocks.ca/just-for-laughs-returns-with-its-2025-lineup/ [S]) — a "Fortune Feimster Gala" photo from 2025 appears in The Main's 2026 guide (https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide [F]). Official wrap claim: total budget "more than $45 million invested in culture and the economy", sold-out venues, across Montreal + Quebec City (https://quebec.hahaha.com/page/detail/news/juste-pour-rire--just-for-laughs-quebec--announces-2026-festival-dates-74/ [F]).
- **2026 Montreal** — **44th edition, Jul 15–26, back "at full volume": 250 shows, 25 venues, 800+ artists** (The Main [F]) — full detail in §3.

**Stability verdict:** the brand survived receivership intact and is past the danger zone: a full-scale 2026 Montreal edition ran, the 2026 dates were announced a year ahead by press release [F], government partners are visible (Loto-Québec collaboration, Canada/Québec/City-of-Montreal messages on the official site [F]), and 2027 satellite dates are already published (Bermuda Feb 17–20, 2027 [F]; Namur Mar 15–21, 2027 [F]). It is now a regional-champion-owned company (Quebec City, private) rather than a media-conglomerate portfolio piece. Treat Montreal as a durable annual anchor again, with one caveat: the owner is 2 years into the turnaround and audited attendance/scale figures are its own marketing claims.

## 3. Montreal flagship dossier

**Scale & shape (2026, 44th edition, Jul 15–26 — 12 days):** ~250 ticketed shows across ~25 downtown venues, "hundreds" of free outdoor performances, 800+ artists in both official languages (The Main [F]); Place des Arts' page claims ~1,700 artists from 19 countries and "nearly two million visitors" (https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival [F] — marketing copy; the 2M figure includes free outdoor crowds). Jerry Seinfeld added to the 2026 edition (https://deadline.com/2026/05/just-for-laughs-new-shows-jerry-seinfeld-2026-edition-1236882104/ [S]).

**The model — three tiers [all F: The Main, Cult MTL, Place des Arts]:**
1. **Galas**: TV-taping showcase galas at Théâtre Maisonneuve (Place des Arts), host + curated lineup — the festival's signature product.
2. **Ticketed indoor shows**: mostly **curated multi-night showcase runs**, not fringe runs — e.g. The Culture Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19, 7pm), The Nasty Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19+21, 9:30pm), Brit(ish) (Le Gesù, Jul 21–25), Midnight Surprise (Studio TD, Jul 22–25, midnight), plus premium one-offs (An Evening with David Letterman + Will Arnett, Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, Jul 21, $148–$550) (Cult MTL [F]). Typical run: 1–5 nights.
3. **Free outdoor**: Place des Festivals site open daily from 4pm; 2026's "world's largest comedy cabaret" — DJ at 7, free headline show at 9 nightly (SNL's Sarah Sherman hosting Comedy All-Stars; a free "Weird Al" Yankovic concert) (The Main, Cult MTL [F]).

**Two festivals in one:** francophone **Juste pour rire** and anglophone **Just For Laughs** programming run simultaneously under one org and one website; PdA phrases it "performances in both English and French (under Juste pour rire)" [F]; the official release brands it "Juste pour rire / Just for Laughs" and claims French+English+Spanish programming [F]. The site itself defaults French with an EN toggle; PWA name "JPR Montréal" [F].

**OFF-JFL / Zoofest:** Zoofest (est. 2009, ~125 shows/yr, the emerging-talent/fringe-ish wing; brand acquired in the 2024 sale) has been relaunched as **OFF-JPR** ("OFF JFL" in English media): zoofest.com now lands on the OFFJPR site (https://zoofest.com/ [S-redirect], https://www.offjpr.com/ [F], https://www.mtl.org/en/what-to-do/festivals-and-events/zoofest-alternative-multidisciplinary-festival [S]). 2026 OFF shows ran Jul 16–25 at The Comedy Nest, Café Cléopâtre and Théâtre Sainte-Catherine at $24–32, mostly **one-night** solo/variety sets (Cult MTL [F]). Industry side: **ComedyPRO** conference Jul 22–25 with the **New Faces** showcases (47 performers in 2026) (https://www.thenorwester.ca/just-for-laughs-unveils-2026-new-faces-lineup-as-montreal-festival-showcases-emerging-comedy-talent/ [S]).

**Venue geography:** heavily concentrated in/around the **Quartier des Spectacles**: Place des Festivals (outdoor), Place des Arts halls (Wilfrid-Pelletier, Maisonneuve), Club Soda, Le Gesù, Olympia, MTELUS, Le National, Théâtre St-Denis/Studio St-Denis, Studio TD, Café Cléopâtre, Théâtre Sainte-Catherine — with The Comedy Nest (2313 Ste-Catherine W.) the notable outlier ~3km west (The Main's venue list + Cult MTL addresses [F]).

**Clash reality at peak:** with ~250 shows over 12 days across ~25 venues, peak evenings stack 7:00pm / 9:30pm / midnight slots plus the free 9pm outdoor headliner — real but modest clash density compared to a fringe (tens of simultaneous shows, not hundreds). The repeated 3–5-night runs materially reduce clash pain (a missed showcase usually repeats the next night). 2026 also collided with the FIFA World Cup final (Jul 19) mid-festival (The Main [F]).

## The fringe-shaped tier: dossiers

The festivals where "which of tonight's shows can I make" is a real problem —
long runs, repeated performances, many parallel rooms. This is the tier a
planning product can serve.

### Melbourne International Comedy Festival — the southern Edinburgh

The standout of the whole census, and the closest thing to a second Edinburgh
Fringe anywhere in comedy.

- **Scale, delivered 2026** (the festival's own
  [40th-year wrap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/)):
  **803 shows and events, 9,164 performances, 26 days** (25 Mar–19 Apr),
  796,975 attendees (+13% YoY), A$26.6m box office, average paid ticket
  A$38.20. That is ~350 performances a day — genuinely fringe-like clash
  density. Launch press said "over 750 shows", so ~50 more landed after
  launch: the launch-undercount trap
  [market-and-audience/](../market-and-audience/README.md) documents holds
  here too.
- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style seasons — one show is the same hour repeated
  across the run (sampled runs of 7–24 performances; cheaper previews,
  cheap-Tuesday flags). Participation is **open registration**
  ([registrations open each October](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/),
  with independent venues found via a venue finder) — the Fringe's
  open-access mechanism, at ~one-fifth Edinburgh's scale.
- **Organizer & recurrence**: its own festival organization, annual every
  autumn since 1987, always Melbourne, centred on Melbourne Town Hall;
  [self-described](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/about-us/) as "one of
  the three largest comedy festivals in the world, alongside Edinburgh
  Festival Fringe and Montreal's Just for Laughs" and "Australia's largest
  ticketed cultural event". Stable through a 2026 leadership handover
  (Susan Provan retired after 32 years;
  [Dylan Cole appointed CEO/Festival Director](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/melbourne-international-comedy-festival-appoints-dylan-cole-as-new-ceofestival-director/)).
  2027 dates already announced (24 Mar–18 Apr).
- **Venues**: 143 venue buildings in its own venues data — 66 in the CBD, the
  rest a suburban tail (Northcote, Box Hill…) — a walkable core plus
  outliers, the Edinburgh pattern loosened one notch.
- **Ticketing**: comedyfestival.com.au is **its own central box office** with
  one basket across shows (a cart API, accounts, native favourites with
  share-a-favourites-list); a minority of external-venue shows link out to
  Ticketmaster/Ticketek/Arts Centre Melbourne.
- **Data reachability — best in the census**: unauthenticated JSON endpoints,
  verified by fetch:
  `POST /umbraco/api/searchapi/searchShows` (826 show records for 2026, paged,
  with runs, performance counts, venue rooms),
  `GET /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues` (all 143 venues with address,
  capacity, accessibility flags), and each show page embeds a `sessionData`
  JSON array with per-performance date, time, **on-sale status and
  sold-out/preview/cheap-night flags** — near enough 1:1 onto the fields the
  Edinburgh scraper already produces. A
  [sitemap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/sitemap.xml) lists every show
  URL.
- **Concurrent**: Melbourne Food & Wine Festival and the Flower & Garden Show
  overlap the window, with the AFL season running throughout (per
  [melbournetourism.org](https://www.melbournetourism.org/melbourne-events-and-festivals-calendar/))
  — city-draw amplifiers, though nothing on the scale of Edinburgh's August
  cluster.
- **Planner field**: the site's account favourites are the only planning tool;
  no current official app found (a
  [2010-era iPhone app](https://itwire.com/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html)
  is the last trace), and no third-party planner exists — see
  [competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

### Adelaide Fringe — covered elsewhere, plus the ticketing angle

Scale, open access and the "Mad March" cluster are on
[festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/](../festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/README.md);
what this pass adds is ticketing and data. Adelaide Fringe Inc. (a
not-for-profit, incorporated 1975) runs **its own ticketing platform,
FringeTIX** — [first used in 1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_Fringe),
today a Rails app inside adelaidefringe.com.au with a central cart across all
shows and venues — and [markets that platform (AVR) to other open-access
festivals](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/about-us) as "the best solution for
collating and managing open access festivals". No public API was found
(probes 404/500 off-season); a scrape would target the server-rendered
FringeTIX listing in season. Comedy's share of the ~1,500-show programme is
not published —
[the 2026 launch](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringefeed/news/2026-program-unveiled-with-more-than-1500-shows)
lists comedy first among genres with no counts.

### NZ International Comedy Festival — one festival, two cities at once

- **Organizer**: the [New Zealand Comedy Trust](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/the-new-zealand-comedy-trust/),
  a charitable not-for-profit; festival annual each May since 1995 (roots
  1993), 2026 = the 33rd Auckland edition and the Wellington leg's 30th.
- **The two-city model**: one programme, one window (1–24 May 2026), running
  **simultaneously** in Auckland and Wellington with region-filtered listings
  (plus a "Gala toe-dip" in Christchurch in 2026); some acts play a season in
  each city inside the window. Each city is a compact centre cluster
  (Auckland: Q Theatre, Basement, The Classic + big halls for headliners;
  Wellington: BATS' three rooms, Te Auaha, Hannah Playhouse).
- **Scale & model**: the Trust's steady-state description is
  ["over 120 show seasons, over 600 performances, around 200 comedians"](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/new-zealand-international-comedy-festival/),
  75,000+ attendance in 2025 — Edinburgh-style short seasons (~5 performances
  each), a real but small evening-choice problem (~a dozen parallel shows per
  city on peak nights).
- **Ticketing**: **no central basket** — the festival site is a catalogue that
  [hands buyers to the right agent per show](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/how-to-buy-tickets):
  Ticketmaster, Q Theatre's box office, Eventfinda or iTicket, each with its
  own fees. A cross-show plan means juggling up to four seller accounts.
- **Data**: server-rendered SilverStripe site, no JSON API found; a scrape
  targets the find-a-show HTML per region.
- **Concurrent**: May in Auckland is genuinely congested — NZ Music Month plus
  the Auckland Writers Festival inside the window;
  [The Spinoff](https://thespinoff.co.nz/pop-culture/06-05-2026/auckland-has-a-problem-everything-awesome-is-happening-in-may-all-at-once):
  "Auckland has a problem. Everything awesome is happening in May, all at
  once."
- **Planner field**: the official planning tool is a downloadable timetable
  PDF. Nothing else exists.

### Sydney Comedy Festival — the boundary case

Fringe-scale show count, showcase-shaped mechanics — the census's clearest
demonstration that show count alone doesn't decide the shape:

- **Delivered 2026** (per the festival's wrap, carried by
  [The Movie Boards](https://www.themovieboards.net/2026/05/18/record-growth-and-huge-crowds-for-sydney-comedy-festival/)):
  **411 shows, close to 1,000 performances, 57 venues, 175,000+ attendees**
  over 35 days (13 Apr–17 May) — but that is **~2.4 performances per show**
  against MICF's ~11.4: mostly weekend-length visits, galas and showcases,
  not month-long seasons.
- **Structure**: run by [Century Entertainment](https://www.century.com.au/about/),
  a commercial venue group (Enmore Theatre, Comedy Store…), **curated by
  application**, venues scattered "from Bondi to Penrith" (a metro
  constellation, not a walkable core), **per-venue ticketing** with no
  central basket (Century venues on TicketSearch, tour venues on their own
  sellers), followed by a national showcase tour May–December. Concurrent:
  Sydney Royal Easter Show and Writers' Festival brush the window, Vivid
  starts just after.
- Century also produces the **[Perth Comedy Festival](https://www.perthcomedyfestival.com/about/)**
  (20 Apr–17 May 2026, ~70 gigs across 5 venues — fully showcase-shaped) on
  the same WordPress codebase — one scrape adapter would cover both.

PLACEHOLDER-UK-TIER

# US Majors — Comedy Festival Research Dossiers

**Evidence key:** *(fetched)* = page retrieved by curl/WebFetch and read directly; *(snippet)* = WebSearch result attributed to its publisher. Today = 2026-09-01.

## Cross-festival findings (the headlines)

- **No US major is fringe-shaped.** Every festival here is one-night curated events, not repeated runs. The fringe-like elements that do exist are partial: Moontower's badge club-binge, DCM's marathon badge, Skankfest's compound pass.
- **November is the US comedy-festival pile-up**: NYCF (Nov 6–15), 312 Chicago (Nov 5–15), Boston (Nov 10–14), Skankfest New Orleans (Nov 13–15) all overlap in 2026 — different cities, same touring headliners circulating.
- **Central discovery, fragmented purchase is the US norm**: even corporate-run Netflix Is A Joke routes its 498 listed events to 12+ different ticket vendors (counted from its own schedule payload, fetched).
- **Netflix Is A Joke is biennial, not annual** — 2022, 2024, 2026; no 2023 or 2025 edition (Wikipedia; the prompt's "2025 edition" premise is wrong — netflixisajoke2025.com is a third-party resale SEO site).
- **Data reachability is generally good**: 4 of the 5 majors serve server-rendered HTML with structured data (Netflix inlines its full event dataset; NYCF exposes a live WordPress REST API). SF Sketchfest is the exception (captcha-walled).

---

## 1. SF Sketchfest — San Francisco, Jan 15–Feb 1 2026

- **Organizer**: Independent — founded 2001 by David Owen, Cole Stratton and Janet Varney as a showcase for six Bay Area sketch groups; same founders still run it (snippet: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SF_Sketchfest, podnews.net press release). Stability: 23 editions across 25 years.
- **Recurrence**: Annual in SF each Jan/Feb since 2002, with a COVID gap: last pre-pandemic edition Feb 2020; 2021 canceled; Jan 2022 postponed for Omicron; returned Jan 20–Feb 5 2023 as the 20th annual (snippets: sfgate.com, ktvu.com, localnewsmatters.org). 2026 = 23rd edition (snippet: deadline.com).
- **Scale**: 200+ shows, 500+ performers, 13 venues, 18 days (Jan 15–Feb 1) (snippets: deadline.com, brooklynvegan.com, sfchronicle.com). Attendance: NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: One-night curated specials — reunions and tributes that structurally can't repeat (Kids in the Hall *Brain Candy* 30th anniversary, "The Women of SNL", Futurama Live, a Nickelodeon *Doug* 35th reunion), plus stand-up, podcasts, improv (snippet: brooklynvegan.com). Curated, not open-submission. NOT FOUND: any repeated-run programming.
- **Venue geography**: 13 venues spread across San Francisco — Cobb's (North Beach), Punch Line (FiDi), Great American Music Hall (Tenderloin), Sydney Goldstein Theater (Civic Center area) (snippet: brooklynvegan.com). A transit/rideshare spread, not one walkable cluster — but SF is compact vs LA.
- **Clash reality**: ~200 shows / 18 days ≈ 11/day average — clashes exist on weekends but it's mostly a pick-your-events problem; the one-off reunion format makes each clash unresolvable (no second chance).
- **Ticketing**: Single tickets per show via **Eventbrite** — official SF Sketchfest organizer account, "124 upcoming events" at announcement time (snippet: eventbrite.com/o/sf-sketchfest-57967098043; organizer page itself fetched, 200, but events are client-loaded — JSON-LD carries only Organization/ProfilePage). No badge/pass found.
- **Data reachability**: **sfsketchfest.com is curl-hostile** — SiteGround captcha (`sg-captcha: challenge`, HTTP 202 meta-refresh to `/.well-known/sgcaptcha/`) on every path incl. sitemap.xml (fetched); WebFetch also returns empty. Schedule lives on **Sched**: sfsketchfest2026.sched.com — 403 to curl too (Cloudflare). Practical path: Eventbrite organizer listing.
- **Concurrent festivals**: None found in the Jan window.
- **Official planner**: Sched instance (sfsketchfest2026.sched.com) — Sched provides per-user agendas/sync; a yearly instance exists (2023 one confirmed via snippet).
- **Verdict**: **Showcase-like at fringe breadth** — 200+ shows over 18 days but every one a curated one-off with per-show Eventbrite tickets; nothing runs twice, nothing is open-entry.

## 2. Netflix Is A Joke Fest — Los Angeles, May 4–10 2026

- **Organizer**: Netflix (corporate); promoted with Live Nation involvement historically. Produced by Netflix per Wikipedia (snippet).
- **Recurrence**: **Biennial** — announced for spring 2020, canceled for COVID (snippet: hollywoodreporter.com); debut Apr–May 2022; editions 2022, 2024, 2026; **no 2023 or 2025 edition** (snippet: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Is_a_Joke_Festival). 2026 edition confirmed delivered — ran May 4–10 (snippet: netflix.com/tudum "2026 Is Underway"). Growth: 130 comedians/25 venues (2022) → "500+ shows" 2024 (snippets: Wikipedia, variety.com) → 2026 below. 2022 reportedly sold 260,000+ tickets (snippet, origin claim Netflix).
- **Scale**: Official meta description (fetched): "**475+ Shows 500+ artists 45+ venues May 4-10. The largest comedy event in history**". The site's own schedule payload carries **498 dated events referencing 116 distinct venue slugs** (fetched, counted); press said 35 venues / 350+ events at January announcement (snippets: hollywoodreporter.com, timeout.com) — the count grew to fest time; "45+" is the official venue figure, 116 includes rooms/pop-ups.
- **Show model**: One-night showcases, galas, arena/amphitheater headliners (Hollywood Bowl, Greek Theatre, Intuit Dome), live podcast tapings, table reads, live tapings of Netflix specials (fetched meta + snippet: hollywoodreporter.com). Curated; no submissions. Some comedians play multiple nights/venues, but as distinct events, not runs.
- **Venue geography**: The extreme car-city case — Hollywood Bowl to Intuit Dome (Inglewood) is ~15 mi; clubs cluster on Sunset/Hollywood but the fest spans greater LA (snippet: hollywoodreporter.com venue list; payload venues carry per-venue `parkingInfo`, lat/long — fetched). Cross-town same-night stacking is impractical; scheduling means choosing a neighborhood per night.
- **Clash reality**: From the payload's own timestamps: 63–101 events per day (peak Sat May 9 = 101) (fetched, computed). At ~90 parallel-ish events/day in a car city this is the hardest clash problem in US comedy — but consumers treat it as pick-your-headliner, since most attendees buy 1–3 marquee tickets.
- **Ticketing**: **Single tickets only — explicitly no pass**: FAQ (fetched): "For every show you want to go to, you'll need an individual ticket. There are no festival passes that grant you access to every event." Purchase fragments across vendors — counted from 498 `ticketUrl`s (fetched): Ticketmaster 167, Eventbrite 118, ShowClix 51, TicketWeb 34, Hotel Café 23, UCB 14, Eventim 14, Tixr 12, plus SquadUp, Universe, Leap, venue sites. Ticketmaster-first (Platinum pricing, Transfer referenced in FAQ, fetched) but a third of inventory is elsewhere.
- **Data reachability**: Excellent — Next.js with the **entire event dataset inlined in the server-rendered RSC payload** of `/schedule` (1.4 MB, fetched): per-event `dateAndTime`, `venue{id,slug,name}`, `ticketUrl`, `showType`, `tags`; per-venue address, lat/long, capacity, `parkingInfo`, `bagPolicy`, `containsFreeEvents`. IDs are Airtable-style (`rec…`); CMS refs to Sanity. No separate public JSON endpoint needed — one HTML fetch gives everything. sitemap.xml 404s (fetched).
- **Concurrent festivals**: None found overlapping in LA that week.
- **Official planner/app**: No dedicated app found (searched). The site itself is the planner: /schedule with date browsing and an on-page "favorite" feature (84 favorite-related strings in payload, fetched), /search, /venues; Netflix Tudum publishes guide articles (snippet).
- **Verdict**: **Pure showcase at maximum scale** — 498 curated one-offs in 7 days, individual tickets only across 12+ vendors, in the least walkable city in the set; the deciding facts are the FAQ's "no festival passes" and 100-events-per-peak-day spread across greater LA.

## 3. New York Comedy Festival — NYC, Nov 6–15 2026

- **Organizer**: Founded 2004 by Caroline Hirsch; still hers — "The festival is produced by Carolines" (official FAQ, fetched); footer: "Produced By [Carolines] © 2026 550 Comedy Inc." (fetched); volunteer email @carolines.com (fetched). The Carolines on Broadway club closed Dec 2022 but the brand persists as the festival's producer; Hirsch still fronts it in 2026 press (snippet: abc7ny.com interview).
- **Recurrence**: Annual since 2004; 2026 = "22nd annual" (FAQ, fetched) — arithmetic implies one skipped year (likely 2020; not directly verified).
- **Scale**: Official banner (fetched): "10 days / 5 boroughs / 100+ shows / 200+ comedians"; after an August wave, "more than 150 shows" (snippets: iloveny.com, iconvsicon.com). Sitemap has 204 lineup pages incl. multi-night duplicates (fetched). NY State tourism calls it "the largest and longest-running comedy festival in the country" (snippet: iloveny.com — a contestable claim given Sketchfest/Netflix numbers). Attendance: NOT FOUND.
- **Show model**: Headliner one-nighters at theatres (Ziwe, Marc Maron, Daniel Sloss; Stand Up for Heroes 20th-anniversary gala with Springsteen/Stewart at David Geffen Hall) + club showcases; some tours do 2 nights (Ms. Pat, Jess Hilarious ×2–4, fetched homepage/sitemap). **Open submissions exist** for three curated showcase slots: The Breakouts, Creators to Watch, New York's Funniest Stand-Ups (deadline Sep 16; fetched submissions page).
- **Venue geography**: 39 venues in the venue sitemap (fetched) — Beacon Theatre, Town Hall, David Geffen Hall, Kings Theatre (Brooklyn), Tribeca PAC, Hard Rock's Venue on Music Row, plus ~30 comedy clubs from Harlem to Astoria (QED) to Bushwick (Tiny Cupboard). "All five boroughs" claimed (FAQ, fetched); the sitemap's borough taxonomy lists only Manhattan as a populated archive (fetched). Subway-linked spread, not walkable as one cluster.
- **Clash reality**: 150+ shows / 10 days ≈ 15/day, mostly evening-stacked — a real same-night choice problem on weekends, but marquee-driven: fans buy their headliner, clubs absorb the rest.
- **Ticketing**: No central platform — homepage Buy Tickets links go per-venue (fetched): Ticketmaster (12 distinct events counted), ATG Tickets (Kings Theatre), Tribeca PAC's own system; club shows on club systems. No badge/pass found.
- **Data reachability**: Good — WordPress, server-rendered; sitemaps enumerate lineup (204 URLs), venues (39), boroughs (fetched); **live REST API**: `/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup?per_page=2` returns 200 with JSON (fetched). Scrapable without a browser.
- **Concurrent festivals**: 312 (Chicago) and Boston overlap the same week; within NYC itself nothing found.
- **Official planner/app**: None found — website lineup + venue pages only.
- **Verdict**: **Showcase-like** — a curated headliner umbrella over per-venue ticketing; the deciding facts are one-night theatre bills on Ticketmaster/ATG/house systems and no pass, with submissions confined to three contest-style showcases.

## 4. Moontower Comedy Festival — Austin, Apr 8–19 2026

- **Organizer**: Nonprofit venue — "produced by the Paramount Theatre" (official site, fetched); the Paramount & State Theatres are run by the Austin Theatre Alliance. Stable: 2026 = 14th year (snippet: kxan.com), founded 2012.
- **Recurrence**: Annual each April in downtown Austin; ran through COVID era with disruptions (not detailed on-page). 2026: Apr 8–19 full window (snippet: do512.com; official page confirms "TWO-WEEK... every April", fetched), with the **4-day Club Binge Apr 15–18** (official FAQ, fetched).
- **Scale**: "Over 150 of the world's top and emerging comedians"; Club Binge: "Over 100 comedians... at 10+ walkable comedy clubs" (official, fetched). Show count and attendance: NOT FOUND (likely 100+ club shows; not published as a number).
- **Show model**: Two-tier: (a) headliner one-nighters across two weeks at Paramount/State (single tickets); (b) 4-day badge-driven club programming — curated showcases ("New York's Finest", "Cheers Queers", "The Internationals"), podcasts, one-person shows, nightly parties (FAQ, fetched). Club comedians play multiple showcase slots across the binge. Curated; no public submissions found.
- **Venue geography**: The walkable exception — Paramount, State, Antone's, The Creek & The Cave, Velveeta Room, Higbies, Sunset Strip, Rozco's, Vulcan Gas Company, Fallout Theater, all downtown; one outlier, Cap City Comedy Club at The Domain (~10 mi north, needs pre-requested tickets) (FAQ, fetched).
- **Clash reality**: During the binge, 10+ rooms run simultaneously nightly — genuinely fringe-like grazing: badge-holders walk in anywhere, "No tickets or reservations necessary" (FAQ, fetched). Room-capacity risk replaces ticket clashes.
- **Ticketing**: The hybrid that matters: **badge** (club binge all-access + headliner presale priority) + **single tickets** for theatres; **daily wristbands**; club single tickets sold but "do not guarantee entry — badges and wristbands [may] fill a venue, resulting in... refunds" (FAQ, fetched). Platform: **Tessitura** on the venue's own tickets.austintheatre.org (fingerprinted in page source, fetched). Badge prices: NOT FOUND (page shows "see you next year"; a "Full Moon Badge" tier existed, page now 404, fetched).
- **Data reachability**: Good — WordPress (wp-json present) with server-rendered pages: /moontower-comedy/comics/, /theatreschedule/, /faq/ (all curl-clean, fetched); event detail on Tessitura pages, server-rendered (fetched a sample). No public JSON API identified beyond standard wp-json.
- **Concurrent festivals**: Nothing in Austin in April (SXSW is March); note the Nashville fest runs the near-identical Apr 9–19 window in 2026 — competing for the same touring headliners, not the same audience.
- **Official planner/app**: NOT FOUND for 2026 — schedule pages + daily fest emails with "programmer picks" (FAQ, fetched). (Historical Moontower apps existed; nothing current found.)
- **Verdict**: **The closest thing to a fringe in the US majors — but only its badge half**: turn-up-and-graze entry at 10+ walkable downtown clubs with no reservations is fringe mechanics; the two-week headliner layer on Tessitura single tickets is a standard showcase series.

## 5. SXSW Comedy — Austin, Mar 13–16 2026 (within SXSW Mar 12–18)

- **Organizer**: SXSW, LLC (corporate; majority-owned by Penske Media since 2021 — background knowledge, unverified here). Comedy track "since 2008 — 20 years" (official page, fetched).
- **Recurrence**: Annual within SXSW; 19th edition in 2026 (snippet: deadline.com). 2027 already scheduled: comedy Mar 17–20 within SXSW Mar 15–21 (official page, fetched).
- **Scale**: Tiny inside the giant — official 2027 stats block (fetched): "**4 Nights, 2 Venues, 65+ Performers, 30 Shows, 6 Types of showcases**". 2026 matched the shape: The Creek and The Cave + Esther's Follies (snippet: deadline.com).
- **Show model**: Curated showcases fronted by club brands (The Stand, Gotham, Cracked Comedy Club showcases), stand-up, improv, game shows, podcast tapings; alumni pipeline framing (Schumer 2011, Nanjiani 2013, Kroll 2017) (fetched page + deadline.com snippet). No open submissions for comedy (PanelPicker is for conference sessions).
- **Venue geography**: 2 venues, downtown Austin; SXSW's own FAQ: "Once you are downtown, most everything is within walking, pedicab or shuttle distance" (fetched).
- **Clash reality**: Comedy barely clashes with itself (2 rooms) — it clashes with **everything else at SXSW**: film premieres, 1,000+ music showcases, conference tracks, all on one credential. The purest "the city is the draw" case: comedy is a track you graze between other festivals.
- **Ticketing**: Badge-only access — comedy is included for all badge holders ("Open to all badge holders", fetched); 2027 badge tiers: Platinum $1,395 / Innovation $895 / Film & TV $775 / Music $550 (fetched). Exceptions exist (2026 Dropout Improv show: Platinum badges + separately sold tickets, snippet: deadline.com). No per-show tickets otherwise; secondary single-ticket sales are not the model.
- **Data reachability**: schedule.sxsw.com is a client-rendered SPA (Vite/JS bundle; shell HTML only, fetched) — no public JSON endpoint identified without executing JS; sxsw.com marketing pages are server-rendered and curl-clean (fetched). sitemap.xml present (fetched).
- **Concurrent festivals**: SXSW *is* the case study — Interactive + Film & TV + Music + Comedy under one badge, one week, one downtown.
- **Official planner/app**: **SXSW GO** — the flagship of festival schedule builders: browse the full lineup, star "My Favorites", sync across devices, toggle full schedule vs My Schedule, badge upload, attendee networking; iOS + Android (developer: Xomo Digital), paired with the schedule.sxsw.com web planner (official sxsw.com/mobile + app-store listings, snippets).
- **Verdict**: **Badge-showcase hybrid where the badge buys the city, not the comedy** — 30 curated shows in 2 walkable venues inside a 4-figure-badge multi-festival; the deciding facts are "open to all badge holders" access and a 2-venue footprint dwarfed by its host.

---

## Briefer dossiers

# Just For Laughs (JFL) empire — research report (2026-09-01)

Evidence tags: **[F]** = page fetched with curl/WebFetch and read directly; **[S]** = search-snippet evidence (not opened; attribute to the named publisher). All dates below verified against at least one tagged source.

## 1. Ownership story — who owns JFL and how stable is it

Timeline:

- **1983** — first Montreal festival; founded by Gilbert Rozon; grew into "the world's largest comedy festival" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **2017–2018** — Rozon (majority stakeholder) resigns amid sexual-misconduct allegations; company put up for sale. **Mar–Jun 2018**: Howie Mandel + ICM Partners, joined by Bell Media and Groupe CH (owner of evenko/L'Équipe Spectra/Bell Centre), acquire Groupe Juste pour rire (https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-and-groupe-ch-join-howie-mandel-and-icm-partners-in-just-for-laughs-ownership-group/ [S], https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/bell-media-just-for-laughs-1.4697493 [S]).
- **Mar 5, 2024** — Groupe Juste pour rire files for creditor protection; the 2024 Montreal **and Toronto** festivals are cancelled outright. Blamed: COVID revenue losses, inflation, shrinking network/streamer spending. Later revealed: **$22.5M in debt plus $3.4M owed to creditors**, and **$800K lost to an email-phishing scheme in 2023** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F], citing CBC; https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **May 29 – Jun 2024** — **ComediHa!** (Quebec City entertainment group founded 1997 by Sylvain Parent-Bédard) acquires the assets — brands Juste pour rire, Just For Laughs, ZooFest, ComedyPro, the Gags, and the audiovisual catalogue — with Quebec Superior Court endorsement (https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/comediha-acquires-assets-of-just-for-laughs-811817974.html [S], https://playbackonline.ca/2024/05/30/comediha-to-acquire-select-just-for-laughs-assets/ [S]).
- **Since then** — the parent group has been renamed **Groupe Juste pour divertir**, HQ in Quebec City; site footers read "©2026 Juste Pour Divertir" (https://www.hahaha.com/fr/public/le-groupe/a-propos-377/ [F]; rename reported by https://sorstu.ca/le-comediha-fest-quebec-devient-le-festival-juste-pour-rire-quebec/ [S]). ComediHa!'s own 25-year-old Quebec City festival was folded into the JPR brand (see Quebec City below); Parent-Bédard keeps ComediHa! as the TV/scripted brand (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]).
- **Summer 2024** — no Montreal festival, but ComediHa staged a stopgap outdoor event, "ComediHa! salue Montréal", with JFL-branded events at Place des Festivals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs [F]). Satellites restarted first (Sydney, Bermuda, Vancouver) (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-comedy-festival-return-australia-bermuda-bankruptcy-1235980376/ [S]).
- **2025 Montreal** — comeback edition **Jul 16–27, 2025** (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/just-for-laughs-returns-2025-1236069413/ [S]). Wikipedia describes it as smaller and "without the usual televised galas" [F]; Montreal Rocks reports gala tapings returned with hosts Fortune Feimster, Roy Wood Jr., Michelle Buteau, Mikey Day (https://montrealrocks.ca/just-for-laughs-returns-with-its-2025-lineup/ [S]) — a "Fortune Feimster Gala" photo from 2025 appears in The Main's 2026 guide (https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide [F]). Official wrap claim: total budget "more than $45 million invested in culture and the economy", sold-out venues, across Montreal + Quebec City (https://quebec.hahaha.com/page/detail/news/juste-pour-rire--just-for-laughs-quebec--announces-2026-festival-dates-74/ [F]).
- **2026 Montreal** — **44th edition, Jul 15–26, back "at full volume": 250 shows, 25 venues, 800+ artists** (The Main [F]) — full detail in §3.

**Stability verdict:** the brand survived receivership intact and is past the danger zone: a full-scale 2026 Montreal edition ran, the 2026 dates were announced a year ahead by press release [F], government partners are visible (Loto-Québec collaboration, Canada/Québec/City-of-Montreal messages on the official site [F]), and 2027 satellite dates are already published (Bermuda Feb 17–20, 2027 [F]; Namur Mar 15–21, 2027 [F]). It is now a regional-champion-owned company (Quebec City, private) rather than a media-conglomerate portfolio piece. Treat Montreal as a durable annual anchor again, with one caveat: the owner is 2 years into the turnaround and audited attendance/scale figures are its own marketing claims.

## 3. Montreal flagship dossier

**Scale & shape (2026, 44th edition, Jul 15–26 — 12 days):** ~250 ticketed shows across ~25 downtown venues, "hundreds" of free outdoor performances, 800+ artists in both official languages (The Main [F]); Place des Arts' page claims ~1,700 artists from 19 countries and "nearly two million visitors" (https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival [F] — marketing copy; the 2M figure includes free outdoor crowds). Jerry Seinfeld added to the 2026 edition (https://deadline.com/2026/05/just-for-laughs-new-shows-jerry-seinfeld-2026-edition-1236882104/ [S]).

**The model — three tiers [all F: The Main, Cult MTL, Place des Arts]:**
1. **Galas**: TV-taping showcase galas at Théâtre Maisonneuve (Place des Arts), host + curated lineup — the festival's signature product.
2. **Ticketed indoor shows**: mostly **curated multi-night showcase runs**, not fringe runs — e.g. The Culture Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19, 7pm), The Nasty Show (Club Soda, Jul 15–19+21, 9:30pm), Brit(ish) (Le Gesù, Jul 21–25), Midnight Surprise (Studio TD, Jul 22–25, midnight), plus premium one-offs (An Evening with David Letterman + Will Arnett, Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, Jul 21, $148–$550) (Cult MTL [F]). Typical run: 1–5 nights.
3. **Free outdoor**: Place des Festivals site open daily from 4pm; 2026's "world's largest comedy cabaret" — DJ at 7, free headline show at 9 nightly (SNL's Sarah Sherman hosting Comedy All-Stars; a free "Weird Al" Yankovic concert) (The Main, Cult MTL [F]).

**Two festivals in one:** francophone **Juste pour rire** and anglophone **Just For Laughs** programming run simultaneously under one org and one website; PdA phrases it "performances in both English and French (under Juste pour rire)" [F]; the official release brands it "Juste pour rire / Just for Laughs" and claims French+English+Spanish programming [F]. The site itself defaults French with an EN toggle; PWA name "JPR Montréal" [F].

**OFF-JFL / Zoofest:** Zoofest (est. 2009, ~125 shows/yr, the emerging-talent/fringe-ish wing; brand acquired in the 2024 sale) has been relaunched as **OFF-JPR** ("OFF JFL" in English media): zoofest.com now lands on the OFFJPR site (https://zoofest.com/ [S-redirect], https://www.offjpr.com/ [F], https://www.mtl.org/en/what-to-do/festivals-and-events/zoofest-alternative-multidisciplinary-festival [S]). 2026 OFF shows ran Jul 16–25 at The Comedy Nest, Café Cléopâtre and Théâtre Sainte-Catherine at $24–32, mostly **one-night** solo/variety sets (Cult MTL [F]). Industry side: **ComedyPRO** conference Jul 22–25 with the **New Faces** showcases (47 performers in 2026) (https://www.thenorwester.ca/just-for-laughs-unveils-2026-new-faces-lineup-as-montreal-festival-showcases-emerging-comedy-talent/ [S]).

**Venue geography:** heavily concentrated in/around the **Quartier des Spectacles**: Place des Festivals (outdoor), Place des Arts halls (Wilfrid-Pelletier, Maisonneuve), Club Soda, Le Gesù, Olympia, MTELUS, Le National, Théâtre St-Denis/Studio St-Denis, Studio TD, Café Cléopâtre, Théâtre Sainte-Catherine — with The Comedy Nest (2313 Ste-Catherine W.) the notable outlier ~3km west (The Main's venue list + Cult MTL addresses [F]).

**Clash reality at peak:** with ~250 shows over 12 days across ~25 venues, peak evenings stack 7:00pm / 9:30pm / midnight slots plus the free 9pm outdoor headliner — real but modest clash density compared to a fringe (tens of simultaneous shows, not hundreds). The repeated 3–5-night runs materially reduce clash pain (a missed showcase usually repeats the next night). 2026 also collided with the FIFA World Cup final (Jul 19) mid-festival (The Main [F]).

## 6. Data reachability (montreal.hahaha.com)

- The whole hahaha.com family runs on a proprietary CMS ("**Nova**", assets served from `nova.justepourdivertir.com`, vendor origin `nova.melliom.com`) [F].
- **Server-rendered shell, client-loaded programme**: the shows/lineup page (`/fr/public/spectacles-1061/`, Toronto `/en/public/shows-87/`) arrives with an **empty** gallery container — `<div data-nova-module='shows' data-nova-filters-options='{...,"pagesize":16,"paginationStyle":"loadmore",...}'>` — populated by JS after load [F].
- **Endpoints (named, all observed in the shipped JS [F])**: pagination `GET {site}/{lang}/templates/{account}/{section}/{page}/{perpage}/{sectionid}/{contentid}/` returning **JSON-wrapped HTML fragments** `{html, pagination}` — not structured data; utility JSON: `/json/getvenue/{id}`, `/json/getspeaker/{id}`, `/json/getvariant/{variant}/{0|1}`, `/json/getmodalcontent/{id}` (verified live: `getmodalcontent/search` returns `{html:...}`; bare `getvenue/` returns `[]`).
- `sitemap.xml` → **503** ("ERREUR : Le système est actuellement indisponible") [F]. Show **detail** pages are fully server-rendered but huge (a Toronto session page: 2.7MB HTML) [F].
- **Listings are ephemeral**: Montreal and Quebec pages were emptied within weeks of the festival ending ("Merci ! À l'année prochaine") — any programme capture must happen **during** the on-sale window. Each site also ships a PWA `/manifest` [F].
- Net: no public structured-data API; programme extraction would mean parsing HTML fragments per city site. (No scraper built, per instructions.)

## 7. Concurrent festivals

- **Montreal, Jul 15–26**: **Fantasia International Film Festival** Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026 (30th) — near-total overlap [S: Wikipedia]; **Nuits d'Afrique** Jul 7–19 (40th, 120+ shows, mostly free) — overlaps the first JFL weekend [S: Cult MTL]; **Montréal Complètement Cirque** Jul 2–12 ends just before [S: mtl.org]; Jazz Fest ends ~Jul 4 (per task brief; not re-verified). Plus the World Cup final Jul 19, 2026 [F: The Main].
- **Toronto, Sep 24–Oct 3**: **TIFF** is Sep 10–20, 2026 [S: Wikipedia] — **no overlap**; JFL Toronto has the city's festival calendar largely to itself.
- **Vancouver, Feb 12–22**: **PuSh Festival** Jan 22–Feb 8, 2026 ends just before [S: pushfestival.ca]; **Chutzpah!** has moved off winter (2026 dates TBC) [S: Stir/vancouversbestplaces] — effectively clash-free.

## 8. Official planner/app

- **No current official mobile app found** for the ComediHa-era festivals (searches surface only websites and listings — NOT FOUND is the finding). What exists instead [F]: each hahaha.com site is an installable **PWA** (`/manifest`, "JPR Montréal") with a logged-in **favourites/wishlist** feature (`novaLoadWishlist()`, "Mes favoris") — i.e., a light on-site planner. Sydney/Singapore sites have no planner at all (mailing-list + external ticket links) [F].
- **Third-party planners**: none found; the gap is filled by editorial guides (The Main, Cult MTL picks) and local listing sites (do604's JFL Vancouver hub, Miss604's schedule posts) [S].

## Fringe-like ↔ showcase-like verdicts

- **Montreal**: firmly **showcase-like** — curated galas, 1–5-night showcase runs and free outdoor headliners concentrated in one district — with OFF-JPR as a small fringe-like annex (~one-night $25 club sets); it is a "pick your nights" festival, not an Edinburgh-style open-access run grid.
- **Satellites (all cities)**: pure **showcase/tour-stop** presenting models — one-to-three nights per act on venue ticketing (Sydney/Singapore fully external), tens not hundreds of shows; planner/clash value is modest everywhere except possibly Vancouver (100+ shows/10 days).

All research is complete. I have fetched primary evidence from every official site, API-level measurements for Leicester and Brighton, and press coverage for the Leicester collapse story. Here is the full report.

---

# Comedy festivals — UK & Ireland (ex-Edinburgh): research report

Evidence markers: **(F)** = fetched directly with curl and read from the bytes; **(S)** = search-snippet evidence attributed to its publisher. Today: 2026-09-01.

## 1. Leicester Comedy Festival — comedy-festival.co.uk

**The headline finding: the organising charity collapsed in August 2026.** The Feb 2026 festival delivered, then the organiser went insolvent owing performers their ticket money. A council-backed successor and a performer-built rival are both aiming at Feb 2027.

- **Organizer**: Big Difference Company Ltd, registered charity 1135167, LCB Depot, 31 Rutland Street, Leicester (F: site footer, https://comedy-festival.co.uk/). **Became insolvent and ceased trading; FRP Advisory Ltd handling liquidation** (F: statement docx dated 26 Aug 2026 linked from homepage, https://irp.cdn-website.com/b436dc39/files/uploaded/Statement+BDC+26_08_2026.docx). Debts exceed £215,000, 100+ creditors, six staff owed >£50k between them (S: Chortle, 22 Aug 2026). It filed a "serious incident report" with the Charity Commission in July 2026 after its own venue was repossessed over unpaid rent (F: Chortle, 5 Aug 2026). Founder Geoff Rowe stepped down after the 2023 festival (30 years); Laura Arends became CEO (S: Niche Magazine / Beyond The Joke).
- **What the 2025 news actually was**: a fundraising appeal — a "Bridging The Gap" Big Give match-funding campaign (S: donate.biggive.org campaign page) — not a sale. **No Gloucester connection exists.** Likely confusion source found: the official homepage carries an auto-generated image alt text reading "Comedian on stage at the Gloucester Comedy Festival" on a 1997 Graham Norton photo (F: homepage HTML). NOT FOUND: any Gloucester-based ownership. The Feb 2026 edition was still run by Big Difference Company (F: BDC statement — "the charity that organised Leicester Comedy Festival").
- **Recurrence**: annual each February since 1994, same city; inaugural edition 40 events / 23 venues / 5,000 tickets; county fringe events in Loughborough, Lutterworth, Foxton, Coalville (F: Wikipedia). Note: Wikipedia's lede says "In 2026 … the festival was cancelled" — **wrong as written**; Chortle's reporting and the BDC statement are unambiguous that the Feb 2026 festival happened and money is owed *from* it (F: both).
- **Scale**: 2026 launch claim: 700+ shows across 81 venues, Feb 4–22 (19 days), plus the UK Kids' Comedy Festival (8th year, 70 shows) (S: Leicester Times; Beyond The Joke; Visit Leicester). Delivered totals for 2026 NOT FOUND. Historic peaks: 870 shows / 72 venues (2019); 780/65 (2016); 560+/64 (2022) (F: Wikipedia stats table). Equity calls it "the largest comedy-only performance festival" (F: Chortle, 5 Aug).
- **Show model**: **open access — "anyone can pay a fee to put on an event"**, registered via Eventotron; 2026 registration window 27 Aug–3 Oct 2025 (S: comedy-festival-takepart.co.uk). Short visits, not Edinburgh runs: the events API shows 1,715 performance-day listings across 753 shows = **avg 2.28 days per show** (F: computed from API).
- **Venue geography**: 81 venues, city-centre core plus county spread (village halls, rugby clubs — e.g. Cosby Village Hall, Old Newtonians RFC) (S: Leicester Times).
- **Clash reality**: genuine. Per the site's own data API: **242 shows on peak day (Sat 21 Feb 2026)**; other Saturdays 186 and 177 (F: `dates` taxonomy counts).
- **Ticketing**: central box office at events.comedy-festival.co.uk (WordPress + official Eventotron plugin) (F); ticket revenue demonstrably flowed through the festival — performers are owed "their ticket money", and venue operator Just The Tonic alone is owed £13k+ in ticket sales (F: Chortle 5 & 11 Aug).
- **Data reachability**: **excellent — open WordPress REST API**: `https://events.comedy-festival.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/events` returns `X-WP-Total: 753` with `dates`/`genres`/`venues`/`seasons` taxonomies (F). Main marketing site (Duda-built) has a minimal sitemap.xml (F).
- **Official app**: existed — homepage nav still links /download-our-app, but the page now 404s as the site is dismantled (F).
- **Aftermath / who runs 2027**: (a) official site banner: "A new Leicester comedy festival will rise in 2027", 3–21 Feb 2027, "Leicester City Council and other partners will provide details of a new model" (F: homepage); the mayor publicly promised a 2027 festival (S: Chortle, 6 Aug). (b) **The Independent Comedy Festival** — founded by comedian Alex Hylton with promoter Colin Bowles (TripleCeePee), same February window, "hundreds of shows in many of the same venues", using ticket platform **TixEvery** which pays comedians directly with the festival never holding box-office money; Mark Watson backing (F: Chortle, 11 Aug). (c) leicesterfringe.com is collecting interest for "future fringe activity" (F). The events API already carries a "Leicester Comedy Festival 2027" season with 2 events (F).
- **Concurrent festivals**: NOT FOUND — no significant overlapping Leicester festival in February.

**Verdict**: **Fringe-like** — open access, 700+ shows / 81 venues / 240-show peak days and a central box office — but built from 1–3-night visits rather than Edinburgh-length runs; and the operating entity is now dead, so 2027 is two rival reboots.

## 2. Brighton Fringe — brightonfringe.org (comedy share + mechanics)

- **Organizer/model**: open-access, 21st year in 2026, "welcoming any artist"; Managing Director Amy Keogh; ~30% of events from Brighton & Hove-based companies (S: Brighton & Hove News, 8 Apr 2026; Visit Brighton). Dates 1–31 May 2026 (F: site; S).
- **Comedy's share of programme**: measured from the site's own API — **394 of 864 events in the live events store are tagged Comedy = 46%**, the largest genre (Theatre 2nd) (F: `/wp-json/wp/v2/events?genres=328` → `X-WP-Total`). Cross-edition genre-tag totals give the same picture: Comedy 1,386 of 3,284 tags = 42% (F: genres taxonomy).
- **Ticketing**: central box office on brightonfringe.org itself — the same Eventotron WordPress plugin as Leicester, with in-page booking (`etron-button-book` / performance picker on each show page) and **Stripe** (stripe.com JS + Stripe Terminal loaded) (F). One site-wide store → single basket structurally (F). Whether the large venues also self-ticket in parallel: NOT VERIFIED this pass.
- **Data reachability**: the what's-on grid is client-rendered by `etron-core.js` — curl gets no show links (F) — but the **WordPress REST API is fully open** (events, genres, venues, dates taxonomies; same shape as Leicester's) (F). sitemap.xml 301s to an index (F).
- **Concurrent-festival cluster — confirmed, all inside the Fringe's May window**: Brighton Festival (curated, 60th edition) **1–25 May 2026**, 105 events (S: Brighton Festival press release; Theatre Weekly); **The Great Escape** (new-music showcase) **13–16 May 2026**, 30+ venues (S: Live Nation; official site). Adjacent but separate: Brighton Comedy Garden (57 Festivals) runs in June/July, outside the cluster (S: Beyond The Joke).
- **Official planner/app**: NOT FOUND (no current app evident).

**Verdict**: **Fringe-like by construction** (open access, central box office, month-long, city-wide) — and comedy is its biggest single genre at ~46% of listings, so roughly "half a Fringe" is a comedy festival.

## 3. Galway Comedy Festival — galwaycomedyfestival.ie

- **Branding**: now plain "Galway Comedy Festival" (GCF26); formerly title-sponsored as the **Vodafone Comedy Carnival Galway** (S: entertainment.ie); zero Vodafone mentions anywhere in the current site bundle (F).
- **Dates/recurrence**: Tue 20 – Mon 26 Oct 2026; full programme reveals 10 Sept 2026; bills itself "Ireland's largest comedy festival" (F: meta description). Annual, October, Galway.
- **Scale (2025, delivered)**: 69 shows, 16 venues, 70+ comedians, Oct 21–27 2025; hub at Pálás Cinema (3 rooms); Róisín Dubh the cornerstone venue with the Bulmers Festival Club (S: RTÉ, 11 Sept 2025). 2026 first names: Dara Ó Briain, Mike Wozniak, Emma Doran (F: bundle strings).
- **Organizer**: formal entity NOT FOUND. Strong site evidence it grew out of the Róisín Dubh venue's operation: the new site migrated "Róisín Dubh ticket access" customer accounts (F: bundle strings), and the programme launch is a Róisín Dubh event (S: roisindubh.net).
- **Show model**: curated ("Carefully Curated Craic" — F: manifest/bundle), one-night headline shows.
- **Clash reality**: modest — ~69 shows over 7 days ≈ 10/day average; a busy Saturday night poses some choice but nothing like Leicester (assessment from S figures).
- **Ticketing**: self-run on the festival site — a custom SPA with its own checkout and customer accounts (routes `/CheckoutSuccess`, `/CustomerAccount`); one Stripe reference in the bundle (vendor NOT CONFIRMED) (F).
- **Data reachability**: poor for scraping-by-page, odd but possible via API: the whole site is a **Base44-built** (AI app-builder) client-rendered SPA; data comes from `base44.app/api/apps/<app-id>/…` (F: bundle). Notably, the HTML shell exposes the operator's admin routes (`/ArtistEditor`, `/Customer360`, `/ClearTestPurchases`) (F).
- **Concurrent festivals**: none in the same week found; Baboró (Ireland's flagship children's arts festival) runs immediately before, ~Oct 8–16/18 2026 (S: baboro.ie/GalwayBayFM); Galway's other majors (GIAF, Film Fleadh) are July.

**Verdict**: **Showcase-like** — a curated headliner week from one promoter lineage with its own central ticketing, not an open-access fringe.

## 4. "Dublin Comedy Festival" — the untangling

- **What's at the URL**: dublinwestcomedyfest.ie **301-redirects to dublincomedyfestival.ie** (F: curl). The site is titled "Dublin Comedy Festival — September 2026" but its own H1 is **"West Dublin's Comedy Takeover"**: "20+ shows across Lucan, Clondalkin, Tallaght, Palmerstown, Clonsilla & Swords" (F: meta + page).
- **What it actually is**: a promoter's suburban pub/hotel circuit — the same few acts rotating venues (Reginald D Hunter ×4 nights, David McSavage ×3, Willa White & Eric Lalor ×4, Al Porter ×3), venues like the Clonsilla Inn, Palmerstown House, Louis Fitzgerald Hotel, plus music nights (Sharon Shannon, Paddy Casey) (F: ticket links). Window matches the tracker: ticket links run **11 Sept – 3 Oct 2026** with strays in July and November (F). Organizer entity NOT FOUND (footer is just "© 2026 Dublin Comedy Festival") (F).
- **Ticketing**: per-event links to **Universe.com** (Ticketmaster's self-serve platform); no central basket (F).
- **So does "the big September thing in Dublin" exist?** No. Dublin's big comedy festival is the **Paddy Power Comedy Festival (formerly Vodafone Comedy Festival), Iveagh Gardens, 23–26 July 2026**, promoted by Aiken Promotions (S: aikenpromotions.com; Visit Dublin). The September slot belongs to **Dublin Fringe Festival, 5–20 Sept 2026** — curated, theatre-led, multi-art (S: fringefest.com) — which is almost certainly the confusion source for a "Dublin festival in September", and is the genuine concurrent festival for anything running then.

**Verdict**: **Showcase-like, barely festival-shaped** — a rebranded rotating pub circuit with per-event ticketing and no clash problem; our tracker's label should point at it with that caveat.

## 5. Aberdeen Comedy Festival — brief

- **Organizer**: Aberdeen Performing Arts (the charity running the Music Hall, His Majesty's, The Lemon Tree); CEO Sharon Burgess quoted as organiser (F: Chortle, 30 May 2026). Earlier editions were associated with Aberdeen Inspired (the city BID) — relationship/handover NOT VERIFIED (S: aberdeeninspired.com page exists).
- **Dates/scale**: Sat 19 Sept – Sun 4 Oct 2026, "three weekends"; venues: APA spaces (Music Hall, Lemon Tree, Tivoli) "and venues across the city"; headliners Russell Howard, Susan Calman, Connor Burns, Larry Dean; expanded late-night and family strands (F: Beyond The Joke; S: Chortle). Total show count NOT FOUND.
- **Model / clash**: curated venue programming; one-night touring shows; a few events per night — no real clash problem (assessment).
- **Ticketing**: central via aberdeenperformingarts.com — **Spektrix** (25 references in page source) (F).
- **Data**: server-rendered listings on the APA site; no dedicated feed found (F). Concurrent festivals: NOT FOUND.

**Verdict**: **Showcase-like** — a venue trust's curated comedy season compressed into three weekends.

## 6. The small-town-weekend model: Wells + Machynlleth

**Wells Comedy Festival — wellscomfest.com**
- Produced by **Plosive Limited** (the podcast production company; Companies House No 10528628) (F: site footer). Established 2015; **2026 was the 10th-anniversary edition (22–24 May)**; 2027 announced for 28–30 May (F: homepage; S: Beyond The Joke).
- Venues: Cedars Hall + Wells Little Theatre (Main House and Rehearsal Room) — a 3-room walkable core in England's smallest city (S: wellscomfest.com/info). Show count NOT FOUND (site's what's-on pages are taken down between editions — F: 404s).
- Model: curated big-name weekend (2026: James Acaster, Sara Pascoe, Nish Kumar, Tim Key, Bridget Christie…) (S: Beyond The Joke). Ticketing: **TicketSource** (S: ticketsource.com/wellscomfest). Site is Squarespace, server-rendered (F).
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a producer's curated weekend.

**Machynlleth Comedy Festival — machcomedyfest.co.uk** *(missing from our tracker — should be added)*
- Organizer: **Little Wander** (F: site copyright + littlewander.co.uk asset domain). **15th year in 2026: May 1–3, 200+ shows** (comedy, theatre, music, kids, Welsh-language strand) taking over the whole town (pop. ~2,000) (F: 2 Apr 2026 news post; nav).
- Has an **official festival app** and "almost sold out" tracking, implying central sales; ticketing vendor NOT FOUND from the site (F).
- Clash: ~65+ shows/day across a tiny town for 3 days — a real clash problem at its scale (computed from F claim).
- **Verdict**: fringe-like in feel (dense parallel town takeover) though single-curator in structure — the strongest UK "small-town takeover" and the model's reference point.

## 7. The single-venue model: Greenwich + Roundhouse — brief

**Greenwich Comedy Garden** *(tracker correction: rebranded — greenwichcomedyfestival.co.uk now redirects to greenwichcomedygarden.co.uk)* (F)
- 15–19 July 2026, five nights, single site: big top at the Old Royal Naval College; "London's biggest comedy festival" with street food/craft beer (F: title/meta/homepage).
- Producer: **57 Festivals** (Will Briggs & Cass Randolph), running it since 2009, 15,000+ ticketholders a year; same team runs the Brighton/Cambridge/Norwich Comedy Gardens (S: Access All Areas; Beyond The Joke).
- Mixed-bill nights of headliners; ticketing via **See Tickets** (F: page source). JS-dependent site (F).
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a promoter's big-top residency.

**Roundhouse Comedy Festival** *(tracker correction: 2026 ran 1–18 Aug, not Aug 23–26)*
- Aug 1–18 2026, one building (Camden's Roundhouse), "biggest programme yet"; curated with production company **Berk's Nest**; headline one-nighters + live podcasts (Lycett, Ryan, Gamble, Skinner, Dropout live shows); 30 £5 tickets per show for under-30s (S: Theatre Weekly; Chortle 21 Apr 2026; BroadwayWorld; Broadsheet). Runs through the Edinburgh Fringe month.
- Ticketing: Roundhouse's own box office on roundhouse.org.uk; platform vendor NOT FOUND on page (F: checked, no Spektrix string).
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — a single-building curated season.

## 8. London Clown Festival — brief

- 10th-anniversary 2026 edition, **30 May – 13 June** (S: London Cheapo, matching our tracker; one report says "through 13 July" — discrepancy noted, not resolved), across two partner venues: **Soho Theatre (Dean St) + Jacksons Lane (Highgate)** — not walkable between (F: official site londonclownfest.online; S: BroadwayWorld). Note the tracker's .co.uk domain is dead (F: connect fail); the live site is londonclownfest.online.
- Niche curated programme (clown/physical comedy, international acts, workshops); organizer entity NOT FOUND (site © since 2017) (F). Ticketing: per-venue box offices, £14–20 (S: BroadwayWorld).
- **Verdict**: showcase-like — curated niche programming hosted inside partner venues' own seasons and ticketing.

## Cross-cutting observations for our product

- **Only Leicester and Brighton have Edinburgh-shaped clash problems** (240 and unmeasured-but-large peak days); Machynlleth has one at miniature scale for one weekend. Everything else is a handful of curated shows per night.
- **Eventotron is the shared open-access substrate**: both Leicester and Brighton run registration *and* their public programme through the same Eventotron WordPress plugin, leaving an **identical open REST API** (`/wp-json/wp/v2/events` + dates/genres/venues taxonomies) on both sites — one adapter would read both.
- **Leicester is a live product opportunity and a live risk**: the incumbent data source works today but its owner is in liquidation; Feb 2027 will be contested between a council-backed reboot and the performer-run Independent Comedy Festival (on TixEvery) — which festival "is" Leicester next year is genuinely open.
- Ticketing vendors seen: Eventotron+Stripe (Leicester, Brighton), Spektrix (Aberdeen), See Tickets (Greenwich), TicketSource (Wells), Universe/Ticketmaster (Dublin West), TixEvery (Independent Comedy Festival, announced), self-built Base44 checkout (Galway). No Red61 outside Edinburgh; no third-party planner tools found for any of these festivals.

## Sources
