# Film festivals with planner-relevant complexity — light survey (2026-09-01)

Legend: [S] = search snippet, [F] = fetched page. Bar = many parallel screenings, multi-venue, public single tickets, ~8+ days, ideally repeat screenings per film.

## Ranked: strongest planner-fits

1. **Berlinale** — the fringe-iest: huge public sale, films screen up to 5×, official planner tool
2. **TIFF** — 11 days, 2–3 public screenings/film, clustered venues, has a *third-party planner* (tiffr)
3. **MIFF Melbourne** — 18 days, 275+ films, ~10 venues, 180k attendees
4. **IFFR Rotterdam** — 11 days, ~480 films, 300k+ admissions, city-wide
5. **SIFF Seattle** — 11 days, most-attended US fest, walkable venue cluster
6. **BFI London** — 12 days, ~240 features, 7 venues, per-event public ticketing
7. **Locarno** — 11 days, 233 films, public tickets, 8,000-seat open-air Piazza
8. **Sundance** — 11 days, $35 public single tickets, two towns (moving to Boulder 2027)
9. **Fantasia Montreal** — 18 days, clustered, overlaps JFL; repeats only selective
10. **Sydney FF** — 12 days, 13 spread venues, Eventival
11. **Busan** — 10 days, 31 screens in 7 theatres, tickets sell out in minutes
12. **IDFA / Hot Docs / Glasgow** — real but second-tier (docs-niche or smaller)

## Per-festival entries

**Berlinale (Berlin)** — Feb 12–22, 2026 (11 days); since 1951. 274 films in 2026 [S berlinale.de press releases]. **Each film screens up to 5× during the festival** [S berlinale.de guidelines] — best repeat-screening property found. Fully public: tickets €9–15 (€20 Palast), released online 3 days before each screening, first-come [S berlin.de, the-berliner.com]; record audience admissions in 2026, "Audience Days" added for 2027 [S berlinale.de]. Venues spread across the city (Potsdamer Platz core + others). Own webshop; official **"My Festival Planner"**: log in, favourite films, build a schedule, subscribe as iCal [S berlinale.de/en/programme/festival-planner.html]. **Planner-fit: the strongest — Fringe-like short-notice ticketing plus genuine repeat-screening optimization.**

**TIFF (Toronto)** — Sep 10–20, 2026 (11 days); since 1976. 200+ films; venues clustered downtown: Lightbox, Roy Thomson Hall, Princess of Wales, Scotiabank, Royal Alexandra, + new 1,200-seat John Bassett Theatre [S nowtoronto.com]. Standard practice ~2 public screenings per film, 2–3 for buzzy titles [S Wikipedia 2009 TIFF, ultimateontario.com]. Major public-audience festival, single tickets + packages. Official app: favourites, calendar mode, in-app ticket purchase [S apps/tiff.net]. **Third-party planner exists: tiffr.com (by Ryan Ming & Mina Mikhail), live for 2026** [S 2026.tiffr.com]; "tiff.to" NOT FOUND. **Planner-fit: excellent — and the one confirmed third-party-planner ecosystem.**

**MIFF (Melbourne)** — Aug 6–23, 2026 (18 days); 74th edition. 275+ films at ~10 venues (ACMI, Capitol, Forum, Cinema Nova, Hoyts Melbourne Central, IMAX, Kino, Astor, Village Crown) across CBD + inner suburbs, plus regional/online arms; 180k+ attendees, claimed top-5 festival audience worldwide [S acmi.net.au, onlymelbourne.com.au]. Repeats: encore screenings added for sell-outs confirmed [S filmink.com.au]; a per-film 2-screening norm NOT FOUND as a stated policy. **Planner-fit: excellent — longest run of the majors, Fringe-like sprawl.**

**IFFR Rotterdam** — Jan 29–Feb 8, 2026 (11 days); since 1972. ~482 films (2025) in cinemas throughout the city incl. galleries/unexpected venues [S iffr.com, Wikipedia]; 300k+ admissions with 2,300 professionals — an audience festival, public single tickets [S Wikipedia]. Repeat screenings: strongly implied by 300k admissions over ~480 titles but a citable per-film statement NOT FOUND (FAQ is JS-rendered [F iffr.com]). **Planner-fit: very strong on scale and public access; repeats unconfirmed.**

**SIFF (Seattle)** — May 7–17, 2026 (11 days); 52nd edition. 203 films from 71 countries [S siff.net, Wikipedia]; self-described largest & most-attended US festival, ~155k attendees [S siff.net history]. Venues 2026: SIFF Cinema Uptown (3 screens), SIFF Cinema Downtown, SIFF Film Center + PACCAR IMAX (Seattle Center) — explicitly "close enough to traverse on foot, bus or monorail" [F Wikipedia 2026 SIFF]. Repeats: "some films screened twice" [S Wikipedia]; historically SIFF ran ~25 days, now 11. Publishes official Letterboxd lineup list [S letterboxd.com/siff]. **Planner-fit: strong — dense clustered multi-screen puzzle, US-public archetype.**

**BFI London FF** — Oct 7–18, 2026 (12 days); 70th edition. ~240 features + 150 shorts typical [S Wikipedia]; 7 London venues centred on BFI Southbank + partner cinemas, some UK-wide/virtual [S bfi.org.uk, Wikipedia]. Event-by-event public ticketing (members' priority tiers, then general sale) via BFI's own box office [S whatson.bfi.org.uk]. Repeats: typically 2–3 screenings per film widely reported but not pinned in snippets — NOT VERIFIED. **Planner-fit: strong; venue spread across central London adds a real travel-time dimension.**

**Locarno** — Aug 5–15, 2026 (11 days); 79th edition. 233 films incl. 103 world premieres [S Wikipedia 79th]. Public tickets: Piazza Grande CHF 33–50, 8,000-seat open-air screen [S pixidia.com]; venues clustered in a small lakeside town. **Planner-fit: good — public and compact, though premiere-driven; smaller optimization space than Berlin/Toronto.**

**Sundance (Park City/SLC → Boulder)** — Jan 22–Feb 1, 2026 (11 days) was the **final Park City edition; moves to Boulder, CO for 2027 (10-year contract; beat Cincinnati & Salt Lake City)** [S hollywoodreporter.com, deadline.com, NPR]. 97 feature/episodic projects in 2026 [S sundance.org]. Public single tickets $35 + queue system at festival.sundance.org; 10-ticket limit; seating first-come even with a ticket [S parkrecord.com, kpcw.org]. Two-town geography (Park City + Salt Lake) = genuinely spread; online at-home program too. Per-film repeat counts NOT FOUND in snippets (premiere + additional screenings is the known pattern but unverified this pass). **Planner-fit: good; 2027 Boulder reboot makes it a moving target worth rechecking.**

**Fantasia (Montreal)** — Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026 (18 days); 30th edition. 125 features + 200+ shorts; venues clustered: Concordia Hall + J.A. de Sève + Cinéma du Musée [S fantasiafestival.com, cultmtl.com]. Genre (horror/fantasy/Asian) with a devoted public audience. Repeats: second screenings for sell-outs and select series, not systematic [S various]. **Planner-fit: moderate-plus — long run and clustered, but mostly single screenings; its real interest is the JFL overlap (below).**

**Sydney FF** — Jun 3–14, 2026 (12 days); 73rd edition. 200–250+ films across **13 venues** spread city-wide (State Theatre flagship + Randwick Ritz, Hayden Orpheum, Dendy Newtown, two Palaces, Event George St, AGNSW, City Recital Hall…) [S sff.org.au, timeout.com]. Ticketing/program platform visibly **Eventival** (vp.eventival.com/sff/2026) [S]. **Planner-fit: good — real geographic spread; repeats NOT VERIFIED.**

**Busan (BIFF)** — Oct 6–15, 2026 (10 days); since 1996. 2025: 329 films on **31 screens in 7 theatres**, 241 in official selection [S Wikipedia 30th BIFF]; venues clustered at Centum City (Busan Cinema Center + CGV + Lotte multiplexes) [S gofarther.blog]. Public tickets — Cinema Center seats "fill within minutes" [S gofarther.blog]. **Planner-fit: good — Asia's public-festival archetype, compact cluster, but scarcity-driven (you take what you can get) more than optimization-driven.**

**IDFA (Amsterdam)** — Nov 12–22, 2026 (11 days); 39th edition. 300+ documentaries, venues across central Amsterdam (Rembrandtplein to West/Zuidoost) [S festival.idfa.nl, iamsterdam.com]; large public audience. **Planner-fit: decent but docs-niche; repeats NOT VERIFIED.**

**Hot Docs (Toronto)** — Apr 23–May 3, 2026 (11 days). 115 docs (80 features + 35 shorts) from 51 countries; Ted Rogers Cinema home base; public tickets, free for students/60+ [S hotdocs.ca, torontolife.com]. **Planner-fit: moderate — public and multi-day but materially smaller than its pre-2024 scale.**

**Glasgow FF** — Feb 25–Mar 8, 2026 (12 days). 126 films; GFT core + ODEON Luxe + scattered special venues [S screen.scot]. **Planner-fit: borderline — public and 12 days, but essentially a 2-venue puzzle.**

## Fails the bar (one line each)

- **Cannes** — no meaningful public ticketing; Palais effectively closed to non-industry for competition [S joinpearl.co]. Fails on public access.
- **Venice** — *does* sell public tickets incl. competition [S labiennale.org, joinpearl.co], but industry/press absorb most seats and it's a premiere-driven Lido event — fails on parallel-choice abundance.
- **SXSW Film** — cut to 7 days in 2026; badge-first ($600+) with badge-holder reservations; single tickets only leftover at select venues [S statesman.com, sxsw.com]. Fails on public-first and duration.
- **Fantastic Fest** — 8 days but single venue (Alamo South Lamar), badge-driven and sold out [S fantasticfest.com, drafthouse.com]. Fails on venues/ticketing.
- **Toronto After Dark** — 5 nights, single venue (Scotiabank), 10 features [S torontoafterdark.com]. Trivial.

## Cross-circuit observations

- **Montreal, confirmed overlap:** Fantasia (Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026) × Just For Laughs (Jul 15–26/27, 2026) — 11 shared days, both clustered near downtown/Quartier des Spectacles [S fantasiafestival.com, cultmtl.com]. The one genuine film×comedy co-planning city.
- **Toronto, adjacent not overlapping:** JFL Toronto 2026 runs Sep 24–Oct 3 vs TIFF Sep 10–20 (2025 likewise: JFL Sep 18–27 after TIFF Sep 4–14) [S streetsoftoronto.com, nowtoronto.com] — same city+month, back-to-back.
- **Austin:** comedy at SXSW is a track inside the same badge, not a separate festival to cross-plan.
- **Melbourne/Edinburgh (prior project knowledge, not re-verified this pass):** MICF runs Mar–Apr vs MIFF in Aug — no overlap; EIFF runs in August alongside the Fringe itself — the closest-to-home film×fringe overlap.
- **Planner tools as a category:** per-festival, thin, and mostly official — Berlinale's My Festival Planner (favourites + iCal) [S berlinale.de], TIFF's app (favourites/calendar/in-app tickets) [S tiff.net], SXSW GO / Eventbase-powered apps [S eventbase.com], Sundance's queue-based site [S kpcw.org]. Only one healthy third-party planner surfaced: **tiffr.com** (TIFF-only, year-per-site, alive for 2026) [S]. Festivals also publish official Letterboxd lineup lists (Berlinale, SIFF) — tracking, not scheduling. **No cross-festival, constraint-based consumer planner found — the fringe-style optimization niche looks unoccupied.**

6. **BFI London** — 12 days, ~240 features, 7 venues, per-event public ticketing

Venues spread across the city (Potsdamer Platz core + others). Own webshop; official **"My Festival Planner"**: log in, favourite films, build a schedule, subscribe as iCal [S berlinale.de/en/programme/festival-planner.html]. **Planner-fit: the strongest — Fringe-like short-notice ticketing plus genuine repeat-screening optimization.**

**TIFF (Toronto)** — Sep 10–20, 2026 (11 days); since 1976. 200+ films; venues clustered downtown: Lightbox, Roy Thomson Hall, Princess of Wales, Scotiabank, Royal Alexandra, + new 1,200-seat John Bassett Theatre [S nowtoronto.com]. Standard practice ~2 public screenings per film, 2–3 for buzzy titles [S Wikipedia 2009 TIFF, ultimateontario.com]. Major public-audience festival, single tickets + packages. Official app: favourites, calendar mode, in-app ticket purchase [S apps/tiff.net]. **Third-party planner exists: tiffr.com (by Ryan Ming & Mina Mikhail), live for 2026** [S 2026.tiffr.com]; "tiff.to" NOT FOUND. **Planner-fit: excellent — and the one confirmed third-party-planner ecosystem.**

**MIFF (Melbourne)** — Aug 6–23, 2026 (18 days); 74th edition. 275+ films at ~10 venues (ACMI, Capitol, Forum, Cinema Nova, Hoyts Melbourne Central, IMAX, Kino, Astor, Village Crown) across CBD + inner suburbs, plus regional/online arms; 180k+ attendees, claimed top-5 festival audience worldwide [S acmi.net.au, onlymelbourne.com.au]. Repeats: encore screenings added for sell-outs confirmed [S filmink.com.au]; a per-film 2-screening norm NOT FOUND as a stated policy. **Planner-fit: excellent — longest run of the majors, Fringe-like sprawl.**

**IFFR Rotterdam** — Jan 29–Feb 8, 2026 (11 days); since 1972. ~482 films (2025) in cinemas throughout the city incl. galleries/unexpected venues [S iffr.com, Wikipedia]; 300k+ admissions with 2,300 professionals — an audience festival, public single tickets [S Wikipedia]. Repeat screenings: strongly implied by 300k admissions over ~480 titles but a citable per-film statement NOT FOUND (FAQ is JS-rendered [F iffr.com]). **Planner-fit: very strong on scale and public access; repeats unconfirmed.**

**SIFF (Seattle)** — May 7–17, 2026 (11 days); 52nd edition. 203 films from 71 countries [S siff.net, Wikipedia]; self-described largest & most-attended US festival, ~155k attendees [S siff.net history]. Venues 2026: SIFF Cinema Uptown (3 screens), SIFF Cinema Downtown, SIFF Film Center + PACCAR IMAX (Seattle Center) — explicitly "close enough to traverse on foot, bus or monorail" [F Wikipedia 2026 SIFF]. Repeats: "some films screened twice" [S Wikipedia]; historically SIFF ran ~25 days, now 11. Publishes official Letterboxd lineup list [S letterboxd.com/siff]. **Planner-fit: strong — dense clustered multi-screen puzzle, US-public archetype.**

**BFI London FF** — Oct 7–18, 2026 (12 days); 70th edition. ~240 features + 150 shorts typical [S Wikipedia]; 7 London venues centred on BFI Southbank + partner cinemas, some UK-wide/virtual [S bfi.org.uk, Wikipedia]. Event-by-event public ticketing (members' priority tiers, then general sale) via BFI's own box office [S whatson.bfi.org.uk]. Repeats: typically 2–3 screenings per film widely reported but not pinned in snippets — NOT VERIFIED. **Planner-fit: strong; venue spread across central London adds a real travel-time dimension.**

**Locarno** — Aug 5–15, 2026 (11 days); 79th edition. 233 films incl. 103 world premieres [S Wikipedia 79th]. Public tickets: Piazza Grande CHF 33–50, 8,000-seat open-air screen [S pixidia.com]; venues clustered in a small lakeside town. **Planner-fit: good — public and compact, though premiere-driven; smaller optimization space than Berlin/Toronto.**

Public single tickets $35 + queue system at festival.sundance.org; 10-ticket limit; seating first-come even with a ticket [S parkrecord.com, kpcw.org]. Two-town geography (Park City + Salt Lake) = genuinely spread; online at-home program too. Per-film repeat counts NOT FOUND in snippets (premiere + additional screenings is the known pattern but unverified this pass). **Planner-fit: good; 2027 Boulder reboot makes it a moving target worth rechecking.**

**Fantasia (Montreal)** — Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026 (18 days); 30th edition. 125 features + 200+ shorts; venues clustered: Concordia Hall + J.A. de Sève + Cinéma du Musée [S fantasiafestival.com, cultmtl.com]. Genre (horror/fantasy/Asian) with a devoted public audience. Repeats: second screenings for sell-outs and select series, not systematic [S various]. **Planner-fit: moderate-plus — long run and clustered, but mostly single screenings; its real interest is the JFL overlap (below).**

**Sydney FF** — Jun 3–14, 2026 (12 days); 73rd edition. 200–250+ films across **13 venues** spread city-wide (State Theatre flagship + Randwick Ritz, Hayden Orpheum, Dendy Newtown, two Palaces, Event George St, AGNSW, City Recital Hall…) [S sff.org.au, timeout.com]. Ticketing/program platform visibly **Eventival** (vp.eventival.com/sff/2026) [S]. **Planner-fit: good — real geographic spread; repeats NOT VERIFIED.**

**Busan (BIFF)** — Oct 6–15, 2026 (10 days); since 1996. 2025: 329 films on **31 screens in 7 theatres**, 241 in official selection [S Wikipedia 30th BIFF]; venues clustered at Centum City (Busan Cinema Center + CGV + Lotte multiplexes) [S gofarther.blog]. Public tickets — Cinema Center seats "fill within minutes" [S gofarther.blog]. **Planner-fit: good — Asia's public-festival archetype, compact cluster, but scarcity-driven (you take what you can get) more than optimization-driven.**

- **SXSW Film** — cut to 7 days in 2026; badge-first ($600+) with badge-holder reservations; single tickets only leftover at select venues [S statesman.com, sxsw.com]. Fails on public-first and duration.

- **Austin:** comedy at SXSW is a track inside the same badge, not a separate festival to cross-plan.
- **Melbourne/Edinburgh (prior project knowledge, not re-verified this pass):** MICF runs Mar–Apr vs MIFF in Aug — no overlap; EIFF runs in August alongside the Fringe itself — the closest-to-home film×fringe overlap.
- **Planner tools as a category:** per-festival, thin, and mostly official — Berlinale's My Festival Planner (favourites + iCal) [S berlinale.de], TIFF's app (favourites/calendar/in-app tickets) [S tiff.net], SXSW GO / Eventbase-powered apps [S eventbase.com], Sundance's queue-based site [S kpcw.org]. **Sydney FF** — Jun 3–14, 2026 (12 days); 73rd edition. 200–250+ films across **13 venues** spread city-wide (State Theatre flagship + Randwick Ritz, Hayden Orpheum, Dendy Newtown, two Palaces, Event George St, AGNSW, City Recital Hall…) [S sff.org.au, timeout.com]. Ticketing/program platform visibly **Eventival** (vp.eventival.com/sff/2026) [S]. **Planner-fit: good — real geographic spread; repeats NOT VERIFIED.**

**Busan (BIFF)** — Oct 6–15, 2026 (10 days); since 1996. 2025: 329 films on **31 screens in 7 theatres**, 241 in official selection [S Wikipedia 30th BIFF]; venues clustered at Centum City (Busan Cinema Center + CGV + Lotte multiplexes) [S gofarther.blog]. Public tickets — Cinema Center seats "fill within minutes" [S gofarther.blog]. **Planner-fit: good — Asia's public-festival archetype, compact cluster, but scarcity-driven (you take what you can get) more than optimization-driven.**

**IDFA (Amsterdam)** — Nov 12–22, 2026 (11 days); 39th edition. 300+ documentaries, venues across central Amsterdam (Rembrandtplein to West/Zuidoost) [S festival.idfa.nl, iamsterdam.com]; large public audience. **Planner-fit: decent but docs-niche; repeats NOT VERIFIED.**

**Hot Docs (Toronto)** — Apr 23–May 3, 2026 (11 days). 115 docs (80 features + 35 shorts) from 51 countries; Ted Rogers Cinema home base; public tickets, free for students/60+ [S hotdocs.ca, torontolife.com]. **Planner-fit: moderate — public and multi-day but materially smaller than its pre-2024 scale.**

**Glasgow FF** — Feb 25–Mar 8, 2026 (12 days). 126 films; GFT core + ODEON Luxe + scattered special venues [S screen.scot]. **Planner-fit: borderline — public and 12 days, but essentially a 2-venue puzzle.**

## Fails the bar (one line each)

- **Cannes** — no meaningful public ticketing; Palais effectively closed to non-industry for competition [S joinpearl.co]. Fails on public access.
- **Venice** — *does* sell public tickets incl. competition [S labiennale.org, joinpearl.co], but industry/press absorb most seats and it's a premiere-driven Lido event — fails on parallel-choice abundance.
- **SXSW Film** — cut to 7 days in 2026; badge-first ($600+) with badge-holder reservations; single tickets only leftover at select venues [S statesman.com, sxsw.com]. Fails on public-first and duration.
- **Fantastic Fest** — 8 days but single venue (Alamo South Lamar), badge-driven and sold out [S fantasticfest.com, drafthouse.com]. Fails on venues/ticketing.
- **Toronto After Dark** — 5 nights, single venue (Scotiabank), 10 features [S torontoafterdark.com]. Trivial.

## Cross-circuit observations

- **Montreal, confirmed overlap:** Fantasia (Jul 16–Aug 2, 2026) × Just For Laughs (Jul 15–26/27, 2026) — 11 shared days, both clustered near downtown/Quartier des Spectacles [S fantasiafestival.com, cultmtl.com]. The one genuine film×comedy co-planning city.
- **Toronto, adjacent not overlapping:** JFL Toronto 2026 runs Sep 24–Oct 3 vs TIFF Sep 10–20 (2025 likewise: JFL Sep 18–27 after TIFF Sep 4–14) [S streetsoftoronto.com, nowtoronto.com] — same city+month, back-to-back.
- **Austin:** comedy at SXSW is a track inside the same badge, not a separate festival to cross-plan.
- **Melbourne/Edinburgh (prior project knowledge, not re-verified this pass):** MICF runs Mar–Apr vs MIFF in Aug — no overlap; EIFF runs in August alongside the Fringe itself — the closest-to-home film×fringe overlap.
- **Planner tools as a category:** per-festival, thin, and mostly official — Berlinale's My Festival Planner (favourites + iCal) [S berlinale.de], TIFF's app (favourites/calendar/in-app tickets) [S tiff.net], SXSW GO / Eventbase-powered apps [S eventbase.com], Sundance's queue-based site [S kpcw.org]. Only one healthy third-party planner surfaced: **tiffr.com** (TIFF-only, year-per-site, alive for 2026) [S]. ## Key Timeline and Facts

Effective December 12, 2019, Eventbrite removed public access to the Event Search API (GET /v3/events/search/). However, Eventbrite creators' API keys were whitelisted to access this API until 11:59 pm PT on February 20, 2020.

## Reason for Removal

Eventbrite removed the Event Search API to further improve the platform and allow them to support more creators and their events, stating that allowing public access to this API was impacting their platform and the service they provide to creators and attendees.

## Current State (2024)

As of August 2024, there is no public API endpoint for searching events across the entire Eventbrite platform. Eventbrite recommends using alternative APIs instead: retrieving an event by ID, listing events by venue, or listing events by organization.

Eventbrite's API is not a public event-discovery API since search was deprecated, and there is no public search endpoint, so plans that relied on discovering arbitrary public events will not work.

## API Overview

The GetYourGuide Partner API provides access to GetYourGuide's marketplace for tours and activities, with a RESTful interface using JSON format. Access is secured via SSL and an API access token.

GetYourGuide offers multiple levels of API access with different requirements:

Minimum 100,000 monthly visits (for websites) or total downloads (for app integrations)

Minimum traffic of 1 million visits and at least 300 monthly bookings (for partners who already have Basic API access)

## The film adjacency — surveyed light, on the owner's direction

Film festivals run on the same two axes as comedy, and the owner asked for
the planner-complex ones flagged without deep research (2026-09-01; each
entry is one look, not a dossier). The bar: multi-venue, many parallel
screenings, public single tickets, ~8+ days, ideally **repeat screenings**
— the recurrence property that turns triage into optimization.

The strongest planner-fits, ranked:

1. **Berlinale** (Berlin, 11 days each Feb) — film's closest thing to a
   fringe: 274 films in 2026, **each screening up to five times**
   ([its own entry guidelines](https://www.berlinale.de/en/film-entry/guidelines/general-guidelines.html)),
   fully public tickets at €9–15 released online three days before each
   screening, venues spread across the city — and an official
   [**"My Festival Planner"**](https://www.berlinale.de/en/programme/festival-planner.html)
   (favourites → schedule → iCal), the most planner-shaped official tool
   seen in any circuit this wiki covers.
2. **TIFF** (Toronto, 11 days each Sep) — 200+ films, ~2 public screenings
   each, clustered downtown venues, an official app with favourites and
   in-app tickets — and the only healthy **third-party festival planner
   found in film**: [tiffr.com](https://2026.tiffr.com/), TIFF-only, one
   site per year, alive for 2026.
3. **MIFF** (Melbourne, **18 days** each Aug) — 275+ films, ~10 venues,
   180,000+ attendees ([ACMI](https://www.acmi.net.au/whats-on/miff-2026/))
   — the longest major, in a city we already track for MICF (different
   months; no overlap).
4. **IFFR Rotterdam** (11 days, ~480 films, 300k+ admissions citywide),
   **SIFF Seattle** (11 days, 203 films, a walkable multi-screen cluster,
   the most-attended US festival), **BFI London** (12 days, ~240 features,
   7 venues), **Locarno** (11 days, public, an 8,000-seat open-air piazza),
   **Sundance** (11 days, $35 public single tickets, two towns — **moving
   to Boulder for 2027** on a ten-year deal, per
   [THR](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/sundance-boulder-colorado-move-from-park-city-1236135102/) —
   the census's rare city *move*), **Sydney FF** (12 days, 13 spread
   venues, on Eventival), **Busan** (10 days, 329 films on 31 screens in
   one cluster, sell-out-in-minutes scarcity).
5. Second tier: Fantasia (Montreal, 18 days, clustered, selective repeats),
   IDFA, Hot Docs, Glasgow.

Failing the bar, for the record: **Cannes** (no meaningful public
ticketing), **Venice** (public tickets exist but premiere-driven, industry
absorbs the seats), **SXSW Film** (badge-first, cut to 7 days), **Fantastic
Fest** (one venue, badge-driven).

What the light pass established for the taxonomy: **repeat screenings are
the norm at the big public film festivals and absent at the premiere
festivals** — the same recurrence split as comedy's fringe-vs-showcase; the
**Fantasia × JFL overlap gives Montreal eleven shared days** of film ×
comedy co-planning (the one such city found); and film's third-party
planner category is one TIFF-only specimen — as empty as comedy's outside
Edinburgh. A future film expansion would start at Berlinale/TIFF/MIFF, and
each needs the deep pass this survey deliberately skipped.

## Festival trackers

+# The comedy-festival circuit
+
+The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
+and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
+This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
+EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
+the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
+genre. Compiled once, refined in place.
+
+Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
+[festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/](../festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh/README.md)
+owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
+pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
+the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
+reachability. Planner-type competitors found along the way live on
+[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).
+
+## Key insights
+
+- Only ~8 of 85 census festivals are fringe-shaped. Most of the circuit is one-night showcases with nothing to schedule.
+- MICF is the southern Edinburgh — 803 shows, 9,164 performances, open registration — with unauthenticated JSON APIs.
+- Leicester's operator went bust in Aug 2026 owing performers ticket money. Feb 2027 is two rival reboots.
+- Nearly everything is annual in the same city, but brands churn: JFL survived receivership, Netflix Is A Joke is biennial.
+- Recurrence decides the planning problem: a Fringe show plays ~14 times, a US festival show plays once — clashes there are terminal.
+- Leicester and Brighton share one platform (Eventotron) and identical open APIs — one adapter reads both.
+- No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists. The best tracker is one journalist's hand-kept page.
+
