- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- static-site-releases: The release standard every static-site repo of ours ships — the date-anchored version scheme, release-on-push, the explicit publish set, .github/site.config, the vendored workflows, the Pages deploy, and the setup a new site repo needs. Use when setting up a site repo, changing or debugging its release pipeline or site.config, when asked to "bump version" on a site repo, or when a static-website check fires.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

content.content:
142	~1,600 companies (about 90% French). Average auditorium fill was **54%** —
143	the same "too much supply chasing too little attention" economics as the Fringe.
144	
145	If any city is EdFringeNow's second market on structure alone, it is this one.
146	The blocker is not the bar — every dimension clears — it is that the entire
147	corpus is in French.
148	
149	#### The rest of the clear tier
150	
151	- **Perth, Australia — FRINGE WORLD** (Jan–Feb; open access). The third-largest
152	  fringe on the planet: **600+ shows across 110 venues** advertised ahead of the
153	  2026 edition (21 Jan–15 Feb 2026), ~3,000 artists, off **256,000 tickets**
154	  sold in 2025. That 2026 edition has since run and closed (this repo's clock
155	  is now 2 Aug 2026): its own final report counts **599 events**, more than
156	  3,000 artists, **nearly 500,000 attendees**, and **$10.9m spent at the Box
157	  Office** ($8.34m paid to artists and venues) — up from 2025's 570 events /
158	  492,369 attendees / $10.78m box office. Note "attendees" and "tickets sold"
159	  are not the same metric (the 256,000 figure is a narrower paid-ticket count);
160	  both are kept because neither source reconciles them into one number.
161	- **Brighton, UK** (1–31 May; open access). Around **400,000 in-person
162	  attendances**, with over 30% of events from Brighton & Hove companies. English
163	  language, UK ticketing conventions — the cheapest possible second market.
164	  Comedy share and its open Eventotron API are on
165	  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md).
166	- **Melbourne — MICF** (Mar–Apr; open registration). The strongest
167	  fringe-shaped candidate found anywhere outside the fringe network itself:
168	  803 shows, 9,164 performances, 26 days, with open JSON endpoints.
169	  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md) owns the
170	  detail; it sits in this tier on every dimension.
171	- **Montreal in July** (festival season). Festival International de Jazz de
172	  Montréal (25 Jun – 4 Jul 2026) puts **350+ shows** and 3,000 performers in
173	  front of a claimed 2m+ guests; Just For Laughs (15–26 Jul 2026) runs **250
174	  shows across 25 downtown venues** and 800+ artists **in both official
175	  languages**, and the Fantasia film festival overlaps JFL for eleven shared
176	  days. Concentrated in the Quartier des Spectacles, so reachability is real.
177	  Bilingual by default — the first candidate that forces the localization
178	  question. On the bar it clears as a *stacked season* rather than one
179	  festival, which multiplies the data-source cost (each festival is separately
180	  run). (Corrected 2026-09-01: this entry called JFL "the world's largest
181	  comedy festival". That label is JFL marketing that survives on attendance
182	  counting its free outdoor crowds; by ticketed shows it is roughly a third of
183	  Melbourne's 803, and the company behind it went through 2024 receivership
184	  and a 2024 cancellation before its 2026 relaunch — see
185	  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md), which now
186	  owns the comedy-festival detail for this and every other comedy entry.)
187	- **Makhanda (Grahamstown), South Africa — National Arts Festival** (late
188	  June–July; open-access fringe beside a curated core). **270+ productions** on
189	  the main programme in 2026 plus a Fringe of **200+ new works**, in a town
190	  small enough that the visitor-to-resident ratio may be the most extreme of
191	  any candidate here. Clears the bar at the small end — abundance is relative
192	  to the visitor's capacity, and eleven days of ~470 productions clears it.
193	- **Sibiu, Romania — FITS** (19–28 June 2026; curated season). **800+ events**
194	  in ten days in a small old town; one of Europe's largest performing-arts
195	  festivals. Curated rather than open access, but 80 events a day produces
196	  real simultaneity — the mechanism differs, the bar clears.
197	- **The film festivals that clear it** — Berlinale above all (274 films, each
198	  screened up to five times, public tickets €9–15), then TIFF and MIFF.
199	  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md)'s film
200	  adjacency owns the detail and citations; they belong on this page's map
201	  because each is an anchored, publicly-ticketed, repeat-screening city event.
202	
203	### Near misses — one dimension short
204	
205	- **Milan — Salone del Mobile / Fuorisalone** (April; curated core + off). The
206	  purest non-theatre version of the Edinburgh dynamic: a ticketed trade fair at
207	  Rho with 1,900+ exhibitors, plus **1,100+ events listed on the official
208	  Fuorisalone guide (1,300+ across the city) spread over 16 districts** and
209	  **500,000+ visitors**. Brera alone carried 320 events across 217 showrooms.
210	  Installations run for the week rather than to performance times, so
211	  simultaneity (dimension 3) never bites: the *scheduling* problem is weaker
212	  than the *reachability* problem — which is the half of the product the Now
213	  page serves.
214	- **Charleston, SC — Spoleto Festival USA / Piccolo Spoleto** (late May–June;
215	  curated core + open companion). Piccolo Spoleto 2026 offered **250 events**,
216	  190 of them produced by independent arts and community groups, 113 free — a
217	  deliberately open companion to a curated core, at a scale where a planner is
218	  plausible but not urgent. Short of the bar on abundance (dimension 2).
219	- **Toronto, Canada** (30 Jun – 12 Jul 2026; lottery-selected fringe). **123
220	  shows**, selected by *lottery* rather than pure open access — a different
221	  supply mechanism, and small enough that overwhelm is not really the user's
222	  problem. Short on abundance (dimension 2).
223	- **Galway, Ireland — GIAF** (13–26 July 2026; curated season). Fourteen days,
224	  audiences well in excess of 200,000, in a small city fully consumed by it.
225	  Programme size unassessed — provisionally here until a show count is cited.
226	
227	### Fails the bar, instructively
228	
229	- **Salzburg, Austria** (17 Jul – 30 Aug 2026). **208 performances** across
230	  opera, drama and concerts. The town is overwhelmed, but the programme is
231	  curated, expensive and elite — 208 performances is a brochure, not an
232	  overwhelm problem. The boundary case this page keeps on purpose: *city
233	  swarming* alone fails abundance (dimension 2).
234	- **Venice — Biennale Arte** (9 May – 22 Nov 2026). **100 national
235	  participations** — 29 in the Giardini, 25 in the Arsenale and **46 scattered
236	  across the city** — plus **31 collateral events**. A months-long run means
237	  opening hours, not performance times: fails time-boxing (1) and simultaneity
238	  (3) at once. **Kassel — Documenta** (every five years, 100 days) fails the
239	  cadence half of recurrence; the roving **Manifesta** fails the anchor half.
240	- **Cannes**, **SXSW Austin** (March). Both convert a city into temporary
241	  venues at high density with genuine clash-resolution problems, but both are
242	  trade/badge-driven rather than public-audience-driven — failing open access
243	  (dimension 6) — and SXSW already ships its own scheduling tool.
244	
245	### The unassessed tail
246	
247	Also in the fringe network and unassessed: **Prague**, **Dublin**, **Winnipeg**,
248	**Orlando**, **Minnesota**, **Wellington**, **Camden**, **Melbourne Fringe**.
249	**Miami Beach — Art Basel plus satellite fairs** (December) is the same
250	curated-core-plus-off shape as Milan, unassessed.
251	
252	## Where Edinburgh is still singular
253	
254	Two findings cut against expanding, and both should be said plainly:
255	
256	- **Nothing is close on density.** Edinburgh's Fringe alone is ~2.6× Adelaide on
257	  show count (4,206 vs 1,648, both 2026) and ~2.4× on tickets (2.6m in 2025 vs
258	  1.08m in 2026 — the newest full-year figure each publishes), in a smaller, more
259	  walkable centre, and it overlaps five other major festivals. The overwhelm the
260	  product exists to solve is genuinely worst here. (Corrected 2026-08-09: the
261	  Edinburgh side of this comparison was 3,649, the 4 June programme-launch
262	  snapshot, against Adelaide's delivered total — an unfair comparison that
263	  *understated* the gap, at ~2.2×. Both sides are now delivered figures. The
264	  general trap is worth carrying to every candidate on this page: **a
265	  festival's launch announcement and its delivered programme are different
266	  numbers**, and this page's tail is built almost entirely from launch
267	  announcements.)
268	- **Edinburgh is the only candidate with an official aggregation layer.** The
269	  Edinburgh Festivals Listings API is a free API over the official listings
270	  database for all **11** Edinburgh festivals, carrying over **640,000
271	  performances**, with `events` and `venues` endpoints and a self-service access
272	  key. Its coverage, fields, licence terms and the two edges that matter (it is
273	  **availability-blind**, and its no-redistribution clause sits awkwardly with
274	  this repo's committed static data) are worked through on
275	  [festival-season/](../festival-season/README.md) and not repeated here. The
276	  point for *this* page is comparative: **no equivalent single-source feed was
277	  found for Adelaide, Avignon, Perth, Milan or Montreal** — those are
278	  per-festival scrapes or nothing. That asymmetry, not language, is the real cost
279	  of a second city.

~1,600 companies (about 90% French). Average auditorium fill was **54%** —
the same "too much supply chasing too little attention" economics as the Fringe.

If any city is EdFringeNow's second market on structure alone, it is this one.
The blocker is not the bar — every dimension clears — it is that the entire
corpus is in French.

#### The rest of the clear tier

- **Perth, Australia — FRINGE WORLD** (Jan–Feb; open access). The third-largest
  fringe on the planet: **600+ shows across 110 venues** advertised ahead of the
  2026 edition (21 Jan–15 Feb 2026), ~3,000 artists, off **256,000 tickets**
  sold in 2025. That 2026 edition has since run and closed (this repo's clock
  is now 2 Aug 2026): its own final report counts **599 events**, more than
  3,000 artists, **nearly 500,000 attendees**, and **$10.9m spent at the Box
  Office** ($8.34m paid to artists and venues) — up from 2025's 570 events /
  492,369 attendees / $10.78m box office. Note "attendees" and "tickets sold"
  are not the same metric (the 256,000 figure is a narrower paid-ticket count);
  both are kept because neither source reconciles them into one number.
- **Brighton, UK** (1–31 May; open access). Around **400,000 in-person
  attendances**, with over 30% of events from Brighton & Hove companies. English
  language, UK ticketing conventions — the cheapest possible second market.
  Comedy share and its open Eventotron API are on
  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md).
- **Melbourne — MICF** (Mar–Apr; open registration). The strongest
  fringe-shaped candidate found anywhere outside the fringe network itself:
  803 shows, 9,164 performances, 26 days, with open JSON endpoints.
  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md) owns the
  detail; it sits in this tier on every dimension.
- **Montreal in July** (festival season). Festival International de Jazz de
  Montréal (25 Jun – 4 Jul 2026) puts **350+ shows** and 3,000 performers in
  front of a claimed 2m+ guests; Just For Laughs (15–26 Jul 2026) runs **250
  shows across 25 downtown venues** and 800+ artists **in both official
  languages**, and the Fantasia film festival overlaps JFL for eleven shared
  days. Concentrated in the Quartier des Spectacles, so reachability is real.
  Bilingual by default — the first candidate that forces the localization
  question. On the bar it clears as a *stacked season* rather than one
  festival, which multiplies the data-source cost (each festival is separately
  run). (Corrected 2026-09-01: this entry called JFL "the world's largest
  comedy festival". That label is JFL marketing that survives on attendance
  counting its free outdoor crowds; by ticketed shows it is roughly a third of
  Melbourne's 803, and the company behind it went through 2024 receivership
  and a 2024 cancellation before its 2026 relaunch — see
  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md), which now
  owns the comedy-festival detail for this and every other comedy entry.)
- **Makhanda (Grahamstown), South Africa — National Arts Festival** (late
  June–July; open-access fringe beside a curated core). **270+ productions** on
  the main programme in 2026 plus a Fringe of **200+ new works**, in a town
  small enough that the visitor-to-resident ratio may be the most extreme of
  any candidate here. Clears the bar at the small end — abundance is relative
  to the visitor's capacity, and eleven days of ~470 productions clears it.
- **Sibiu, Romania — FITS** (19–28 June 2026; curated season). **800+ events**
  in ten days in a small old town; one of Europe's largest performing-arts
  festivals. Curated rather than open access, but 80 events a day produces
  real simultaneity — the mechanism differs, the bar clears.
- **The film festivals that clear it** — Berlinale above all (274 films, each
  screened up to five times, public tickets €9–15), then TIFF and MIFF.
  [comedy-festival-circuit/](../comedy-festival-circuit/README.md)'s film
  adjacency owns the detail and citations; they belong on this page's map
  because each is an anchored, publicly-ticketed, repeat-screening city event.

### Near misses — one dimension short

- **Milan — Salone del Mobile / Fuorisalone** (April; curated core + off). The
  purest non-theatre version of the Edinburgh dynamic: a ticketed trade fair at
  Rho with 1,900+ exhibitors, plus **1,100+ events listed on the official
  Fuorisalone guide (1,300+ across the city) spread over 16 districts** and
  **500,000+ visitors**. Brera alone carried 320 events across 217 showrooms.
  Installations run for the week rather than to performance times, so
  simultaneity (dimension 3) never bites: the *scheduling* problem is weaker
  than the *reachability* problem — which is the half of the product the Now
  page serves.
- **Charleston, SC — Spoleto Festival USA / Piccolo Spoleto** (late May–June;
  curated core + open companion). Piccolo Spoleto 2026 offered **250 events**,
  190 of them produced by independent arts and community groups, 113 free — a
  deliberately open companion to a curated core, at a scale where a planner is
  plausible but not urgent. Short of the bar on abundance (dimension 2).
- **Toronto, Canada** (30 Jun – 12 Jul 2026; lottery-selected fringe). **123
  shows**, selected by *lottery* rather than pure open access — a different
  supply mechanism, and small enough that overwhelm is not really the user's
  problem. Short on abundance (dimension 2).
- **Galway, Ireland — GIAF** (13–26 July 2026; curated season). Fourteen days,
  audiences well in excess of 200,000, in a small city fully consumed by it.
  Programme size unassessed — provisionally here until a show count is cited.

### Fails the bar, instructively

- **Salzburg, Austria** (17 Jul – 30 Aug 2026). **208 performances** across
  opera, drama and concerts. The town is overwhelmed, but the programme is
  curated, expensive and elite — 208 performances is a brochure, not an
  overwhelm problem. The boundary case this page keeps on purpose: *city
  swarming* alone fails abundance (dimension 2).
- **Venice — Biennale Arte** (9 May – 22 Nov 2026). **100 national
  participations** — 29 in the Giardini, 25 in the Arsenale and **46 scattered
  across the city** — plus **31 collateral events**. A months-long run means
  opening hours, not performance times: fails time-boxing (1) and simultaneity
  (3) at once. **Kassel — Documenta** (every five years, 100 days) fails the
  cadence half of recurrence; the roving **Manifesta** fails the anchor half.
- **Cannes**, **SXSW Austin** (March). Both convert a city into temporary
  venues at high density with genuine clash-resolution problems, but both are
  trade/badge-driven rather than public-audience-driven — failing open access
  (dimension 6) — and SXSW already ships its own scheduling tool.

### The unassessed tail

Also in the fringe network and unassessed: **Prague**, **Dublin**, **Winnipeg**,
**Orlando**, **Minnesota**, **Wellington**, **Camden**, **Melbourne Fringe**.
**Miami Beach — Art Basel plus satellite fairs** (December) is the same
curated-core-plus-off shape as Milan, unassessed.

## Where Edinburgh is still singular

Two findings cut against expanding, and both should be said plainly:

- **Nothing is close on density.** Edinburgh's Fringe alone is ~2.6× Adelaide on
  show count (4,206 vs 1,648, both 2026) and ~2.4× on tickets (2.6m in 2025 vs
  1.08m in 2026 — the newest full-year figure each publishes), in a smaller, more
  walkable centre, and it overlaps five other major festivals. The overwhelm the
  product exists to solve is genuinely worst here. (Corrected 2026-08-09: the
  Edinburgh side of this comparison was 3,649, the 4 June programme-launch
  snapshot, against Adelaide's delivered total — an unfair comparison that
  *understated* the gap, at ~2.2×. Both sides are now delivered figures. The
  general trap is worth carrying to every candidate on this page: **a
  festival's launch announcement and its delivered programme are different
  numbers**, and this page's tail is built almost entirely from launch
  announcements.)
- **Edinburgh is the only candidate with an official aggregation layer.** The
  Edinburgh Festivals Listings API is a free API over the official listings
  database for all **11** Edinburgh festivals, carrying over **640,000
  performances**, with `events` and `venues` endpoints and a self-service access
  key. Its coverage, fields, licence terms and the two edges that matter (it is
  **availability-blind**, and its no-redistribution clause sits awkwardly with
  this repo's committed static data) are worked through on
  [festival-season/](../festival-season/README.md) and not repeated here. The
  point for *this* page is comparative: **no equivalent single-source feed was
  found for Adelaide, Avignon, Perth, Milan or Montreal** — those are
  per-festival scrapes or nothing. That asymmetry, not language, is the real cost
  of a second city.

content.content:
faq 200
Home page
Frequently Asked Question
I want to watch multiple films during the festival- how can I get the best price?
In order to enjoy discounted prices- you can purchase our
multiple passes combinations
before you purchase the tickets.
Please notice that while purchasing a topical pass (like Haifa Docu, which includes the documentary films at this year's festival)- you will have to choose your desired screenings.
I purchased a multiple pass and i have a few open tickets left. how can I order them on line?
To set up open tickets with an already purchased multiple pass, just go to the "Buy tickets" page for the screening you want to order tickets to.
If you are not already connected to the site, click on the "התחברות מנויים" button above the hall map.
* Connect via email and password (there is also a possibility to connect using a one-time code - just enter a mobile phone number and you'll receive a one-time password via SMS message)
*Click in the button “מימוש כרטיסיית 10 כניסות” and then select your seat at the screening.
*At the bottom of the page, click the red button "Add to Basket"
Attention, your order is not yet finished
*Click on the red button “Continue”.
Check to see if your personal information is correct and proceed to the bottom of the page. Click on the red button “Continue”.
*Your order has been successfully received!
The appearance of the  Purchase Confirmation on the next screen confirms your order, the tickets will now be sent automatically to your e-mail address.
How do I get my tickets?
A digital copy of the tickets will be sent automatically ti the e-mail address you filled while purchasing.
An automated text message will be sent to your cell phone the day before each screening with a link to the digital tickets- so you can show them straight the the ushers at the entrance. There is no need to print the tickets.
If you'd like you can of course always visit us at the physical box office and ask to print your tickets.
I ordered tickets as part of my multiple pass and I'd like to make some changes
Not a problem!
Just contact our box office by dialing *9300 and our sales representatives will gladly help with any change you would like to do.
I got late to a screening. can I still enter?
Your selected seats will be reserved until the start time of the screening. In case you are running late, you will still be allowed to enter the screening up to 15 minutes after the screening's start time- but will be directed to the available seats ny our ushers. After 15 minutes we won't allow further entrance.
I ordered tickets with my multiple pass online but didn't get them by mail!
When you order a multiple pass and choose your desired screenings at the same time- you won't get the tickets attached to the e-mail at the end of your purchase- but by an automated text messaged to your cell phone the day before your screening.
The end of the festival is near and I didn't got around to using all the tickets in my multiple pass
Mind that you won't be able to use your ticket reserves that might be left in your multiple pass after the end of the festival and no refund will be issued for usused tickets.
I have another question!
You can always contact our customer service representatives by dialing *9300 or by the

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Paris 2024's official ticket resale platform:

## Launch and Platform Details

The Paris 2024 Organising Committee launched the official Games ticket app "Paris 2024 tickets", which was made available on May 15, 2024.

## Resale Features

The app allows users to download, transfer and even resell tickets for the Paralympic and Olympic Games. This is the only official and authorised resale channel: the resale is completely transparent for both the seller and the purchaser.

## Pricing Structure

Buyers can purchase the ticket at its initial price (face value), plus a processing fee (5 per cent of the initial price for the seller, 10 per cent for the purchaser).

## Resale Timeline

Resale will be possible up to 12 hours before the start of the session concerned.

The platform was designed to prevent scalping and fraud by ensuring all resales occurred at face value with transparent fees, making it easier for genuine fans to purchase tickets at fair prices.

לאחר רכישת הכרטיסיה, היכנסו לעמוד הסרט בו תרצו לצפות, בחרו את ההקרנה הרצויה ולחצו על כפתור הרכישה. לאחר מכן לחצו על כפתור מימוש מנוי / קוד הטבה, בחרו במימוש מנוי והקלידו את תעודת הזהות שהזנתם בעת רכישת הכרטיסיה, ואת מספר הכרטיסיה שקיבלתם בתום תהליך רכישת הכרטיסיה. המערכת תזהה את הכרטיסיה שברשותכם ותעדכן את סכום התשלום ל-0 ש’‘ח. לאחר מכן, לחצו על הכפתור ‘‘הבא’‘. כעת מלאו את פרטיכם האישיים ולחצו על ‘‘סיים הזמנה’‘. את הכרטיסים שהזמנתם תקבלו בהודעת טקסט ובדואר האלקטרוני שהזנתם במהלך הרכישה.

## Animix 2026 - International Animation, Comics & Caricature Festival

Animix, the annual Israeli International Animation, Comics, & Caricature Festival will take place from August 4 – 8, 2026, at the Tel Aviv Cinematheque. Now in its 26th edition, the festival showcases a diverse array of outstanding local and international animation, provides a platform for an emerging generation of cartoonists and animators, and reflects and responds to the complex reality in Israel.

### Festival Highlights

The festival offers five days of funny, thought-provoking, and visually stunning exhibitions, performances, film screenings, workshops, and meetings with leading Israeli and international artists.

This year's program reflects the fraught political and social climate in Israel, with artists responding to elections, war, trauma, extremism, and the events of October 7 through satire, personal storytelling, and animation.

## Overview

The Icon Festival (פסטיבל אייקון in Hebrew) is an Israeli science fiction and fantasy fan convention held annually in Tel Aviv during the Sukkot holiday in September–October. Established in 1997 (first named Sector972), it is the largest convention held in Israel.

## 2026 Festival Details

The Icon Festival is held every year in Sukkoth (September/October various dates), with the 2026 festival scheduled for the Eshkol Pais site in Tel Aviv during the Sukkoth holiday.

## Festival Program

The festival's programme features film screenings, lectures, panels, workshops, original theatre productions, the occasional poetry jam, and competitions for the Israeli Science-Fiction and Fantasy loving (or curious) public to enjoy. The three days of the festival include original productions, legend beer site, funny games with the participation of the audience, science and academic lectures, exciting lectures and reading club.

## Organization

Icon is produced by group of non-profit organizations that work all year round to promote the fandoms and creators of science fiction, fantasy and role-playing games, and to strive to make these genres more accessible to their audience.

# Festmaxxing fit assessment: non-festival environments

Definition dimensions: (1) time-boxed week+, (2) abundance, (3) simultaneity, (4) venue spread, (5) repeat chances, (6) open per-event access, (7) anchored recurrence, (8) city context. [F] = page fetched and read; [S] = search snippet only.

## 1. Fashion weeks (Paris, Milan, NYC, London) — the owner's direct question

- Official NYFW (CFDA calendar) Feb 2026: Feb 11–16, 6 days; 60+ runway shows and presentations on the official schedule — https://cfda.com/news/view-the-preliminary-official-nyfw-february-2026-schedule/ / https://wwd.com/fashion-news/designer-luxury/cfda-preliminary-official-new-york-fashion-week-schedule-february-2026-1238452346/ [S]
- Access to official CFDA designer shows (Ralph Lauren, Michael Kors, Tory Burch...) is limited to invitation lists and press credentials; runway seats go to press, buyers, industry professionals — https://runway7fashion.com/is-new-york-fashion-week-open-to-the-public/ [S]
- What the public CAN buy in NYC: paid showcases run by independent producers alongside the official week (Runway 7, The Bureau, hiTechMODA, Art Hearts Fashion sell GA/VIP tickets to their own shows, separate from the CFDA schedule) — https://runway7fashion.com/new-york-fashion-week-tickets-public-vs-invite/ [S]
- Paris Fashion Week womenswear SS27 (Sep 28–Oct 6, 9 days): 68 shows + 33 presentations on the official FHCM calendar — https://www.complex.com/style/a/will-lavin/paris-fashion-week-ss27-women-schedule-2026 [S]; FHCM also runs separate menswear and haute couture weeks — https://www.fhcm.paris/en/paris-fashion-week [F]
- Milan womenswear Sep 23–29 2025: 54 physical + 8 digital shows, 73 presentations + 27 events on the Camera Moda calendar — https://www.yesmilano.it/en/whats-on/all-events/milano-fashion-week-women [S]. Milan-specific official access statement: NOT FOUND (site 403s; Wikipedia carries none), but no public ticket channel surfaced anywhere.
- London: the BFC sold public tickets for the first time in Sept 2019 — £135 standard / £245 front row — the first of the four capitals to do so — https://fashionista.com/2019/07/london-fashion-week-open-to-public / https://hypebeast.com/2019/7/london-fashion-week-buy-public-tickets-information [S]; current public offer is a free "City Wide Celebration" plus VIP packages, while catwalk invitations remain industry — https://www.addisonlee.com/addlib/no-invite-needed-public-events-at-london-fashion-week/ [S]
- Copenhagen (the friendliest): official schedule events "can be by invitation only or be open to the public" — https://copenhagenfashionweek.com/application/event-talk-schedule-information [S]; CPHFW tickets sold through Billetlugen, Denmark's ticketing platform — https://www.billetlugen.dk/en/artist/copenhagen-fashion-week/ [S]; SS27 edition Aug 3–7 2026, 36 shows/presentations — https://events.europa.tips/copenhagen-fashion-week-sommer?lang=en [S]

**Verdict: does not apply.** Passes 1 (a defined week), 3, 4 (shows scattered across the city), 7 (same city, twice+ a year), 8. **Fails 6 decisively** — the catalogue that matters is invitation/accreditation-only; what is publicly ticketed is a parallel shadow programme, not the actual catalogue — and **fails 5** (every show happens exactly once; a missed slot is gone, so it's triage, not optimization). Even for insiders it's a scheduling problem, not a market. Copenhagen is the only edition drifting toward open access, and London's 2019 experiment shows the model was tried, at £135 a seat. Answer to the owner: fashion week has festival *shape* (window, simultaneity, spread) but no festival *market* — a planner has nothing the public can book.

## 2. Summer Olympics (Paris 2024 as data point)

- 26 July – 11 Aug 2024 (17 days; football/rugby began 24 July); 329 events in 32 sports; 10,714 athletes — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics [F]
- 767 ticketed sessions across the Games — https://www.olympics.com/en/news/registration-phase-two-paris-2024-ticket-sale [S]
- ~10 million tickets on offer; 9.5 million sold (record), buyers from 222 countries; 62% bought by French residents; 2.6M more for the Paralympics — https://www.paris.fr/en/pages/the-paris-2024-games-in-numbers-28797 [F], corroborated https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics [F]
- 35 competition venues, ~20 in/around central Paris; also Lille (225 km), Marseille (777 km), Tahiti (15,716 km) — https://www.nbcnewyork.com/paris-2024-summer-olympics/where-are-2024-olympics-venues-list-paris-france/5193077/ [S], https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics [F]
- Sale mechanics: phase 1 (Feb 2023) was a lottery draw for build-your-own packs of 3 sessions, 3.25M+ tickets; phase 2 (from Mar 2023) single tickets for all 767 sessions — https://www.olympics.com/en/news/paris-2024-ticketing-first-phase-figures / https://www.olympics.com/en/news/registration-phase-two-paris-2024-ticket-sale [S]; first draw announced Nov 2022 — https://www.malaymail.com/news/sports/2022/11/28/paris-2024-to-launch-streamlined-public-ticketing-first-draw-starts-dec-1/42341 [S]
- Prices: sport tickets from €24, half of all tickets under €50 — https://www.infobae.com/aroundtherings/articles/2022/03/22/paris-2024-unveils-ticketing-program-for-the-olympic-and-paralympic-games [S]; opening ceremony €90–€2,700 — https://www.nbcmiami.com/paris-2024-summer-olympics/2024-paris-olympics-opening-ceremony-tickets/3365688/ [S]
- Official face-value resale platform via the "Paris 2024 Tickets" app, launched 15 May 2024, resale up to 12h before a session — https://theticketingbusiness.com/2024/05/15/paris-2024-ticketing-app-launches [S], https://ticket-resale.paris2024.org/?language=en [S]
- Structural: host city changes every Games (LA 2028 next) — inherent to the format; contrast FIFA World Cup 2026: 104 matches across 16 cities in 3 countries, 11 June–19 July — https://www.britannica.com/event/2026-FIFA-World-Cup [S] — even more scattered, zero anchoring.

**Verdict: fails on exactly the two dimensions a planning product compounds on.** Passes 1, 2 (767 sessions vs ~30 a person could attend), 3, 4 (35 venues, city-to-region scale), 6 (genuinely public, from €24, with an official resale market — better-behaved access than most festivals), 8. **Fails 5** (a session happens once; the 100m final does not "recur Tuesday") and **fails 7** (venue data, travel times, and vendor knowledge are worthless in 4 years). It is a one-shot, city-scale triage problem — a real planning market for exactly one summer. The World Cup is the same failure amplified: inter-city flights as the "travel time" constraint.

## 3. Gen Con (Indianapolis)

- 2025: nearly 72,000 attendees, record, sold out; four days; Indiana Convention Center + Lucas Oil Stadium — https://www.gencon.com/press/record-breaking-gencon-2025 [F]
- "Nearly 30,000 unique ticketed events" at Gen Con 2025 — https://www.gencon.com/press/gen-con-arrives-2025 [S]; the con's own attend page says "Over 20,000+ Events to Explore" and "thousands of ticketed events" — https://www.gencon.com/attend/event-registration [F]
- Model: badge grants entry; each event is booked individually with its own ticket; $2 generic tickets can substitute for an event ticket without guaranteeing a seat — https://gencon.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/36966863600404-What-are-Generic-Tickets [S]
- 4-Day badge 2025: $155 (+10% Marion County admissions tax) — https://www.gencon.com/press/2025-reg-dates-and-badge-prices-chairman [S]
- Founded 1968 (Lake Geneva, WI); in Indianapolis since 2003 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen_Con [F]; 2026 dates July 30–Aug 2, contracted to Indianapolis annually through 2030 — https://www.gencon.com/press/record-breaking-gencon-2025 [F]

**Verdict: the closest non-festival analogue found.** Passes 2 emphatically (30,000 events vs ~20 a person can play — a deeper catalogue than the Fringe's ~3,700 shows), 3 (hundreds of simultaneous time slots), 5 (popular games run many sessions across the four days), 6 (public badge + per-event tickets — literally the Fringe's model with a cover charge), 7 (same city 20+ years, contracted years ahead), 8 (downtown Indianapolis). **Fails 4** (essentially one connected campus — ICC + Lucas Oil + surrounding hotels; walking, not travel, is the constraint) and **half-fails 1** (4 days is under the "week+" bar, though the sold-out scarcity makes planning mandatory). Event registration itself is a famous rush (tickets sell out in minutes), which adds a scarcity dimension Edinburgh lacks.

## 4. San Diego Comic-Con

- Attendance capped around 130,000; digital registration introduced to manage demand; RFID badges tap in/out — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con [F]
- Badge-only: no tickets for individual panels; all rooms first-come, first-served, no reserved seating; fans camp overnight for Hall H (approx. 6,500 seats) — https://www.conrangers.com/sdcc / https://sdccblog.com/2026/07/guide-to-hall-h-at-san-diego-comic-con/ [S]
- Badges sold per-day through randomized online sales (returning-attendee sale, then open sale); 2026 prices: Preview Night $64, Thu–Sat $85/day, Sun $64 — https://www.thingstodoinsandiego.us/events/comic-con-san-diego-2026 [S]
- SDCC 2025 ran July 24–27 (4 days + preview night) — https://www.kpbs.org/news/arts-culture/2025/07/17/comic-con-2025-top-offsite-events-that-dont-require-a-badge [S]
- Count of parallel program rooms: NOT FOUND as an official figure (press schedules show dozens of concurrent tracks per day — https://deadline.com/lists/comic-con-2025-schedule/ [S])
- Offsites (activations across the Gaslamp Quarter) are open without a badge and are covered as their own no-badge programme — https://www.10news.com/entertainment/comic-con/no-badge-needed-offsites-for-san-diego-comic-con-2025 [S]
- Third-party planning ecosystem exists (fan-run SDCC Unofficial Blog guides, schedule walk-throughs) — https://sdccblog.com/ [S]

**Verdict: fails on access mechanics despite massive abundance.** Passes 2, 3, 7 (San Diego every July), 8. **Fails 6** — one badge, then queueing; there is no per-item slot the public can book, so a planner can optimize queue strategy but never inventory. **Fails 5** (panels are one-offs) and 1 (4 days). Venue spread is partial: convention center + hotel ballrooms + a district of offsites. Instructive as the "wristband world": scarcity is allocated by standing in line, not by booking — the optimization is real but unbookable.

## 5. Walt Disney World + TouringPlans (the commercial existence proof)

- TouringPlans WDW subscription: $24.97/year — https://touringplans.com/walt-disney-world/join [S]
- What it sells: step-by-step touring plans that "tell you when to visit, which park, and how to wait less in line", re-optimized live in the park; Crowd Calendar; wait-time predictions via the Lines app; dining-reservation sniper; room finder — https://touringplans.com/ / https://touringplans.com/blog/disney-in-a-minute-what-is-a-touring-plan/ [S]
- (Site blocks non-browser fetches — 403 to both curl and WebFetch — so all lines above are [S] from its own indexed pages.)
- Structural contrast: the park is open year-round; there is no fixed shared window — the "time box" is each visitor's own trip, and every attraction recurs continuously all day.

**Verdict: not a festmaxxing environment — but the proof people pay for itinerary optimization.** Fails 1 (no shared fixed window) and mostly 3 (nothing is foreclosed; the ride runs again in 10 minutes); 8 is inverted (the resort is the context). Passes 5 trivially, 6 (park ticket + per-ride paid slots), 7 (permanently anchored — which is exactly why its data business compounds: two decades of wait-time data on the same rides). The lesson for the owner: recurrence + anchoring is what made a $25/yr subscription viable; the Fringe has the anchor but only a 25-day season.

## 6. Open House Festival, London (Doors Open archetype)

- 2026 edition: 12–20 September (9 days), 35th edition, buildings and sites across all 33 boroughs, free — https://open-city.org.uk/open-house-festival [F]
- 2025 edition: 13–21 Sept, over 800 free open days and events — https://open-city.org.uk/blog/ohfprogrammelaunch [S]
- Booking model: mostly free drop-in; ticketed activities require booking via a free account, bookings opening ~3.5 weeks before the festival (19 Aug for 2025-style programme) — https://open-city.org.uk/open-house-festival [F]; a recognized split between "just turn up" buildings and "needs booking" buildings — https://londonist.com/london/festivals/open-house-2025-which-buildings-are-open-which-need-booking [S]

**Verdict: genuinely clears most of the bar.** Passes 1 (9 fixed days), 2 (800+ items vs the ~10–15 one person can visit), 3 (everything open in the same two weekends), 4 emphatically (all 33 boroughs — travel time is *the* constraint), 6 (free but per-item: drop-in or a booked/balloted slot), 7 (annual, same city, 35 editions), 8. **Weak on 5**: many buildings open only one day of the nine, so part of the catalogue is triage rather than optimization — and the value axis is interest, not price. Closest thing to a "free Fringe for buildings"; the scarce-slot booking race (popular buildings gone in minutes) is a real planning pain today.

## 7. Burning Man

- 2025: Aug 24 – Sep 1 (9 days), Black Rock Desert, Nevada — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/domesticnotices/dom25017_sp.html / https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/burning-man-2025-murder-investigation-baby-delivery-massive-dust-storm-rcna228513 [S]
- One admission ticket covers everything: 2025 main sale tiers $550/$650/$750/$950/$1,500/$3,000 + $150 vehicle pass — https://journal.burningman.org/2025/02/black-rock-city/ticketing/2025ticketinfo/ [S]
- No commerce inside: "No cash transactions are permitted between burners", cash usable only for a few charity/fuel/sanitation vendors; decommodification is one of the ten principles — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]
- Participant-run event catalogue: 4,300+ events submitted to the Playa Events calendar in 2018 (up from 3,626), of which only ~1,500 fit the printed What Where When guide — https://journal.burningman.org/2018/08/black-rock-city/participate-in-brc/playa-events-the-what-the-where-and-the-when/ [S]; current-year counts: NOT FOUND
- Population cap: 80,000 people on site at any time under the BLM permit (2019, retained) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]
- Same site annually (Black Rock City is rebuilt every year) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]

**Verdict: shape without a market, desert without a city.** Passes 1, 2 (thousands of events), 3, 4 (a temporary city crossed by bicycle — travel genuinely binds), 5 partially (camp events recur daily), 7 (same place, every year — the WWW guide *is* the community's own festmaxxing artifact). **Fails 6** (one wristband-equivalent for everything; per-event access is unticketable by ideology, and listings are radically unreliable) and **fails 8** (there is no surrounding non-event city — food, rest and shelter are things you truck in). Instructive: proof that a self-published event catalogue emerges wherever abundance + a time box exist, even with no commerce at all.

## 8. NYC Restaurant Week (restaurant-week archetype)

- Summer 2025: Mon Jul 21 – Sun Aug 17 (4 weeks; Saturdays excluded, Sundays optional), with optional extension to Sep 2 — https://www.business.nyctourism.com/press-media/press-releases/summer-2025-nyc-restaurant-week [F]
- Nearly 600 restaurants across all five boroughs, 50+ cuisines, 70+ neighborhoods; twice-yearly program (winter and summer) — same URL [F]
- Prix-fixe menus at $30 / $45 / $60 for lunch/brunch/dinner; browse and reserve through nyctourism.com with OpenTable integration — same URL [F]

**Verdict: clears the bar more cleanly than expected.** Passes 1 (fixed 4-week window), 2 (600 restaurants vs ~40 meal slots), 3 (in the aggregate — each mealtime forecloses the alternatives), 4 (five boroughs), 5 strongly (each restaurant repeats daily through the window — this is optimization territory: sequence by neighborhood, spread cuisines), 6 (the reservation is a real, scarce, per-item public slot — hot restaurants book out immediately), 7 (NYC, twice a year, long-running), 8 (trivially — the "event" *is* the city's ordinary fabric). Weaknesses: intensity is low (2 slots/day, not 8), and "catalogue data" is just the restaurant scene, already served by Resy/OpenTable/Infatuation — the incumbent risk is that general dining tools already own this.

## 9. CES, Las Vegas

- CES 2025: Jan 7–10 (4 days), Las Vegas — https://www.ces.tech/press-releases/dive-in-to-the-future-ces-2025-opens-today [S]
- 141,000 attendees; 4,100+ exhibitors incl. ~1,200 startups — https://exhibitcitynews.com/ces-by-the-numbers/ / https://lasvegassun.com/news/2026/apr/03/attendance-for-ces-in-las-vegas-rose-to-nearly-150/ [S]
- 2.6M+ net sq ft across multiple venues — Las Vegas Convention Center + the Venetian, far enough apart that inter-campus logistics are a named feature (blue-dot navigation added 2025) — https://www.nparallel.com/trade-shows-conferences/exhibitor-guides/ces-las-vegas / https://www.ces.tech/press-releases/what-not-to-miss-at-ces-2025/ [S]
- Trade-only: not open to the general public; attendance requires industry affiliation — https://events.visitorslist.com/consumer-electronics-show/ [S]
- Anchored: Las Vegas every January (same two campuses).

**Verdict: an insider festmaxxing problem, closed to the product's public.** Passes 2, 3, 4 (the LVCC–Venetian split makes travel a genuine constraint), 5 (booths persist all four days — pure optimization), 7, 8 (Las Vegas). **Fails 6** (badge gated on industry affiliation; no per-item public ticket) and 1 is borderline (4 days). Same instructive class as fashion week: the planning problem exists (exhibitor-list routing is a cottage industry) but the addressable user is a badge-holder, not the public.

## 10. Offered extras

**Salzburg Festival (performing-arts season)**
- 2025: 174 performances over 45 days at 16 venues; 98.4% of seats occupied; 256,600 guests from 88 countries; 43 opera performances + 90 concerts + theatre incl. 15 Jedermann — https://www.salzburgerfestspiele.at/en/blog/recap-salzburg-festival-2025 [F]
- Public per-performance ticketing (subscriptions, vouchers, youth tickets) — https://www.salzburgerfestspiele.at/en/ticketing-information [S]; annual in Salzburg since 1920 (105th season context on same site) [S]
- **Verdict:** passes 1 (long but fixed), 5 (productions repeat across the run), 6, 7 (a century in one town — the deepest anchor on this list), 8. **Fails 2–3 as a planning problem** (~4 performances/day, so an evening rarely forecloses more than one alternative) and **4** (16 venues in a compact old town). Instructive: abundance-per-window, not abundance-per-hour — a season you book, not a schedule you optimize.

**Miami Art Week / Art Basel Miami Beach**
- Miami Art Week 2024: Dec 2–9, 20+ international art fairs, 1,200+ galleries in aggregate, across Miami Beach, Wynwood, Design District, Downtown, Coral Gables, Coconut Grove and more — https://www.miamiartweek.org/ / https://www.condoblackbook.com/blog/miami-art-week-2024 [S]
- Anchor fair Art Basel Miami Beach 2024: 280+ galleries from 40+ countries; public days Dec 6–8 at Miami Beach Convention Center; public tickets $85/day, $120 First Access, $65 concession — https://www.timeout.com/miami/news/art-basel-and-miami-art-week-everything-to-know-about-dates-schedules-and-tickets-120324 [S]
- **Verdict: clears the bar.** Passes 1 (one fixed December week), 2, 3 (fairs + museum shows + events overlap all week), 4 emphatically (fairs strewn across greater Miami; traffic is the binding constraint), 5 (each fair open daily — sequencing, not triage), 6 (each fair separately publicly ticketed), 7 (annual, same city and venues), 8 (Miami). The strongest "offer" candidate: structurally a Fringe where the shows are fairs.

---

## Ranked shortlist

**Genuinely clear the bar (non-festival festmaxxing):**
1. **Gen Con** — per-event public tickets on a ~30,000-item catalogue, anchored to Indianapolis through 2030; fails only venue spread (one campus) and runs 4 days, not a week.
2. **Miami Art Week** — one December week, 20+ separately ticketed fairs scattered across a traffic-bound metro, annual; the closest full 8/8 shape after Gen Con.
3. **Open House London** — 800+ items, 9 days, 33 boroughs, per-item slots (free); weak only on repeat chances (many buildings open a single day).
4. **NYC Restaurant Week** — 600 repeating items, real scarce reservations, twice-yearly anchor; low daily intensity and strong incumbent tooling.
5. *(partial)* **Salzburg Festival** — everything but simultaneity and venue spread; a booking season, not an optimization sprint.

**Fail instructively:**
- **Fashion week** (the owner's question): **no** — fails open access and repeat chances; the public-facing programme (Runway 7-style showcases, Copenhagen's open events, London's 2019 £135 experiment) is a fringe around a closed core, not a bookable catalogue.
- **Olympics**: passes access, abundance, spread — fails repeat chances and, fatally for a data product, anchored recurrence (host rotates; World Cup 2026 doubles that failure across 16 cities).
- **SDCC / CES / Burning Man**: three flavors of the access failure — badge + queue (SDCC), industry badge (CES), one ticket + decommodification (Burning Man, which also lacks any city context).
- **WDW + TouringPlans**: fails the time box entirely (continuous park, visitor-defined trip) — but is the standing commercial proof that people pay ($24.97/yr) for constrained-itinerary optimization when recurrence lets the data compound.

Cross-cutting finding: the definition's rarest dimension among big real-world events is **6 (open per-event access)** — most mega-events allocate by badge, invitation, or queue. Where 6 holds and 7 holds (Gen Con, Miami Art Week, Open House, Restaurant Week, and festivals proper), a planning product's data investment compounds; where either fails, the planning problem still exists but has no bookable inventory (fashion week, SDCC, CES) or no future (each Olympics).

- Structural: host city changes every Games (LA 2028 next) — inherent to the format; contrast FIFA World Cup 2026: 104 matches across 16 cities in 3 countries, 11 June–19 July — https://www.britannica.com/event/2026-FIFA-World-Cup [S] — even more scattered, zero anchoring.

**Verdict: fails on exactly the two dimensions a planning product compounds on.** Passes 1, 2 (767 sessions vs ~30 a person could attend), 3, 4 (35 venues, city-to-region scale), 6 (genuinely public, from €24, with an official resale market — better-behaved access than most festivals), 8. **Fails 5** (a session happens once; the 100m final does not "recur Tuesday") and **fails 7** (venue data, travel times, and vendor knowledge are worthless in 4 years). It is a one-shot, city-scale triage problem — a real planning market for exactly one summer. The World Cup is the same failure amplified: inter-city flights as the "travel time" constraint.

## 3. Gen Con (Indianapolis)

- 2025: nearly 72,000 attendees, record, sold out; four days; Indiana Convention Center + Lucas Oil Stadium — https://www.gencon.com/press/record-breaking-gencon-2025 [F]
- "Nearly 30,000 unique ticketed events" at Gen Con 2025 — https://www.gencon.com/press/gen-con-arrives-2025 [S]; the con's own attend page says "Over 20,000+ Events to Explore" and "thousands of ticketed events" — https://www.gencon.com/attend/event-registration [F]
- Model: badge grants entry; each event is booked individually with its own ticket; $2 generic tickets can substitute for an event ticket without guaranteeing a seat — https://gencon.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/36966863600404-What-are-Generic-Tickets [S]
- 4-Day badge 2025: $155 (+10% Marion County admissions tax) — https://www.gencon.com/press/2025-reg-dates-and-badge-prices-chairman [S]
- Founded 1968 (Lake Geneva, WI); in Indianapolis since 2003 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen_Con [F]; 2026 dates July 30–Aug 2, contracted to Indianapolis annually through 2030 — https://www.gencon.com/press/record-breaking-gencon-2025 [F]

**Verdict: the closest non-festival analogue found.** Passes 2 emphatically (30,000 events vs ~20 a person can play — a deeper catalogue than the Fringe's ~3,700 shows), 3 (hundreds of simultaneous time slots), 5 (popular games run many sessions across the four days), 6 (public badge + per-event tickets — literally the Fringe's model with a cover charge), 7 (same city 20+ years, contracted years ahead), 8 (downtown Indianapolis). **Fails 4** (essentially one connected campus — ICC + Lucas Oil + surrounding hotels; walking, not travel, is the constraint) and **half-fails 1** (4 days is under the "week+" bar, though the sold-out scarcity makes planning mandatory). Event registration itself is a famous rush (tickets sell out in minutes), which adds a scarcity dimension Edinburgh lacks.

## 4. San Diego Comic-Con

- Attendance capped around 130,000; digital registration introduced to manage demand; RFID badges tap in/out — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con [F]
- Badge-only: no tickets for individual panels; all rooms first-come, first-served, no reserved seating; fans camp overnight for Hall H (approx. 6,500 seats) — https://www.conrangers.com/sdcc / https://sdccblog.com/2026/07/guide-to-hall-h-at-san-diego-comic-con/ [S]
- Badges sold per-day through randomized online sales (returning-attendee sale, then open sale); 2026 prices: Preview Night $64, Thu–Sat $85/day, Sun $64 — https://www.thingstodoinsandiego.us/events/comic-con-san-diego-2026 [S]
- SDCC 2025 ran July 24–27 (4 days + preview night) — https://www.kpbs.org/news/arts-culture/2025/07/17/comic-con-2025-top-offsite-events-that-dont-require-a-badge [S]
- Count of parallel program rooms: NOT FOUND as an official figure (press schedules show dozens of concurrent tracks per day — https://deadline.com/lists/comic-con-2025-schedule/ [S])
- Offsites (activations across the Gaslamp Quarter) are open without a badge and are covered as their own no-badge programme — https://www.10news.com/entertainment/comic-con/no-badge-needed-offsites-for-san-diego-comic-con-2025 [S]
- Third-party planning ecosystem exists (fan-run SDCC Unofficial Blog guides, schedule walk-throughs) — https://sdccblog.com/ [S]

**Verdict: fails on access mechanics despite massive abundance.** Passes 2, 3, 7 (San Diego every July), 8. **Fails 6** — one badge, then queueing; there is no per-item slot the public can book, so a planner can optimize queue strategy but never inventory. **Fails 5** (panels are one-offs) and 1 (4 days). Venue spread is partial: convention center + hotel ballrooms + a district of offsites. Instructive as the "wristband world": scarcity is allocated by standing in line, not by booking — the optimization is real but unbookable.

## 5. Walt Disney World + TouringPlans (the commercial existence proof)

- TouringPlans WDW subscription: $24.97/year — https://touringplans.com/walt-disney-world/join [S]
- What it sells: step-by-step touring plans that "tell you when to visit, which park, and how to wait less in line", re-optimized live in the park; Crowd Calendar; wait-time predictions via the Lines app; dining-reservation sniper; room finder — https://touringplans.com/ / https://touringplans.com/blog/disney-in-a-minute-what-is-a-touring-plan/ [S]
- (Site blocks non-browser fetches — 403 to both curl and WebFetch — so all lines above are [S] from its own indexed pages.)
- Structural contrast: the park is open year-round; there is no fixed shared window — the "time box" is each visitor's own trip, and every attraction recurs continuously all day.

**Verdict: not a festmaxxing environment — but the proof people pay for itinerary optimization.** Fails 1 (no shared fixed window) and mostly 3 (nothing is foreclosed; the ride runs again in 10 minutes); 8 is inverted (the resort is the context). Passes 5 trivially, 6 (park ticket + per-ride paid slots), 7 (permanently anchored — which is exactly why its data business compounds: two decades of wait-time data on the same rides). The lesson for the owner: recurrence + anchoring is what made a $25/yr subscription viable; the Fringe has the anchor but only a 25-day season.

## 6. Open House Festival, London (Doors Open archetype)

- 2026 edition: 12–20 September (9 days), 35th edition, buildings and sites across all 33 boroughs, free — https://open-city.org.uk/open-house-festival [F]
- 2025 edition: 13–21 Sept, over 800 free open days and events — https://open-city.org.uk/blog/ohfprogrammelaunch [S]
- Booking model: mostly free drop-in; ticketed activities require booking via a free account, bookings opening ~3.5 weeks before the festival (19 Aug for 2025-style programme) — https://open-city.org.uk/open-house-festival [F]; a recognized split between "just turn up" buildings and "needs booking" buildings — https://londonist.com/london/festivals/open-house-2025-which-buildings-are-open-which-need-booking [S]

**Verdict: genuinely clears most of the bar.** Passes 1 (9 fixed days), 2 (800+ items vs the ~10–15 one person can visit), 3 (everything open in the same two weekends), 4 emphatically (all 33 boroughs — travel time is *the* constraint), 6 (free but per-item: drop-in or a booked/balloted slot), 7 (annual, same city, 35 editions), 8. **Weak on 5**: many buildings open only one day of the nine, so part of the catalogue is triage rather than optimization — and the value axis is interest, not price. Closest thing to a "free Fringe for buildings"; the scarce-slot booking race (popular buildings gone in minutes) is a real planning pain today.

## 7. Burning Man

- 2025: Aug 24 – Sep 1 (9 days), Black Rock Desert, Nevada — https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/domesticnotices/dom25017_sp.html / https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/burning-man-2025-murder-investigation-baby-delivery-massive-dust-storm-rcna228513 [S]
- One admission ticket covers everything: 2025 main sale tiers $550/$650/$750/$950/$1,500/$3,000 + $150 vehicle pass — https://journal.burningman.org/2025/02/black-rock-city/ticketing/2025ticketinfo/ [S]
- No commerce inside: "No cash transactions are permitted between burners", cash usable only for a few charity/fuel/sanitation vendors; decommodification is one of the ten principles — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]
- Participant-run event catalogue: 4,300+ events submitted to the Playa Events calendar in 2018 (up from 3,626), of which only ~1,500 fit the printed What Where When guide — https://journal.burningman.org/2018/08/black-rock-city/participate-in-brc/playa-events-the-what-the-where-and-the-when/ [S]; current-year counts: NOT FOUND
- Population cap: 80,000 people on site at any time under the BLM permit (2019, retained) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]
- Same site annually (Black Rock City is rebuilt every year) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Man [F]

**Verdict: shape without a market, desert without a city.** Passes 1, 2 (thousands of events), 3, 4 (a temporary city crossed by bicycle — travel genuinely binds), 5 partially (camp events recur daily), 7 (same place, every year — the WWW guide *is* the community's own festmaxxing artifact). **Fails 6** (one wristband-equivalent for everything; per-event access is unticketable by ideology, and listings are radically unreliable) and **fails 8** (there is no surrounding non-event city — food, rest and shelter are things you truck in). Instructive: proof that a self-published event catalogue emerges wherever abundance + a time box exist, even with no commerce at all.

## 8. NYC Restaurant Week (restaurant-week archetype)

- Summer 2025: Mon Jul 21 – Sun Aug 17 (4 weeks; Saturdays excluded, Sundays optional), with optional extension to Sep 2 — https://www.business.nyctourism.com/press-media/press-releases/summer-2025-nyc-restaurant-week [F]
- Nearly 600 restaurants across all five boroughs, 50+ cuisines, 70+ neighborhoods; twice-yearly program (winter and summer) — same URL [F]
- Prix-fixe menus at $30 / $45 / $60 for lunch/brunch/dinner; browse and reserve through nyctourism.com with OpenTable integration — same URL [F]

**Verdict: clears the bar more cleanly than expected.** Passes 1 (fixed 4-week window), 2 (600 restaurants vs ~40 meal slots), 3 (in the aggregate — each mealtime forecloses the alternatives), 4 (five boroughs), 5 strongly (each restaurant repeats daily through the window — this is optimization territory: sequence by neighborhood, spread cuisines), 6 (the reservation is a real, scarce, per-item public slot — hot restaurants book out immediately), 7 (NYC, twice a year, long-running), 8 (trivially — the "event" *is* the city's ordinary fabric). Weaknesses: intensity is low (2 slots/day, not 8), and "catalogue data" is just the restaurant scene, already served by Resy/OpenTable/Infatuation — the incumbent risk is that general dining tools already own this.

## 9. CES, Las Vegas

- CES 2025: Jan 7–10 (4 days), Las Vegas — https://www.ces.tech/press-releases/dive-in-to-the-future-ces-2025-opens-today [S]
- 141,000 attendees; 4,100+ exhibitors incl. ~1,200 startups — https://exhibitcitynews.com/ces-by-the-numbers/ / https://lasvegassun.com/news/2026/apr/03/attendance-for-ces-in-las-vegas-rose-to-nearly-150/ [S]
- 2.6M+ net sq ft across multiple venues — Las Vegas Convention Center + the Venetian, far enough apart that inter-campus logistics are a named feature (blue-dot navigation added 2025) — https://www.nparallel.com/trade-shows-conferences/exhibitor-guides/ces-las-vegas / https://www.ces.tech/press-releases/what-not-to-miss-at-ces-2025/ [S]
- Trade-only: not open to the general public; attendance requires industry affiliation — https://events.visitorslist.com/consumer-electronics-show/ [S]
- Anchored: Las Vegas every January (same two campuses).

**Verdict: an insider festmaxxing problem, closed to the product's public.** Passes 2, 3, 4 (the LVCC–Venetian split makes travel a genuine constraint), 5 (booths persist all four days — pure optimization), 7, 8 (Las Vegas). **Fails 6** (badge gated on industry affiliation; no per-item public ticket) and 1 is borderline (4 days). Same instructive class as fashion week: the planning problem exists (exhibitor-list routing is a cottage industry) but the addressable user is a badge-holder, not the public.

## 10. Offered extras

**Salzburg Festival (performing-arts season)**
- 2025: 174 performances over 45 days at 16 venues; 98.4% of seats occupied; 256,600 guests from 88 countries; 43 opera performances + 90 concerts + theatre incl. 15 Jedermann — https://www.salzburgerfestspiele.at/en/blog/recap-salzburg-festival-2025 [F]
- Public per-performance ticketing (subscriptions, vouchers, youth tickets) — https://www.salzburgerfestspiele.at/en/ticketing-information [S]; annual in Salzburg since 1920 (105th season context on same site) [S]
- **Verdict:** passes 1 (long but fixed), 5 (productions repeat across the run), 6, 7 (a century in one town — the deepest anchor on this list), 8. **Fails 2–3 as a planning problem** (~4 performances/day, so an evening rarely forecloses more than one alternative) and **4** (16 venues in a compact old town). Instructive: abundance-per-window, not abundance-per-hour — a season you book, not a schedule you optimize.

**Miami Art Week / Art Basel Miami Beach**
- Miami Art Week 2024: Dec 2–9, 20+ international art fairs, 1,200+ galleries in aggregate, across Miami Beach, Wynwood, Design District, Downtown, Coral Gables, Coconut Grove and more — https://www.miamiartweek.org/ / https://www.condoblackbook.com/blog/miami-art-week-2024 [S]
- Anchor fair Art Basel Miami Beach 2024: 280+ galleries from 40+ countries; public days Dec 6–8 at Miami Beach Convention Center; public tickets $85/day, $120 First Access, $65 concession — https://www.timeout.com/miami/news/art-basel-and-miami-art-week-everything-to-know-about-dates-schedules-and-tickets-120324 [S]
- **Verdict: clears the bar.** Passes 1 (one fixed December week), 2, 3 (fairs + museum shows + events overlap all week), 4 emphatically (fairs strewn across greater Miami; traffic is the binding constraint), 5 (each fair open daily — sequencing, not triage), 6 (each fair separately publicly ticketed), 7 (annual, same city and venues), 8 (Miami). The strongest "offer" candidate: structurally a Fringe where the shows are fairs.

---

## Ranked shortlist

**Genuinely clear the bar (non-festival festmaxxing):**
1. **Gen Con** — per-event public tickets on a ~30,000-item catalogue, anchored to Indianapolis through 2030; fails only venue spread (one campus) and runs 4 days, not a week.
2. **Miami Art Week** — one December week, 20+ separately ticketed fairs scattered across a traffic-bound metro, annual; the closest full 8/8 shape after Gen Con.
3. **Open House London** — 800+ items, 9 days, 33 boroughs, per-item slots (free); weak only on repeat chances (many buildings open a single day).
4. **NYC Restaurant Week** — 600 repeating items, real scarce reservations, twice-yearly anchor; low daily intensity and strong incumbent tooling.
5. *(partial)* **Salzburg Festival** — everything but simultaneity and venue spread; a booking season, not an optimization sprint.

**Fail instructively:**
- **Fashion week** (the owner's question): **no** — fails open access and repeat chances; the public-facing programme (Runway 7-style showcases, Copenhagen's open events, London's 2019 £135 experiment) is a fringe around a closed core, not a bookable catalogue.
- **Olympics**: passes access, abundance, spread — fails repeat chances and, fatally for a data product, anchored recurrence (host rotates; World Cup 2026 doubles that failure across 16 cities).
- **SDCC / CES / Burning Man**: three flavors of the access failure — badge + queue (SDCC), industry badge (CES), one ticket + decommodification (Burning Man, which also lacks any city context).
- **WDW + TouringPlans**: fails the time box entirely (continuous park, visitor-defined trip) — but is the standing commercial proof that people pay ($24.97/yr) for constrained-itinerary optimization when recurrence lets the data compound.

Cross-cutting finding: the definition's rarest dimension among big real-world events is **6 (open per-event access)** — most mega-events allocate by badge, invitation, or queue. Where 6 holds and 7 holds (Gen Con, Miami Art Week, Open House, Restaurant Week, and festivals proper), a planning product's data investment compounds; where either fails, the planning problem still exists but has no bookable inventory (fashion week, SDCC, CES) or no future (each Olympics).</result>
